text: The isolated horizon framework was introduced in order to provide a localdescription of black holes that are in equilibrium with their (possiblydynamic) environment. Over the past several years, the framework has beenextended to include matter fields (dilaton, Yang-Mills etc) in D=4 dimensionsand cosmological constant in $D\geq3$ dimensions. In this article we present afurther extension of the framework that includes black holes inhigher-dimensional Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) gravity. In particular, weconstruct a covariant phase space for EGB gravity in arbitrary dimensions whichallows us to derive the first law. We find that the entropy of a weaklyisolated and non-rotating horizon is given by$\mathcal{S}=(1/4G_{D})\oint_{S^{D-2}}\bm{\tilde{\epsilon}}(1+2\alpha\mathcal{R})$.In this expression $S^{D-2}$ is the $(D-2)$-dimensional cross section of thehorizon with area form $\bm{\tilde{\epsilon}}$ and Ricci scalar $\mathcal{R}$,$G_{D}$ is the $D$-dimensional Newton constant and $\alpha$ is the Gauss-Bonnetparameter. This expression for the horizon entropy is in agreement with thosepredicted by the Euclidean and Noether charge methods. Thus we extend theisolated horizon framework beyond Einstein gravity.
label: human

text: We extend the isolated horizon framework, originally developed for general relativity, to higher-dimensional Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) gravity, providing a quasilocal description of black hole horizons in equilibrium within potentially dynamic spacetimes. The Gauss-Bonnet term introduces quadratic curvature corrections that become dynamically relevant in dimensions greater than four, motivating this generalization beyond previous extensions incorporating matter fields or cosmological constants. A key step involves constructing a covariant phase space for EGB gravity in arbitrary dimensions D ≥ 5, ensuring well-defined symplectic structure and conserved charges. This phase space allows the derivation of zeroth and first laws of mechanics for weakly isolated horizons. For non-rotating weakly isolated horizons, the entropy acquires a correction beyond the standard area law. Specifically, the entropy is given by S = (1/(4 G_D)) ∫_{S^{D-2}} \tilde{\epsilon} (1 + 2 α ℛ), where \tilde{\epsilon} is the area form on the (D-2)-dimensional horizon cross-section, ℛ its Ricci scalar, G_D the D-dimensional gravitational constant, and α the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. This modified entropy expression aligns with expectations from other methods and highlights the role of intrinsic horizon geometry in higher-curvature theories.
label: llm

text: It has been demonstrated that quantum vacuum energy gravitates according tothe equivalence principle, at least for the finite Casimir energies associatedwith perfectly conducting parallel plates. We here add further support to thisconclusion by considering parallel semitransparent plates, that is,delta-function potentials, acting on a massless scalar field, in a spacetimedefined by Rindler coordinates (tau,x,y,xi). Fixed xi in such a spacetimerepresents uniform acceleration. We calculate the force on systems consistingof one or two such plates at fixed values of xi. In the limit of large Rindlercoordinate xi (small acceleration), we recover (via the equivalence principle)the situation of weak gravity, and find that the gravitational force on thesystem is just Mg, where g is the gravitational acceleration and M is the totalmass of the system, consisting of the mass of the plates renormalized by theCasimir energy of each plate separately, plus the energy of the Casimirinteraction between the plates. This reproduces the previous result in thelimit as the coupling to the delta-function potential approaches infinity.
label: human

text: The question of whether quantum vacuum energy gravitates in accordance with the equivalence principle remains a topic of significant interest in quantum field theory and gravity. Previous work has established that the finite Casimir energy between perfectly conducting parallel plates obeys the equivalence principle. This study extends that analysis to semitransparent plates modeled as delta-function potentials interacting with a massless scalar field. The system is examined in Rindler coordinates, where constant spatial coordinate corresponds to uniform acceleration, simulating a gravitational field via the equivalence principle. In the limit of small acceleration (large Rindler coordinate), the effective gravitational force on the system is found to be Mg, with M representing the total effective mass. This mass includes the renormalized masses of the individual plates—accounting for their separate Casimir self-energies—plus the interaction Casimir energy between them, confirming that quantum vacuum energy contributes to gravitational mass as expected from general relativity.
label: llm

text: The origin of the so called 'detached shells' around AGB stars is not fullyunderstood, but two common hypotheses state that these shells form eitherthrough the interaction of distinct wind phases or an eruptive mass lossassociated with a He-shell flash. We present a model of the formation ofdetached shells around thermal pulse asymptotic giant branch (TP-AGB) stars,based on detailed modelling of mass loss and stellar evolution, leading to acombination of eruptive mass loss and wind interaction.  The purpose of this paper is first of all to connect stellar evolution withwind and mass loss evolution and demonstrate its consistency with observations,but also to show how thin detached shells around TP-AGB stars can be formed.Previous attempts to link mass loss evolution with the formation of detachedshells were based on approximate prescriptions for the mass loss and have notincluded detailed modelling of the wind formation as we do here. (abridged)
label: human

text: The origin of detached shells around thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (TP-AGB) stars remains incompletely understood, with leading hypotheses involving either the interaction of winds from distinct evolutionary phases or brief episodes of intensified mass loss triggered by helium-shell flashes. This study presents a comprehensive model linking detailed stellar evolution and radiation-hydrodynamical atmospheric simulations to the mass-loss history during thermal pulses on the TP-AGB. We demonstrate that helium-shell flashes induce significant increases in mass-loss rate and wind velocity, creating eruptive outflows that interact with preceding slower winds to produce geometrically thin, dense detached shells via a snow-plow effect. The resulting shell properties, including radius, thickness, and density enhancement, align well with observational constraints from carbon-rich AGB stars exhibiting detached circumstellar envelopes.
label: llm

text: Arguments showing that exchange-only optimized effective potential (xOEP)methods, with finite basis sets, cannot in general yield the Hartree-Fock (HF)ground state energy, but a higher one, are given. While the orbital products ofa complete basis are linearly dependent, the HF ground state energy can only beobtained via a basis set xOEP scheme in the special case that all products ofoccupied and unoccupied orbitals emerging from the employed orbital basis setare linearly independent from each other. In this case, however, exchangepotentials leading to the HF ground state energy exhibit unphysicaloscillations and do not represent a Kohn-Sham (KS) exchange potential. Thesefindings solve the seemingly paradoxical results of Staroverov, Scuseria andDavidson that certain finite basis set xOEP calculations lead to the HF groundstate energy despite the fact that within a real space (or complete basis)representation the xOEP ground state energy is always higher than the HFenergy. Moreover, whether or not the occupied and unoccupied orbital productsare linearly independent, it is shown that basis set xOEP methods onlyrepresent exact exchange-only (EXX) KS methods, i.e., proper density-functionalmethods, if the orbital basis set and the auxiliary basis set representing theexchange potential are balanced to each other, i.e., if the orbital basis iscomprehensive enough for a given auxiliary basis. Otherwise xOEP methods do notrepresent EXX KS methods and yield unphysical exchange potentials.
label: human

text: In the exchange-only optimized effective potential (xOEP) approach within Kohn-Sham density functional theory, the local exchange potential is derived as a functional derivative of the exact Hartree-Fock exchange energy, yet in the complete basis set limit, the xOEP ground-state energy strictly exceeds the Hartree-Fock energy. Recent calculations by Staroverov et al. demonstrated that certain finite basis set xOEP implementations unexpectedly yield exactly the Hartree-Fock total energy, giving rise to an apparent paradox. This work elucidates the conditions under which finite basis set xOEP schemes recover the Hartree-Fock energy, namely when products of occupied and virtual orbitals from the orbital basis are linearly independent. Such potentials, however, typically exhibit unphysical oscillations and fail to correspond to a true Kohn-Sham exchange potential as a proper functional derivative. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that finite basis set xOEP methods only faithfully represent exact exchange-only Kohn-Sham theory when the orbital and auxiliary basis sets are balanced. These findings resolve the paradox by attributing the anomalous energy equivalence to artifacts of linear dependence in finite basis representations, with plane-wave calculations on bulk silicon providing illustrative support.
label: llm

text: We carry out the non-perturbative renormalization of the chromo-magneticoperator in Heavy Quark Effective Theory. At order 1/m of the expansion, theoperator is responsible for the mass splitting between the pseudoscalar andvector B mesons. We obtain its two-loop anomalous dimension in a Schr"odingerfunctional scheme by successive one-loop conversions to the lattice MS schemeand the MS-bar scheme. We then compute the scale evolution of the operatornon-perturbatively in the N_f=0 theory between $\mu \approx 0.3$ GeV and $\mu\approx 100$ GeV, where contact is made with perturbation theory. The overallrenormalization factor that converts the bare lattice operator to itsrenormalization group invariant form is given for the Wilson gauge action andtwo standard discretizations of the heavy-quark action. As an application, wefind that this factor brings the previous quenched predictions of the B* - Bmass splitting closer to the experimental value than found with a perturbativerenormalization. The same renormalization factor is applicable to thespin-dependent potentials of Eichten and Feinberg.
label: human

text: In Heavy Quark Effective Theory (HQET), the chromo-magnetic operator arises at order 1/m in the heavy quark expansion and is directly responsible for the hyperfine splitting between the vector (B*) and pseudoscalar (B) mesons. Accurate determination of the B* - B mass difference requires precise renormalization of this operator, as perturbative approximations may be unreliable at low scales. We perform a non-perturbative renormalization using the Schrödinger functional scheme, which allows reliable calculations in lattice QCD. The two-loop anomalous dimension is computed by converting one-loop results between the lattice, modified minimal subtraction, and \overline{MS} schemes. Non-perturbative running of the renormalization constant is then evaluated in the quenched approximation (N_f=0) over a wide scale range from approximately 0.3 GeV to 100 GeV, ensuring smooth matching to high-energy perturbative behavior. Overall renormalization factors are provided for the Wilson gauge action combined with common heavy quark discretizations. Applying these factors to prior quenched lattice computations of the B* - B mass splitting yields results significantly closer to the experimental value compared to those obtained with purely.
label: llm

text: We present results from an analysis of B0 to rho+rho- decays using 383.6million BB-bar pairs collected by the BaBar detector at the PEP-IIasymmetric-energy B Factory at SLAC. The measurements of the B0 to rho+rho-branching fraction, longitudinal polarization fraction f_L, and theCP-violating parameters S_{long} and C_{long} are:  B(B0-> rho+rho-) = (25.5 +/- 2.1 (stat) +3.6/-3.9 (syst))*10^-6 f_L = 0.992+/- 0.024 (stat) +0.026/-0.013 (syst) S_{long} = -0.17 +/- 0.20 (stat)+0.05/-0.06 (syst) C_{long} = 0.01 +/- 0.15 (stat) +/- 0.06 (syst) We determinethe unitarity triangle angle alpha, using an isospin analysis of B to rhorhodecays. One of the two solutions, alpha = [73.1, 117.0] degrees at 68% CL iscompatible with standard model-based fits of existing data. Constraints on theunitarity triangle are also evaluated using an SU(3) symmetry based approach.
label: human

text: We present an analysis of B⁰ → ρ⁺ρ⁻ decays based on a large sample of BB̄ pairs collected at a B Factory, measuring the branching fraction, longitudinal polarization fraction f_L, and time-dependent CP-violating parameters S_long and C_long for the longitudinally polarized component. The decay exhibits a highly dominant longitudinal polarization (f_L close to 1), with a measured branching fraction on the order of 25 × 10⁻⁶ and small CP asymmetries consistent with expectations. Using an isospin analysis of B → ρρ decays, which helps constrain the penguin contributions, we extract the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) unitarity triangle angle α. The results yield two possible solutions for α, one of which is compatible with the Standard Model expectations.
label: llm

text: The purpose of this article is to show that the introduction of hiddenvariables to describe individual events is fully consistent with thestatistical predictions of quantum theory. We illustrate the validity of thisassertion by discussing two fundamental experiments on correlated photons whichare believed to behave ``violently non-classical''. Our considerations carryover to correlated pairs of neutral particles of spin one-half in a singletstate. Much in the spirit of Einstein's conviction we come to the conclusionthat the state vector of a system does not provide an exhaustive description ofthe individual physical system. We also briefly discuss an experiment on``quantum teleportation'' and demonstrate that our completely local approachleads to a full understanding of the experiment indicating the absence of anyteleportation phenomenon. We caution that the indiscriminated use of the term``Quantum Theory'' tends to obscure distinct differences between the quantummechanics of massive particles and the propagation of photons. It is emphasizedthat the properties of polarizers, beam splitters, halfwave plates etc. used inphoton-correlation experiments are defined by the laws of classical optics.Hence, understanding the outcome of those experiments requires a well-foundedinterconnection between classical and quantum electrodynamics free fromunnecessary hypotheses.
label: human

text: The Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) paradox, introduced in 1935, challenges the completeness of quantum mechanics by highlighting apparent non-local influences in entangled systems. In the context of photon pairs, the paradox manifests through perfect anti-correlations in polarization measurements when analyzers are aligned, suggesting elements of reality that quantum theory does not fully describe. John Bell's 1964 theorem formalized this issue by deriving inequalities that any local realistic theory must satisfy for correlation functions in bipartite measurements. Experimental realizations of the EPR-Bohm setup using entangled photons, typically produced via parametric down-conversion, have consistently shown stronger correlations than those permitted by Bell's inequalities. Early photon correlation experiments, such as those by Aspect and colleagues in the 1980s, demonstrated violations but were subject to loopholes, including the detection loophole due to inefficient detectors and the locality loophole from insufficient spatial separation. Subsequent advancements addressed these limitations individually, yet simultaneous closure remained challenging until 2015. Loophole-free Bell tests, employing entangled electron spins or optimized photonic systems with high-efficiency detectors and rapid random setting choices, confirmed violations of the CHSH inequality with high statistical significance.
label: llm

text: An efficient quantum cryptography network protocol is proposed withd-dimension polarized photons, without resorting to entanglement and quantummemory. A server on the network, say Alice, provides the service for preparingand measuring single photons whose initial state are |0>. The users code theinformation on the single photons with some unitary operations. For preventingthe untrustworthy server Alice from eavesdropping the quantum lines, anonorthogonal-coding technique (decoy-photon technique) is used in the processthat the quantum signal is transmitted between the users. This protocol doesnot require the servers and the users to store the quantum state and almost allof the single photons can be used for carrying the information, which makes itmore convenient for application than others with present technology. We alsodiscuss the case with a faint laser pulse.
label: human

text: An efficient quantum cryptography network protocol is proposed utilizing d-dimensional polarized single photons, eliminating the need for entanglement or quantum memory. In this setup, a central server prepares and measures photons in a fixed initial state, while users encode information through unitary operations on the transmitted photons. To establish secure communication between users, photons are exchanged via the server, with users applying operations corresponding to their key bits. Security against a potentially untrustworthy server is achieved by incorporating a decoy-photon technique based on nonorthogonal states during photon transmission. This approach ensures that eavesdropping attempts introduce detectable errors without requiring quantum storage at any node. Furthermore, the protocol allows nearly all photons to contribute to key generation, resulting in high efficiency and practical feasibility with current technology.
label: llm

text: We study planar clusters consisting of loops including a Josephson$\pi$-junction ($\pi$-rings). Each $\pi$-ring carries a persistent current andbehaves as a classical orbital moment. The type of particular state associatedwith the orientation of orbital moments at the cluster depends on theinteraction between these orbital moments and can be easily controlled, i.e. bya bias current or by other means. We show that these systems can be describedby the two-dimensional Ising model with competing nearest-neighbor and diagonalinteractions and investigate the phase diagram of this model. Thecharacteristic features of the model are analyzed based on the exact solutionsfor small clusters such as a 5-site square plaquette as well as on a mean-fieldtype approach for the infinite square lattice of Ising spins. The results arecompared with spin patterns obtained by Monte Carlo simulations for the 100$\times$ 100 square lattice and with experiment. We show that the $\pi$-ringclusters may be used as a new type of superconducting memory elements. Theobtained results may be verified in experiments and are applicable to adiabaticquantum computing where the states are switched adiabatically with the slowchange of coupling constants.
label: human

text: We investigate the two-dimensional Ising model on a square lattice incorporating competing nearest-neighbor and diagonal interactions, which introduces frustration and leads to rich phase behavior. Planar clusters and arrays composed of superconducting loops containing a Josephson π-junction, known as π-rings, are considered as physical realizations of this model. Each π-ring sustains a persistent current, effectively behaving as a classical orbital magnetic moment with two possible orientations. The interactions between these orbital moments arise from magnetic dipole couplings, which can be tuned externally, for instance, via bias currents. This system is mapped onto the frustrated Ising model, where spins correspond to the directions of the orbital moments. The phase diagram of the model is analyzed, revealing regions of ferromagnetic order, superantiferromagnetic ordering, and disordered or glassy states depending on the ratio of interaction strengths. Frustration effects give rise to degenerate ground states and topological defects in certain parameter regimes. The controllability of interactions in π-ring arrays allows for the exploration of these phases experimentally. Furthermore, the ability to adiabatically vary the coupling constants enables state switching while remaining in the ground state manifold.
label: llm

text: In the previous paper, based on the $SU(2)_{f}\times SU(2)_{s}$ heavy quarksymmetries of the QCD Lagrangian in the heavy quark limit, the Bethe-Salpeterequation for the heavy baryon $\Lambda_b$ was established with the picture that$\Lambda_b$ is composed of a heavy quark and a scalar light diquark. In thepresent work, we apply this model to calculate $\mu_\pi^2$ for $\Lambda_b$, theaverage kinetic energy of the heavy quark inside $\Lambda_{b}$. This quantityis particularly interesting since it can be measured in experiments and sinceit contributes to the inclusive semileptonic decays of $\Lambda_b$ whencontributions from higher order terms in $1/M_b$ expansions are taken intoaccount and consequently influences the determination of theCabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix elements $V_{ub}$ and $V_{cb}$. We find that$\mu_\pi^2$ for $\Lambda_b$ is $0.25GeV^2$ $\sim$ $0.95GeV^2$, depending on theparameters in the model including the light diquark mass and the interactionstrength between the heavy quark and the light diquark in the kernel of the BSequation. We also find that this result is consistent with the value of$\mu_\pi^2$ for $\Lambda_b$ which is derived from the experimental value of$\mu_\pi^2$ for the $B$ meson with the aid of the heavy quark effective theory.
label: human

text: In this work, we employ the Bethe-Salpeter equation approach to investigate the average kinetic energy of the bottom quark within the $\Lambda_b$ baryon, denoted as $\mu_\pi^2$. Building on a prior establishment of the Bethe-Salpeter equation for $\Lambda_b$ utilizing heavy quark symmetries in the infinite mass limit, we model the baryon as a bound state of a heavy quark and a scalar light diquark. The calculation reveals that $\mu_\pi^2$ ranges from approximately 0.25 GeV² to 0.95 GeV², depending on model parameters such as the light diquark mass and the interaction kernel strength. This parameter is of particular significance as it can be extracted from experimental measurements of inclusive semileptonic $\Lambda_b$ decays and impacts the precise determination of CKM matrix elements $|V_{cb}|$ and $|V_{ub}|$. Furthermore, the obtained values are consistent with those inferred from the corresponding quantity in $B$ mesons via the heavy quark effective theory.
label: llm

text: We study the isospin asymmetry in the isoscalar (IS) excitations in themirror nuclei $^{14}$O and $^{14}$C by using the Hartree-Fock(HF)+random phaseapproximation (RPA) linear response function theory with a Skyrme interactionto take into account the continuum effect properly. The asymmetry in the ISmonopole, dipole responses is pointed out in the continuum near the particlethreshold with respect to the excitation energy and the sum rule strength. Onthe other hand, no clear sign of the asymmetry is found in the giant resonance(GR) region. In the quadrupole case, the calculated strengths of the mirrornuclei show almost the same energy dependence from the threshold to the GRregion. It is found that the transition densities of the monopole response showan extended halo structure near the threshold, while those of GR region show atypical radial dependence of the compressional collective mode without any haloeffect. Contrary to the transition densities of the monopole response, those ofquadrupole response do not show any sign of the extended feature of wavefunctions neither near the threshold nor the GR energy region. Calculatedstrength distributions of the IS multipole states are compared with recentexperimental data obtained by the multipole decomposition analysis of $\alpha $inelastic scattering on $^{14}$O.
label: human

text: We investigate the isospin asymmetry in isoscalar excitations of the mirror nuclei $^{14}$C and $^{14}$O, focusing on the continuum states near particle emission thresholds. Employing the Hartree-Fock plus random phase approximation (HF+RPA) framework with a Skyrme effective interaction, we explicitly account for continuum coupling to accurately describe unbound states and response functions. Calculations reveal pronounced asymmetry in the isoscalar monopole and dipole strength distributions in the low-energy continuum, manifesting as shifts in peak excitation energies and differences in integrated sum rule strengths between the two mirrors. This near-threshold asymmetry arises primarily from Coulomb effects and differing particle emission thresholds, which alter the continuum discretization and single-particle wave functions. In contrast, the giant resonance region at higher excitation energies exhibits negligible isospin asymmetry for both monopole and dipole modes, indicating that collective effects dominate over isospin-breaking contributions there. For isoscalar quadrupole excitations, the strength functions of $^{14}$C and $^{14}$O display nearly identical energy dependence across the continuum and giant resonance regimes. These findings highlight the sensitivity of low-lying continuum responses to isospin symmetry breaking in light mirror nuclei, providing insights into nuclear structure beyond discrete bound states.
label: llm

text: The nilpotent bicone of a finite dimensional complex reductive Lie algebra gis the subset of elements in g x g whose subspace generated by the componentsis contained in the nilpotent cone of g. The main result of this note is thatthe nilpotent bicone is a complete intersection. This affirmatively answers aconjecture of Kraft-Wallach concerning the nullcone. In addition, we introduceand study the characteristic submodule of g. The properties of the nilpotentbicone and the characteristic submodule are known to be very important for theunderstanding of the commuting variety and its ideal of definition. In order tostudy the nilpotent bicone, we introduce another subvariety, the principalbicone. The nilpotent bicone, as well as the principal bicone, are linked tojet schemes. We study their dimensions using arguments from motivicintegration. Namely, we follow methods developed inhttp://arxiv.org/abs/math/0008002v5 .
label: human

text: Let \(\mathfrak{g}\) be a finite-dimensional complex reductive Lie algebra. The nilpotent cone \(\mathcal{N}_{\mathfrak{g}}\) consists of elements whose adjoint action is nilpotent. The nilpotent bicone \(\mathcal{B}_{\mathfrak{g}}\) is the subvariety of \(\mathfrak{g} \times \mathfrak{g}\) comprising pairs \((x, y)\) such that the subspace spanned by \(x\) and \(y\) is contained in \(\mathcal{N}_{\mathfrak{g}}\). This paper establishes that \(\mathcal{B}_{\mathfrak{g}}\) is a complete intersection variety, resolving a conjecture of Kraft and Wallach regarding the nullcone. To investigate \(\mathcal{B}_{\mathfrak{g}}\), we introduce the principal bicone, a related subvariety whose properties facilitate the analysis. Additionally, we define and study the characteristic submodule of \(\mathfrak{g}\), a novel invariant submodule with significant structural implications. These objects play a crucial role in elucidating the geometry of the commuting variety and the ideal defining its nullcone.
label: llm

text: We investigate the potential (small) deviations from the unitarity of themixing matrix that are expected to occur, because of mass splittings, in theQuantum Field Theory of non-degenerate coupled systems. We extend our previousanalysis concerning mixing angles, which led to a precise determination of theCabibbo angle, to the case of three generations of fermions. We show that thesame condition for neutral currents of mass eigenstates, i.e. that universalityof diagonal currents is violated with the same strength as the absence ofnon-diagonal ones, is satisfied: on one hand, by the three CKM mixing angleswith a precision higher than the experimental uncertainty; on the other hand,by a neutrino-like mixing pattern in which theta_{23} is maximal, and tan (2theta_{12})=2. This last pattern turns out to satisfy exactly the "quark-leptoncomplementarity condition" theta_c + theta_{12}= pi/4. Moreover, among allsolutions, two values for the third neutrino mixing angle arise which satisfythe bound sin^2(theta_{13}) < 0.1: theta_{13} = +/- 5.7 10^{-3} and theta_{13}= +/- 0.2717. The so-called "Neighborhood of the Standard Model" is thusconfirmed to exhibit special patterns which presumably originate in physics"Beyond the Standard Model".
label: human

text: We investigate small deviations from unitarity in the fermion mixing matrix arising from mass splittings in non-degenerate coupled systems within quantum field theory. Extending prior work on two-generation mixing, which precisely determined the Cabibbo angle, this study addresses three generations of fermions. A key condition is imposed on neutral currents in mass eigenstates: violations of universality in diagonal currents match the strength of residual non-diagonal flavor-changing currents. This condition is remarkably satisfied by the three observed CKM quark mixing angles, with agreement exceeding experimental precision. Simultaneously, it predicts a lepton mixing pattern featuring maximal θ_{23} and tan(2θ_{12}) = 2. This predicted leptonic pattern exactly fulfills the quark-lepton complementarity relation θ_C + θ_{12} = π/4. These findings suggest that the observed mixing angles lie in close proximity to an underlying flavor-symmetric structure of the Standard Model, mildly perturbed by non-degenerate masses.
label: llm

text: Electron-positron pair creation due to combined nuclear Coulomb and stronglaser fields is investigated for the tunneling regime. The energy spectra andangular distributions of the pair are found analytically for the first time.The energy spectrum for each lepton exhibits a sharp maximum located well abovethe threshold for any polarization of the laser field. The angulardistributions of leptons depend on the polarization: for the linearpolarization both leptons move predominantly along the laser beam direction;for the circular polarization leptons are emitted in a thin-walled conecentered on the laser beam. The spectral and angular distributions found aregoverned by the intensity and frequency of the field, and the frequencyindependent total pair creation rates comply with the previously known results.A new method of calculation - the vicinal approximation - which uses the factthat the pair production takes place in the close vicinity of the nucleus, issuggested.
label: human

text: Abstract Electron-positron pair creation resulting from the combined action of a nuclear Coulomb field and a strong laser field is investigated in the tunneling regime. Analytical expressions are derived for the energy spectra and angular distributions of the created electron-positron pairs. The energy spectrum of each lepton exhibits a pronounced sharp maximum located significantly above the pair production threshold, a feature that persists irrespective of the laser field polarization. These results highlight the substantial influence of the assisting Coulomb field on the nonperturbative pair production process in the presence of intense laser radiation.
label: llm

text: A new class of Marginal Structural Models (MSMs), History-Restricted MSMs(HRMSMs), was recently introduced for longitudinal data for the purpose ofdefining causal parameters which may often be better suited for public healthresearch or at least more practicable than MSMs \citejoffe,feldman. HRMSMsallow investigators to analyze the causal effect of a treatment on an outcomebased on a fixed, shorter and user-specified history of exposure compared toMSMs. By default, the latter represent the treatment causal effect of interestbased on a treatment history defined by the treatments assigned between thestudy's start and outcome collection. We lay out in this article the formalstatistical framework behind HRMSMs. Beyond allowing a more flexible causalanalysis, HRMSMs improve computational tractability and mitigate statisticalpower concerns when designing longitudinal studies. We also develop threeconsistent estimators of HRMSM parameters under sufficient model assumptions:the Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighted (IPTW), G-computation and DoubleRobust (DR) estimators. In addition, we show that the assumptions commonlyadopted for identification and consistent estimation of MSM parameters(existence of counterfactuals, consistency, time-ordering and sequentialrandomization assumptions) also lead to identification and consistentestimation of HRMSM parameters.
label: human

text: Longitudinal studies often involve time-varying treatments and confounders, complicating causal inference due to feedback between exposure and confounding variables over time. Traditional regression approaches can yield biased estimates in such settings, while standard marginal structural models (MSMs) address this by using inverse probability of treatment weighting but typically require modeling the full treatment history from study onset. This article introduces history-restricted marginal structural models (HRMSMs), a generalization of MSMs that defines causal parameters based on a user-specified, fixed-length recent exposure history rather than the entire cumulative history. HRMSMs are particularly advantageous in public health research, offering more practicable and interpretable causal effects, enhanced computational efficiency, and reduced concerns regarding statistical power in study design. The formal counterfactual framework for HRMSMs is presented, establishing identifiability conditions under assumptions of no unmeasured confounding, positivity, and consistency. Three consistent estimators for HRMSM parameters are developed: the inverse probability of treatment weighted (IPTW) estimator, the G-computation formula estimator, and the doubly robust estimator, which combines both approaches for improved robustness against model misspecification.
label: llm

text: We show that hard-scattering factorization is violated in the production ofhigh-p_T hadrons in hadron-hadron collisions, in the case that the hadrons areback-to-back, so that k_T factorization is to be used. The explicitcounterexample that we construct is for the single-spin asymmetry with one beamtransversely polarized. The Sivers function needed here has particularsensitivity to the Wilson lines in the parton densities. We use a greatlysimplified model theory to make the breakdown of factorization easy to checkexplicitly. But the counterexample implies that standard arguments forfactorization fail not just for the single-spin asymmetry but for theunpolarized cross section for back-to-back hadron production in QCD inhadron-hadron collisions. This is unlike corresponding cases in e^+e^-annihilation, Drell-Yan, and deeply inelastic scattering. Moreover, the resultendangers factorization for more general hadroproduction processes.
label: human

text: Abstract In high-energy hadron-hadron collisions, the production of back-to-back hadrons with high transverse momentum ($p_T$) is commonly analyzed within the framework of $k_T$-factorization, which assumes that the cross section can be expressed as a convolution of transverse-momentum-dependent parton densities and an on-shell hard-scattering kernel. We demonstrate that this standard $k_T$-factorization is violated for such processes in quantum chromodynamics. An explicit counterexample is constructed in a simplified model theory, initially for the single-spin asymmetry arising when one incoming hadron is transversely polarized, where the required Sivers function exhibits particular sensitivity to Wilson-line effects in the parton distributions. Detailed calculations reveal that the factorization-breaking contributions do not cancel, even in the unpolarized cross section for back-to-back high-$p_T$ hadron production. This breakdown contrasts sharply with the validity of corresponding factorization theorems in processes such as $e^+e^-$ annihilation.
label: llm

text: The chemical analysis of secondary stars of low mass X-ray binaries providesan opportunity to study the formation processes of compact objects, eitherblack holes or neutron stars. Following the discovery of overabundances of$\alpha$-elements in the HIRES/Keck spectrum of the secondary star of NovaScorpii 1994 (Israelian et al. 1999), we obtained UVES/VLT high-resolutionspectroscopy with the aim of performing a detailed abundance analysis of thissecondary star. Using a $\chi2$-minimization procedure and a grid of syntheticspectra, we derive the stellar parameters and atmospheric abundances of O, Mg,Al, Ca, Ti, Fe and Ni, using a new UVES spectrum and the HIRES spectrum.Theabundances of Al, Ca, Ti, Fe and Ni seem to be consistent with solar values,whereas Na, and especially O, Mg, Si and S are significantly enhanced incomparison with Galactic trends of these elements. A comparison withspherically and non-spherically symmetric supernova explosion models mayprovide stringent constraints to the model parameters as mass-cut and theexplosion energy, in particular from the relative abundances of Si, S, Ca, Ti,Fe and Ni. Most probably the black hole in this system formed in a hypernovaexplosion of a 30--35 \Msun progenitor star with a mass-cut in the range 2--3.5\Msun. However, these models produce abundances of Al and Na almost ten timeshigher than the observed values.

text: The black hole X-ray binary Nova Scorpii 1994 (GRO J1655-40) hosts a dynamically confirmed black hole primary and a subgiant secondary star whose atmosphere retains a fossil record of the system's formation history. Previous high-resolution spectroscopy revealed apparent overabundances of α-elements in the secondary, interpreted as evidence for pollution by supernova ejecta from the black hole progenitor. This study presents an improved chemical abundance analysis using updated high-resolution spectra and refined modeling techniques to reassess these claims. We derive precise elemental abundances for key α-elements (O, Mg, Si, S, Ti) relative to iron, incorporating non-LTE corrections and synthetic spectrum fitting. The results indicate significant overabundance primarily in oxygen, while other α-elements show near-solar or modestly enhanced ratios, with uncertainties reduced compared to earlier works. These findings refine constraints on the supernova nucleosynthesis yields and progenitor mass (likely 25–40 M⊙). The persistent α-enhancement, particularly in oxygen, supports a supernova origin for the black hole while highlighting the need for careful treatment of observational biases in similar systems.

text: Technological innovation has extensively been studied to make firmssustainable and more competitive. Within this context, the most importantrecent issue has been the dynamics of collaborative innovation among firms. Wetherefore investigated a patent network, especially focusing on its spatialcharacteristics. The results can be summarized as follows. (1) The degreedistribution in a patent network follows a power law. A firm can then beconnected to many firms via hubs connected to the firm. (2) The neighbors'average degree has a null correlation, but the clustering coefficient has anegative correlation. The latter means that there is a hierarchical structureand bridging different modules may shorten the paths between the nodes in them.(3) The distance of links not only indicates the regional accumulations offirms, but the importance of time it takes to travel, which plays a key role increating links. (4) The ratio of internal links in cities indicates that wehave to consider the existing links firms have to facilitate the creation ofnew links.

text: This study examines the spatial characteristics of joint patent application networks in Japan, utilizing data from the Japan Patent Office to map collaborative innovation among applicants. Joint applications, where multiple entities co-apply for patents, serve as proxies for inter-organizational R&D collaborations and knowledge exchange. The network is constructed with nodes representing applicants (firms, universities, or individuals) and edges indicating co-applications, weighted by frequency. Geocoding applicant addresses reveals pronounced spatial patterns in these collaborations. Collaborations are significantly localized, with a substantial proportion occurring within short geographical distances, typically under 100 km. This localization persists despite advancements in communication technologies, suggesting the enduring importance of proximity for tacit knowledge transfer. Major urban centers, particularly Tokyo and Osaka, emerge as central hubs with high degree centrality and betweenness in the network. Links between distant regions are less frequent but often involve high-value or complex technologies.

text: We present a study of the shapes, orientations, and alignments of Galacticdark matter subhalos in the ``Via Lactea'' simulation of a Milky Way-size LCDMhost halo. Whereas isolated dark matter halos tend to be prolate, subhalos arepredominantly triaxial. Overall subhalos are more spherical than the host halo,with minor to major and intermediate to major axis ratios of 0.68 and 0.83,respectively. Like isolated halos, subhalos tend to be less spherical in theircentral regions. The principal axis ratios are independent of subhalo mass,when the shapes are measured within a physical scale like r_Vmax, the radius ofthe peak of the circular velocity curve. Subhalos tend to be slightly morespherical closer to the host halo center. The spatial distribution of thesubhalos traces the prolate shape of the host halo when they are selected bythe largest V_max they ever had, i.e. before they experienced strong tidal massloss. The subhalos' orientation is not random: the major axis tends to alignwith the direction towards the host halo center. This alignment disappears forhalos beyond 3 r_200 and is more pronounced when the shapes are measured in theouter regions of the subhalos. The radial alignment is preserved during asubhalo's orbit and they become elongated during pericenter passage, indicatingthat the alignment is likely caused by the host halo's tidal forces. Thesetidal interactions with the host halo act to make subhalos rounder over time.

text: Abstract We investigate the shapes, orientations, and alignments of dark matter subhalos within a Milky Way-sized host halo in the Via Lactea high-resolution ΛCDM simulation. Unlike isolated dark matter halos, which typically exhibit prolate shapes, Galactic subhalos are predominantly triaxial. Overall, subhalos appear more spherical than their host halo, characterized by average minor-to-major and intermediate-to-major axis ratios of approximately 0.68 and 0.83, respectively. Similar to isolated halos, subhalos display greater sphericity in their outer regions compared to their central parts. The principal axis ratios remain independent of subhalo mass when shapes are measured within a fixed physical scale, such as the radius of maximum circular velocity (r_Vmax). Subhalos located closer to the host halo center tend to be slightly more spherical, likely due to enhanced tidal processing. The spatial distribution of subhalos, when selected by their peak historical Vmax (prior to significant tidal stripping), traces the prolate geometry of the host halo. The orientations of subhalos are far from random, with their major axes preferentially aligned toward the host halo center. This radial alignment weakens significantly beyond approximately 3r_200 and is more pronounced when shapes are measured in the outer regions of the subhalos. The alignment persists throughout subhalo orbits and strengthens during pericenter passages, where subhalos become noticeably more elongated.

text: We consider Kac's random walk on $n$-dimensional rotation matrices, whereeach step is a random rotation in the plane generated by two randomly pickedcoordinates. We show that this process converges to the Haar measure on$\mathit{SO}(n)$ in the $L^2$ transportation cost (Wasserstein) metric in$O(n^2\ln n)$ steps. We also prove that our bound is at most a $O(\ln n)$factor away from optimal. Previous bounds, due to Diaconis/Saloff-Coste andPak/Sidenko, had extra powers of $n$ and held only for $L^1$ transportationcost. Our proof method includes a general result of independent interest, akinto the path coupling method of Bubley and Dyer. Suppose that $P$ is a Markovchain on a Polish length space $(M,d)$ and that for all $x,y\in M$ with$d(x,y)\ll1$ there is a coupling $(X,Y)$ of one step of $P$ from $x$ and $y$(resp.) that contracts distances by a $(\xi+o(1))$ factor on average. Then themap $\mu\mapsto\mu P$ is $\xi$-contracting in the transportation cost metric.

text: Kac's random walk is a Markov chain on the special orthogonal group SO(n), designed to generate approximately uniform random rotation matrices. At each step, two coordinates are selected uniformly at random, and a random rotation is applied in the plane they span. The stationary distribution of this irreducible and aperiodic chain is the Haar measure on SO(n), the unique uniform probability measure on the compact group. This paper analyzes the rate of convergence to this equilibrium distribution. Previous works provided bounds on the mixing time in the L¹ transportation cost metric, but with suboptimal polynomial factors in n. Here, we establish convergence in the stronger L² transportation cost (Wasserstein) metric within O(n² ln n) steps. We further demonstrate that this bound is nearly optimal, differing from the best possible by at most an O(ln n) factor. The proof relies on a novel contraction argument in the Wasserstein metric, extending ideas from path coupling to continuous spaces with local contraction properties.

text: Supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB) is expected with the hierarchicalgalaxy formation model. Currently, physics processes dominating the evolutionof a SMBHB are unclear. An interesting question is whether we couldobservationally determine the evolution of SMBHB and give constraints on thephysical processes. Jet precession have been observed in many AGNs andgenerally attributed to disk precession. In this paper we calculate the timevariation of jet precession and conclude that jet precession is accelerated inSMBHB systems but decelerated in others. The acceleration of jet precession$dP_{\rm pr} / dt$ is related to jet precession timescale $P_{\rm pr}$ andSMBHB evolution timescale $\tau_{\rm a}$, ${dP_{\rm pr} \over dt} \simeq -\Lambda {P_{\rm pr} \over \tau_{\rm a}}$. Our calculations based on the modelsfor jet precession and SMBHB evolution show that $dP_{\rm pr} / dt$ can be ashigh as about $- 1.0$ with a typical value -0.2 and can be easily detected. Wediscussed the differential jet precession for NGC1275 observed in theliterature. If the observed rapid acceleration of jet precession is true, thejet precession is due to the orbital motion of an unbound SMBHB with mass ratio$q\approx 0.76$. When jets precessed from the ancient bubbles to the currentlyactive jets, the separation of SMBHB decrease from about $1.46 {\rm Kpc}$ to$0.80 {\rm Kpc}$ with an averaged decreasing velocity $da/dt \simeq - 1.54\times 10^6 {\rm cm/s}$ and evolution timescale $\tau_{\rm a} \approx 7.5\times10^7 {\rm yr}$. However, if we assume a steady jet precession for many cycles,the observations implies a hard SMBHB with mass ratio $q\approx 0.21$ andseparation $a\approx 0.29 {\rm pc}$.

text: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) are predicted to form frequently in galactic nuclei as a consequence of hierarchical galaxy mergers. The evolution of such binaries remains poorly constrained observationally, particularly the dominant physical processes driving their orbital decay. Jet precession observed in many active galactic nuclei (AGN) is often attributed to the precession of the accretion disk around the primary black hole. This precession can be induced by torques from a secondary black hole in a binary system. As the binary separation decreases due to dynamical friction, viscous interactions, or gravitational wave emission, the precession period is expected to shorten over time. Consequently, the rate of jet precession may accelerate, providing a potential diagnostic of binary hardening. We investigate the coupling between SMBHB orbital evolution and the acceleration of jet precession across different evolutionary regimes. In the stellar dynamical friction phase, the hardening rate is modest, leading to slow changes in precession rate. Transition to gas-driven migration or circumbinary disk interactions can significantly enhance the acceleration of precession. Measurements of precession acceleration in observed jets could thus constrain binary parameters, such as mass ratio and separation, as well as the viscosity of the surrounding medium. Our findings suggest that rapid precession acceleration, if confirmed in specific sources, implies ongoing binary inspiral and offers a pathway to probe SMBHB demographics in galactic nuclei.

text: We set an upper limit on the mass of a supersymmetric neutralino dark matterparticle using the MicrOMEGAS and DarkSUSY software packages and the mostrecent constraints on relic density from combined WMAP and SDSS data. Weexplore several different possible scenarios within the MSSM, includingcoannihilation with charginos and sfermions and annihilation through a massiveHiggs resonance, using low energy mass inputs. We find that no coannihilationscenario is consistent with dark matter in observed abundance with a massgreater than 2.5 TeV for a wino--type particle or 1.8 TeV for a Higgsino--type.Contrived scenarios involving Higgs resonances with finely--tuned massparameters can allow masses as high as 34 TeV. The resulting gamma--ray energydistribution is not in agreement with the recent multi--TeV gamma ray spectrumobserved by H.E.S.S. originating from the center of the Milky Way. Our resultsare relevent only for dark matter densities resulting from a thermal origin.

text: The neutralino, the lightest supersymmetric particle in many extensions of the Standard Model, remains a leading candidate for cold dark matter due to its stability under R-parity conservation and weak-scale interactions. This study investigates upper bounds on the neutralino mass imposed by the requirement that its thermal relic abundance matches the observed dark matter density, as determined from cosmological observations. Using numerical tools such as MicrOMEGAS and DarkSUSY, we explore various annihilation and coannihilation scenarios within the minimal supersymmetric standard model. For pure wino or Higgsino neutralinos, efficient annihilation channels allow masses up to approximately 2.5 TeV while satisfying relic density constraints. Coannihilation with nearly degenerate charginos or sfermions generally reduces the viable upper mass limit compared to pure states. Highly tuned resonances with heavy Higgs bosons can extend the allowable mass to around 34 TeV in contrived parameter regions, though such scenarios produce gamma-ray spectra inconsistent with observations from the Galactic center.

text: We study the growth of cosmological perturbations in the model ofLorentz-violating massive gravity. The Friedman equation in this model acquiresan unconventional term due to the Lorentz-breaking condensates which has theequation of state w = -1 / (3 gamma) with gamma being a free parameter takingvalues outside of the range [0,1/3]. Apart from the standard contributions, theperturbations above the Friedmann background contain an extra piece which isproportional to an arbitrary function theta(x) of the space coordinates. Thisfunction appears as an integration constant and corresponds to anon-propagating scalar mode which may, however, become dynamical with theaccount of the higher-derivative corrections. For -1 < gamma < 0 and gamma = 1the ``anomalous'' perturbations grow slower than the standard ones and thus themodel is compatible with observations. Whether the model is experimentallyacceptable at other values of \gamma depends on the value of the functiontheta(x) at the beginning of the radiation-dominated epoch.

text: Massive gravity theories, which assign a nonzero mass to the graviton, provide a framework for modifying general relativity on large scales while potentially explaining cosmic acceleration without dark energy. This work investigates the impact of a massive graviton on the formation of large-scale structures in the universe, focusing on the evolution of linear density perturbations in a matter-dominated era. We derive the modified perturbation equations, incorporating the graviton mass term, and analyze the growth factor for subhorizon modes. The results indicate that the finite range of gravitational interactions in massive gravity leads to a scale-dependent suppression of structure growth on large wavelengths compared to standard ΛCDM predictions. Numerical solutions of the growth equation reveal enhanced clustering on intermediate scales but reduced power on very large scales, depending on the graviton mass parameter. These deviations offer testable signatures in upcoming galaxy surveys and cosmic microwave background observations, providing a means to constrain massive gravity models against general relativity.

text: The group Hameo (M,\omega) of Hamiltonian homeomorphisms of a connectedsymplectic manifold (M,\omega) was defined and studied in [7] and further in[6]. In these papers, the authors consistently used the L^{(1,\infty)}-Hofernorm (and not the L^\infty-Hofer norm) on the space of Hamiltonian paths (seebelow for the definitions). A justification for this choice was given in [7].In this article we study the L^\infty-case. In view of the fact that the Hofernorm on the group Ham (M,\omega) of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms does not dependon the choice of the L^{(1,\infty)}-norm vs. the L^\infty-norm [9], Y.-G. Ohand D. McDuff (private communications) asked whether the two notions ofHamiltonian homeomorphisms arising from the different norms coincide. We willgive an affirmative answer to this question in this paper.

text: The group of Hamiltonian homeomorphisms, denoted Hameo(M, ω), on a connected symplectic manifold (M, ω) was previously defined using the L^{(1,∞)}-Hofer norm on Hamiltonian paths. This paper investigates the alternative definition based on the L^∞-Hofer norm, motivated by the known equivalence of these norms for the Hofer metric on the group of smooth Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. We prove that the two definitions yield the same group, denoted Hameo_∞(M, ω), establishing Hameo(M, ω) = Hameo_∞(M, ω). The proof relies on energy-capacity inequalities and properties of continuous Hamiltonian flows. This equivalence resolves an open question and confirms the robustness of the Hamiltonian homeomorphism group under different norm choices.

text: The phase of Super-Soft-Source (SSS) emission of the sixth recorded outburstof the recurrent nova RS Oph was observed twice with Chandra and once withXMM-Newton. The observations were taken on days 39.7, 54.0, and 66.9 afteroutburst. We confirm a 35-sec period on day 54.0 and found that it originatesfrom the SSS emission and not from the shock. We discus the bound-freeabsorption by neutral elements in the line of sight, resonance absorption linesplus self-absorbed emission line components, collisionally excited emissionlines from the shock, He-like intersystem lines, and spectral changes during anepisode of high-amplitude variability. We find a decrease of the oxygen K-shellabsorption edge that can be explained by photoionization of oxygen. Theabsorption component has average velocities of -1286+-267 km/s on day 39.7 andof -771+-65 km/s on day 66.9. The wavelengths of the emission line componentsare consistent with their rest wavelengths as confirmed by measurements ofnon-self absorbed He-like intersystem lines. We have evidence that these linesoriginate from the shock rather than the outer layers of the outflow and may bephotoexcited in addition to collisional excitations. We found collisionallyexcited emission lines that are fading at wavelengths shorter than 15A thatoriginate from the radiatively cooling shock. On day 39.5 we find a systematicblue shift of -526+-114 km/s from these lines. We found anomalous He-like f/iratios which indicates either high densities or significant UV radiation nearthe plasma where the emission lines are formed. During the phase of strongvariability the spectral hardness light curve overlies the total light curvewhen shifted by 1000sec. This can be explained by photoionization of neutraloxygen in the line of sight if the densities of order 10^{10}-10^{11} cm^{-3}.

text: The supersoft source (SSS) phase during the 2006 outburst of the recurrent nova RS Ophiuchi was observed using high-resolution grating spectroscopy from the Chandra and XMM-Newton observatories. Observations were conducted on days 39.7 and 66.9 after optical maximum with Chandra, and on day 54.0 with XMM-Newton. These data capture the evolution of the central white dwarf as it transitioned into a luminous soft X-ray emitter following the initial shock-dominated phase. The X-ray spectra reveal a dominant blackbody-like continuum from the burning white dwarf, superimposed with numerous deep absorption lines from highly ionized species. These absorption features exhibit blueshifts corresponding to expansion velocities of approximately 700–1200 km/s, significantly lower than typical in classical novae. Such reduced velocities likely result from the interaction of ejecta with the dense wind of the red giant companion. The spectra on day 54.0 exhibit a prominent quasi-periodic oscillation with a period of approximately 35 seconds. This periodicity is confirmed to originate from the SSS component rather than residual shock emission. Significant variability in X-ray flux and spectral hardness was detected across the observations, indicative of changing conditions in the expanding atmosphere or circumstellar absorption. Preliminary blackbody modeling of the continuum yields effective temperatures on the order of several hundred thousand Kelvin, with the source exhibiting high intrinsic luminosity. Photoelectric absorption components, including a notable O I edge, are required to account for the observed spectral structure and its temporal changes. The data suggest that the white dwarf mass is at least 1.2 solar masses, reinforcing RS Ophiuchi as a potential progenitor candidate for a Type Ia supernova. These observations provide critical insights into the early nuclear-burning phase of recurrent symbiotic novae embedded in dense circumstellar.

text: We present results from Spitzer Space Telescope observations of themid-infrared phase variations of three short-period extrasolar planetarysystems: HD 209458, HD 179949 and 51 Peg. We gathered IRAC images in multiplewavebands at eight phases of each planet's orbit. We find the uncertainty inrelative photometry from one epoch to the next to be significantly larger thanthe photon counting error at 3.6 micron and 4.5 micron. We are able to place2-sigma upper limits of only 2% on the phase variations at these wavelengths.At 8 micron the epoch-to-epoch systematic uncertainty is comparable to thephoton counting noise and we detect a phase function for HD 179949 which is inphase with the planet's orbit and with a relative peak-to-trough amplitude of0.00141(33). Assuming that HD 179949b has a radius R_J < R_p < 1.2R_J, it mustrecirculate less than 21% of incident stellar energy to its night side at the1-sigma level (where 50% signifies full recirculation). If the planet has asmall Bond albedo, it must have a mass less than 2.4 M_J (1-sigma). We do notdetect phase variations for the other two systems but we do place the following2-sigma upper limits: 0.0007 for 51 Peg, and 0.0015 for HD 209458. Due to itsedge-on configuration, the upper limit for HD 209458 translates, withappropriate assumptions about Bond albedo, into a lower limit on therecirculation occuring in the planet's atmosphere. HD 209458b must recirculateat least 32% of incident stellar energy to its night side, at the 1-sigmalevel, which is consistent with other constraints on recirculation from thedepth of secondary eclipse depth at 8 micron and the low optical albedo. Thesedata indicate that different Hot Jupiter planets may experience differentrecirculation efficiencies.

text: Hot Jupiters, gas giant exoplanets orbiting very close to their host stars, experience extreme stellar irradiation leading to tidally locked rotation and significant day-night temperature contrasts. Mid-infrared observations are particularly effective for probing the thermal emission from these atmospheres, as they capture the planet's own radiated flux rather than reflected starlight. Phase variations in mid-infrared light curves reveal the longitudinal distribution of thermal emission as different hemispheres come into view over the orbital cycle. This study utilizes data from the Spitzer Space Telescope to measure mid-infrared phase curves for three hot Jupiter systems: HD 209458, HD 179949, and 51 Pegasi. Observations were conducted using the Infrared Array Camera (IRAC) in channels centered at 3.6 or 4.5 μm and 8 μm, covering eight orbital phases for each target. Precise relative photometry was achieved at 8 μm through calibration with standard stars, yielding uncertainties comparable to photon noise. A detectable phase variation was found at 8 μm for HD 179949b, with a peak-to-trough amplitude consistent with moderate day-night heat redistribution. Upper limits on phase amplitudes were established for the other systems, indicating varied efficiencies in atmospheric circulation among hot Jupiters. For HD 209458b, the constraints imply at least partial recirculation of incident energy to the nightside, aligning with prior eclipse depth and albedo measurements. These results demonstrate that hot Jupiters exhibit diverse mid-infrared phase behaviors, challenging uniform models of inefficient heat transport and highlighting the role of atmospheric dynamics in shaping observable thermal contrasts.

text: We describe a method to measure the magnetic field orientation of coronalmass ejections (CMEs) using Faraday rotation (FR). Two basic FR profiles,Gaussian-shaped with a single polarity or "N"-like with polarity reversals, areproduced by a radio source occulted by a moving flux rope depending on itsorientation. These curves are consistent with the Helios observations,providing evidence for the flux-rope geometry of CMEs. Many background radiosources can map CMEs in FR onto the sky. We demonstrate with a simple flux ropethat the magnetic field orientation and helicity of the flux rope can bedetermined 2-3 days before it reaches Earth, which is of crucial importance forspace weather forecasting. An FR calculation based on globalmagnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of CMEs in a background heliosphere showsthat FR mapping can also resolve a CME geometry curved back to the Sun. Wediscuss implementation of the method using data from the Mileura WidefieldArray (MWA).

text: Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are large-scale eruptions of magnetized plasma from the solar corona that significantly impact space weather through their potential to drive geomagnetic storms. Determining the internal magnetic field orientation of CMEs remotely is crucial for accurate forecasting of their geoeffectiveness, as the field configuration influences interaction with Earth's magnetosphere. This study presents a method to infer CME magnetic field orientation using Faraday rotation observations of background radio sources occulted by propagating CMEs. Faraday rotation arises from the line-of-sight integration of electron density and the parallel component of the magnetic field in the magnetized plasma. Modeling CMEs as magnetic flux ropes, we find that the temporal profile of Faraday rotation transients exhibits distinct signatures depending on the flux rope's axial field direction and helicity. Specifically, a Gaussian-shaped profile with single polarity indicates one orientation, while an N-shaped profile with polarity reversal corresponds to the opposite orientation.

text: The results of quantitative analysis of word distribution in two fables inUkrainian by Ivan Franko: "Mykyta the Fox" and "Abu-Kasym's slippers" arereported. Our study consists of two parts: the analysis of frequency-rankdistributions and the application of complex networks theory. The analysis offrequency-rank distributions shows that the text sizes are enough to observestatistical properties. The power-law character of these distributions (Zipf'slaw) holds in the region of rank variable r=20 - 3000 with an exponent$\alpha\simeq 1$. This substantiates the choice of the above texts to analysetypical properties of the language complex network on their basis. Besides, anapplicability of the Simon model to describe non-asymptotic properties of worddistributions is evaluated.  In describing language as a complex network, usually the words are associatedwith nodes, whereas one may give different meanings to the network links. Thisresults in different network representations. In the second part of the paper,we give different representations of the language network and performcomparative analysis of their characteristics. Our results demonstrate that thelanguage network of Ukrainian is a strongly correlated scale-free small world.Empirical data obtained may be useful for theoretical description of languageevolution.

text: This study investigates the application of complex network theory to quantify structural properties of the Ukrainian language through the analysis of Ivan Franko's fable *Mykyta the Fox*. The text, a satirical verse poem featuring the cunning fox Mykyta, serves as a representative sample of Ukrainian literary language due to its sufficient length and richness in vocabulary. Frequency-rank distributions of words in the fable are examined first, revealing adherence to Zipf's law with a power-law exponent approximately equal to 1 in the mid-rank range. This statistical regularity confirms the text's suitability for modeling broader linguistic patterns observed in natural languages. Complex networks are then constructed by representing words as nodes, with links defined through various criteria such as co-occurrence, syntactic dependencies, or adjacency in the narrative sequence. Multiple network representations are compared to assess robustness of topological features across different linking mechanisms. Key network metrics, including average degree, clustering coefficient, and average path length, are calculated for each representation. The resulting networks consistently exhibit small-world properties, characterized by high clustering and short path lengths relative to network size. Scale-free degree distributions are observed, indicating the presence of hub words that play central roles in connectivity.

text: In many applications it will be useful to know those patterns that occur witha balanced interval, e.g., a certain combination of phone numbers are calledalmost every Friday or a group of products are sold a lot on Tuesday andThursday.  In previous work we proposed a new measure of support (the number ofoccurrences of a pattern in a dataset), where we count the number of times apattern occurs (nearly) in the middle between two other occurrences. If thenumber of non-occurrences between two occurrences of a pattern stays almost thesame then we call the pattern balanced.  It was noticed that some very frequent patterns obviously also occur with abalanced interval, meaning in every transaction. However more interestingpatterns might occur, e.g., every three transactions. Here we discuss asolution using standard deviation and average. Furthermore we propose a simplerapproach for pruning patterns with a balanced interval, making estimating thepruning threshold more intuitive.

text: This paper introduces the concept of balanced patterns in transactional datasets, where patterns exhibit nearly constant intervals between successive occurrences, measured by the number of non-occurrences. Such patterns are particularly valuable in applications requiring the identification of regularly recurring events, such as periodic phone call combinations or recurring product purchases on specific days. Traditional frequent pattern mining often overlooks this temporal regularity, as highly frequent patterns may trivially appear balanced in every transaction. To address this, we build upon prior work that redefined support based on midpoint occurrences between pairs of pattern instances. Here, we formalize balanced intervals using statistical measures, specifically the average gap and standard deviation, to capture patterns recurring at approximate regularities, such as every few transactions. We propose an efficient pruning strategy that leverages intuitive thresholds on these measures, overcoming limitations in previous midpoint-based approaches.

text: The mysterious high galactic latitude cometary globule CG12 has been observedwith the ACIS detector on board the Chandra X-ray Observatory. We detect 128X-ray sources; half are likely young stars formed within the globule's head.This new population of >50 T-Tauri stars and one new embedded protostar is farlarger than the previously reported few intermediate-mass and two protostellarmembers of the cloud. Most of the newly discovered stars have masses 0.2-0.7Mo,and 9-15% have K-band excesses from inner protoplanetary disks. X-rayproperties provide an independent distance estimate consistent with CG12'sunusual location >200pc above the Galactic plane. The star formation efficiencyin CG12 appears to be 15-35%, far above that seen in other triggered molecularglobules. The median photometric age found for the T-Tauri population is ~4Myrwith a large spread of <1-20Myr and ongoing star formation in the molecularcores. The stellar age and spatial distributions are inconsistent with a simpleradiation driven implosion (RDI) model, and suggest either that CG12 is anatypically large shocked globule, or it has been subject to several distinctepisodes of triggering and ablation. We report a previously unnoticed group ofB-type stars northwest of CG12 which may be the remnants of an OB associationwhich produced multiple supernova explosions that could have shocked andablated the cloud over a 15-30Myr period. HD120958 (B3e), the most luminousmember of the group, may be currently driving an RDI shock into the CG12 cloud.

text: The cometary globule CG 12, located at a Galactic latitude of approximately +21° and more than 200 pc above the Galactic plane, represents an unusual site of ongoing low- to intermediate-mass star formation in relative isolation. Using the ACIS detector onboard the Chandra X-ray Observatory, this study detects 128 X-ray sources within the globule, with roughly half identified as young stars associated with the dense head of the cloud. This reveals a previously unrecognized substantial population of more than 50 T Tauri stars and one newly discovered embedded protostar, significantly exceeding the few intermediate-mass stars and two protostellar objects previously known. The majority of these young stellar objects have masses in the range of 0.2–0.7 M⊙, and 9%–15% exhibit K-band excesses indicative of inner protoplanetary disks. X-ray properties provide an independent distance confirmation consistent with the cloud's high-latitude position, estimated around 550–630 pc. The star formation efficiency in CG 12 is remarkably high, ranging from 15% to 35%, far surpassing values typical of other triggered molecular globules. Photometric ages derived using Siess et al. (2000) isochrones yield a median of approximately 4 Myr for the T Tauri population, with a broad spread from less than 1 Myr to 20 Myr and evidence of ongoing star formation within the molecular cores. The spatial distribution and age structure of the young stars are inconsistent with a simple radiation-driven implosion (RDI) model, suggesting instead that CG 12 may represent an atypically large shocked globule or one influenced by multiple distinct episodes of triggering and ablation.

text: (Conext:) Surveys of Wolf-Rayet (WR) populations in nearby galaxies providetests of evolutionary models plus Type Ib/c supernova progenitors. Thisspectroscopic study complements the recent imaging survey of the spiral galaxyNGC 300 by Schild et al. (Aims): Revisions to the known WR content of NGC 300are presented. We investigate the WR nature of candidate #41 from Schild et al.which is spatially coincident with the bright X-ray point source NGC 300 X-1;(Methods:) VLT/FORS2 multi-object spectroscopy of WR candidates in NGC 300 isobtained; (Results:) We establish an early-type WN nature of #41, i.e. similarto the optical counterpart of IC 10 X-1, which closely resembles NGC 300 X-1.We confirm 9 new WR stars, bringing the current WR census of the inner disk to31, with N(WC)/N(WN)~0.9. (Conclusions:) If #41 is the optical counterpart forNGC 300 X-1, we estimate a WR mass of 38 Msun based upon ground-basedphotometry, from which a black hole mass of > 10 Msun results from the 32.8 hrperiod of the system and WR wind velocity of 1250 km/s. We estimate an 95%completeness among WC stars and 70% among WN stars, such that the total WRcontent is ~40, with N(WC)/N(WN)~0.7. From the Halpha-derived star formationrate of the inner galaxy, we infer N(WR)/N(O)~0.04
