text: Accurate estimation of residual life, also known as remaining useful life (RUL), is essential for effective prognostics and health management (PHM) in machines and components, enabling predictive maintenance and reducing unplanned downtime. Traditional methods often rely on physical models or statistical approaches, which require detailed prior knowledge of degradation processes and may struggle with complex, nonlinear dynamics. This study explores the application of neural networks as a data-driven alternative for RUL prediction, leveraging their ability to learn intricate patterns from historical and condition-monitoring data. Various neural network architectures, including multi-layer perceptrons and recurrent variants, were employed to model degradation trajectories. The investigation incorporated two distinct reliability datasets: one simulating renewal processes and another involving repaired systems with vibration-based condition monitoring. Models were trained using age and, in enhanced variants, additional condition-monitoring features to assess their impact on predictive accuracy. Results demonstrated high precision in the simulated renewal case, with average prediction errors ranging from hundreds of seconds across network types. Incorporating condition-monitoring data significantly improved RUL estimates in the repaired system dataset, highlighting the value of real-time sensor inputs.
label: llm

text: We investigate the action of local unitary operations on multimode (pure ormixed) Gaussian states and single out the minimal number of locally invariantparametres which completely characterise the covariance matrix of such states.For pure Gaussian states, central resources for continuous-variable quantuminformation, we investigate separately the parametre reduction due to theadditional constraint of global purity, and the one following by thelocal-unitary freedom. Counting arguments and insights from the phase-spaceSchmidt decomposition and in general from the framework of symplectic analysis,accompany our description of the standard form of pure n-mode Gaussian states.In particular we clarify why only in pure states with n<=3 modes all the directcorrelations between position and momentum operators can be set to zero bylocal unitary operations. For any n, the emerging minimal set of parametrescontains complete information about all forms of entanglement in thecorresponding states. An efficient state engineering scheme (able to encodedirect correlations between position and momentum operators as well) isproposed to produce entangled multimode Gaussian resources, its number ofoptical elements matching the minimal number of locally invariant degrees offreedom of general pure n-mode Gaussian states. We demonstrate that so-called"block-diagonal" Gaussian states, without direct correlations between positionand momentum, are systematically less entangled, on average, than arbitrarypure Gaussian states.
label: human

text: Multimode Gaussian states of continuous-variable quantum systems are characterized by their covariance matrices, which can be transformed into canonical standard forms through local symplectic operations that preserve entanglement structures. These standard forms reveal the minimal set of locally invariant parameters that fully classify the states up to local unitaries. By exploiting these invariants, we demonstrate that arbitrary multimode Gaussian states can be efficiently engineered from simple seed states using only local Gaussian operations, minimizing the required resources. This approach enables precise control over multipartite entanglement distribution across modes. The results provide an optimal protocol for generating tailored entangled Gaussian resources in quantum information processing tasks.
label: llm

text: We study two recently proposed equations of state (EOS) which are obtainedfrom high temperature QCD, and show how they can be adapted to use them formaking predictions for relativistic heavy ion collisions. The method involvesextracting equilibrium distribution functions for quarks and gluons from theEOS, which in turn will allow a determination of the transport and other bulkproperties of the quark gluon plasma. Simultaneously, the method also yields aquasi particle description of interacting quarks and gluons. The first EOS isperturbative in the QCD coupling constant and has contributions of $O(g^5)$.The second EOS is an improvement over the first, with contributions upto $O(g^6 ln(\frac{1}{g}))$; it incorporates the nonperturbative hard thermalcontributions. The interaction effects are shown to be captured entirely by theeffective chemical potentials for the gluons and the quarks, in both the cases.The chemical potential is seen to be highly sensitive to the EOS. As anapplication, we determine the screening lengths which are, indeed the mostimportant diagnostics for QGP. The screening lengths are seen to behavedrastically differently depending on the EOS considered., and yield, therefore,a way to distinguish the two equations of state in heavy ion collisions.
label: human

text: Relativistic heavy-ion collisions at facilities like RHIC and LHC create extreme conditions of high temperature and energy density, enabling the production of quark-gluon plasma (QGP), a deconfined state of QCD matter. The equation of state (EOS) of hot QCD matter, primarily derived from lattice QCD calculations at vanishing baryon chemical potential, relates pressure, energy density, and temperature in this regime. These EOS parameterizations exhibit a smooth crossover transition rather than a sharp phase change, influencing the hydrodynamic expansion of the fireball. Viscous hydrodynamic models, incorporating lattice-based EOS, successfully describe collective flow observables such as elliptic and higher-order harmonic flows in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in lattice EOS from various collaborations (e.g., HotQCD and Wuppertal-Budapest) lead to quantifiable variations in predicted particle spectra and flow coefficients when implemented in hybrid simulations coupling hydrodynamics to hadronic transport. Transport properties, including shear viscosity over entropy ratio, are constrained by comparing model predictions to experimental data on hadron yields and momentum distributions. The sensitivity of screening lengths and other QGP diagnostics to the underlying EOS provides a pathway to distinguish competing theoretical descriptions in collision experiments.
label: llm

text: A dilatation structure on a metric space, arXiv:math/0608536v4, is a notionin between a group and a differential structure, accounting for the approximateself-similarity of the metric space.  The basic objects of a dilatation structure are dilatations (orcontractions). The axioms of a dilatation structure set the rules ofinteraction between different dilatations.  Linearity is also a property which can be explained with the help of adilatation structure. In this paper we show that we can speak about two kindsof linearity: the linearity of a function between two dilatation structures andthe linearity of the dilatation structure itself.  Our main result here is a characterization of contractible groups in terms ofdilatation structures. To a normed conical group (normed contractible group) wecan naturally associate a linear dilatation structure. Conversely, any linearand strong dilatation structure comes from the dilatation structure of a normedcontractible group.
label: human

text: A dilatation structure on a metric space provides a framework intermediate between a group operation and a differential structure, capturing approximate self-similarity through the use of dilatations or contractions. The axioms governing these dilatations dictate their interactions, enabling notions of linearity to be defined within this context. This paper distinguishes between two forms of linearity: that of functions mapping between dilatation structures and that inherent to the dilatation structure itself. To a normed conical group, or specifically a normed contractible group, one can naturally associate a linear dilatation structure. Conversely, every linear and strong dilatation structure arises from the dilatation structure of a normed contractible group. The principal contribution is a precise characterization of contractible groups via their associated dilatation structures. This equivalence highlights the role of linearity in bridging algebraic and metric properties.
label: llm

text: We present a general scheme for multiparty-controlled teleportation of anarbitrary m-qudit ($d$-dimensional quantum system) state by using non-maximallyentangled states as the quantum channel. The sender performs m generalizedBell-state measurements on her 2$m$ particles, the controllers take somesingle-particle measurements with the measuring basis $X_{d}$ and the receiveronly need to introduce one auxiliary two-level particle to extract quantuminformation probabilistically with the fidelity unit if he cooperates with allthe controllers. All the parties can use some decoy photons to set up theirquantum channel securely, which will forbid some a dishonest party to eavesdropfreely. This scheme is optimal as the probability that the receiver obtains theoriginally unknown m-qudit state equals to the entanglement of the quantumchannel.
label: human

text: We propose a general protocol for multiparty-controlled teleportation of an arbitrary m-qudit state in a d-dimensional Hilbert space, utilizing a pure entangled quantum channel consisting of multiple non-maximally entangled multi-particle states. The sender performs generalized Bell-state measurements on the particles holding the unknown state and her share of the channel, while each controller executes single-particle measurements in the X_d basis. With the cooperation of all controllers, the receiver introduces a single auxiliary qubit and applies appropriate unitary operations to reconstruct the original m-qudit state probabilistically with unit fidelity. This scheme is optimal, as the success probability directly corresponds to the degree of entanglement in the pure channel states.
label: llm

text: We consider a $SO(d)$ gauge theory in an Euclidean $d$-dimensionalspace-time, which is known to be renormalizable to all orders in perturbationtheory for $2\le{d}\le4$. Then, with the help of a space-time representation ofthe gauge group, the gauge theory is mapped into a curved space-time withlinear connection. Further, in that mapping the gauge field plays the role ofthe linear connection of the curved space-time and an effective metric tensorarises naturally from the mapping. The obtained action, being quadratic in theRiemann-Christoffel tensor, at a first sight, spoils a gravity interpretationof the model. Thus, we provide a sketch of a mechanism that breaks the $SO(d)$color invariance and generates the Einstein-Hilbert term, as well as acosmological constant term, allowing an interpretation of the model as amodified gravity in the Palatini formalism. In that sense, gravity can bevisualized as an effective classical theory, originated from a well definedquantum gauge theory. We also show that, in the four dimensional case, twopossibilities for particular solutions of the field equations are the de Sitterand Anti de Sitter space-times.
label: human

text: We propose a framework in which gravity emerges as an effective theory from a renormalizable SO(d) quantum gauge theory formulated in Euclidean d-dimensional spacetime for 2 ≤ d ≤ 4. By employing a spacetime representation of the gauge group, the pure Yang-Mills gauge field is mapped to a linear connection on a curved manifold. In this mapping, the gauge field naturally assumes the role of the affine connection, while an effective metric tensor arises from the structure of the representation. The resulting effective action includes terms resembling the Einstein-Hilbert action in the Palatini formalism, supplemented by a cosmological constant. This demonstrates that classical gravity can be viewed as an emergent phenomenon originating from a well-defined, perturbatively renormalizable quantum gauge theory. For the physically relevant case of d=4, solutions to the effective field equations include de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes. The approach highlights a potential pathway toward reconciling quantum field theory principles with general relativity through gauge-theoretic origins in Euclidean signature.
label: llm

text: Revised Hipparcos parallaxes for classical Cepheids are analysed togetherwith 10 HST-based parallaxes (Benedict et al.). In a reddening-free V,Irelation we find that the coefficient of logP is the same within theuncertainties in our Galaxy as in the LMC, contrary to some previoussuggestions. Cepheids in the inner region of NGC4258 with near solarmetallicities (Macri et al.) confirm this result. We obtain a zero-point forthe reddening-free relation and apply it to Cepheids in galaxies used bySandage et al. to calibrate the absolute magnitudes of SNIa and to derive theHubble constant. We revise their result from 62 to 70+/-5 km/s/Mpc. TheFreedman et al. 2001 value is revised from 72 to 76+/-8 km/s/Mpc. These resultsare insensitive to Cepheid metallicity corrections. The Cepheids in the innerregion of NGC4258 yield a modulus of 29.22+/-0.03(int) compared with amaser-based modulus of 29.29+/-0.15. Distance moduli for the LMC, uncorrectedfor any metallicity effects, are; 18.52+/-0.03 from a reddening-free relationin V,I; 18.47+/-0.03 from a period-luminosity relation at K; 18.45+/-0.04 froma period-luminosity-colour relation in J,K. Adopting a metallicity correctionin V,I from Marci et al. leads to a true LMC modulus of 18.39+/-0.05.
label: human

text: Cepheid variables serve as fundamental standard candles for measuring cosmic distances due to their well-established period-luminosity relation. Precise trigonometric parallaxes to Galactic Cepheids provide a geometric calibration of this relation, independent of secondary anchors. Advances in space-based astrometry, including data from Hipparcos, Hubble Space Telescope, and Gaia missions, have significantly improved parallax measurements for nearby Cepheids. These parallaxes allow direct determination of absolute magnitudes, reducing systematic uncertainties in the Cepheid distance scale. The calibrated period-luminosity relation is then applied to extragalactic Cepheids in hosts of Type Ia supernovae, forming the basis of the cosmic distance ladder. This ladder extends to the Hubble flow, enabling an independent measurement of the Hubble constant, H₀. Recent analyses incorporating Gaia Early Data Release 3 parallaxes for dozens of Milky Way Cepheids yield a highly precise geometric calibration. Consistency checks with independent anchors, such as masers in NGC 4258 and detached eclipsing binaries in the Large Magellanic Cloud, support the robustness of this approach. Metallicity effects on the period-luminosity relation appear minimal when using reddening-free Wesenheit magnitudes.
label: llm

text: A synfire chain is a simple neural network model which can propagate stablesynchronous spikes called a pulse packet and widely researched. However howsynfire chains coexist in one network remains to be elucidated. We have studiedthe activity of a layered associative network of Leaky Integrate-and-Fireneurons in which connection we embed memory patterns by the Hebbian Learning.We analyzed their activity by the Fokker-Planck method. In our previous report,when a half of neurons belongs to each memory pattern (memory pattern rate$F=0.5$), the temporal profiles of the network activity is split intotemporally clustered groups called sublattices under certain input conditions.In this study, we show that when the network is sparsely connected ($F<0.5$),synchronous firings of the memory pattern are promoted. On the contrary, thedensely connected network ($F>0.5$) inhibit synchronous firings. The sparsenessand denseness also effect the basin of attraction and the storage capacity ofthe embedded memory patterns. We show that the sparsely(densely) connectednetworks enlarge(shrink) the basion of attraction and increase(decrease) thestorage capacity.
label: human

text: This study investigates the dynamics of sparse and dense encoding in a layered associative network composed of leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neurons, where memory patterns are embedded via Hebbian learning. Synfire chains, which propagate stable synchronous pulse packets, serve as a foundational model, but their coexistence in a shared network remains challenging. The network architecture supports multiple embedded memory patterns, with the memory pattern rate \(F\) determining the overlap between patterns. When \(F = 0.5\), network activity splits into temporally clustered sublattices under specific input conditions. In contrast, sparse encoding (\(F < 0.5\)) promotes synchronous firing within individual memory patterns, enhancing stable propagation. Conversely, dense encoding (\(F > 0.5\)) reduces synchrony and fragments activity. These findings demonstrate that sparse representations enlarge the basin of attraction for retrieval while increasing storage capacity, offering insights into efficient neural coding mechanisms relevant to biological and neuromorphic systems.
label: llm

text: We analyzed the presently available experimental data on nucleonelectromagnetic form factors within a multipole model based on dispersionrelations. A good fit of the data is achieved by considering the coefficientsof the multipole expansions as logarithmic functions of the momentum transfersquared. The superconvergence relations, applied to this coefficients, makesthe model agree with unitary constraints and pQCD asymptotics for the Dirac andPauli form factors. The soft photon emission is proposed as a mechanismresponsible for the difference between the Rosenbluth, polarization andbeam--target--asymmetry data. It is shown, that the experimentally measuredcross sections depend not only on the Dirac and Pauli form factors, but also onthe average number of the photons emitted. For proton this number is shown tobe different for different types of experimental measurements and thenestimated phenomenologically. For neutron the same mechanism predicts, that thedata form different types of experiments must coincide with high accuracy. Ajoint fit of all the experimental data reproduce the $Q^2-$dependence with theaccuracy $\chi^2/dof=0.86$. Predictions of the model, that 1) the ratios of theproton form factors $G_E/G_M$ are different for Rosenbluth, polarization andbeam--target--asymmetry experiments and 2) similar ratios are nearly the samefor neutron, can be used for experimental verification of the model.
label: human

text: The multipole model provides a phenomenological framework for describing the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon by expanding the charge and magnetization distributions in terms of multipole moments. This approach effectively parametrizes the spatial extension and internal structure probed in electron-nucleon scattering experiments. In this work, we extend the standard multipole ansatz to incorporate logarithmic corrections arising from perturbative QCD effects at intermediate momentum transfers. These corrections manifest as subleading terms that modify the asymptotic fall-off of the form factors beyond the leading dipole behavior. Soft photon phenomenology, particularly in processes involving low-energy photon emission such as nucleon-nucleon bremsstrahlung, offers a complementary probe of the nucleon's electromagnetic structure. We demonstrate that the multipole expansion naturally accommodates contributions from soft photon theorems, linking the off-shell form factors to on-shell elastic amplitudes. The inclusion of logarithmic terms improves agreement with precision data on the proton and neutron Sachs form factors across a wide range of \(Q^2\). Furthermore, these corrections influence the extraction of nucleon radii and provide insights into two-photon exchange effects in parity-violating scattering. Our analysis reveals that soft photon resummation in the multipole framework yields predictions consistent with recent dispersive evaluations and lattice QCD extrapolations.
label: llm

text: Although one-time pad encrypted files can be sent through Internet channels,the need for renewing shared secret keys have made this method unpractical.This work presents a scheme to turn practical the fast sharing of random keysover arbitrary Internet channels. Starting with a shared secret key sequence oflength K_0 the users end up with a secure new sequence K >> K_0. Using thesesequences for posteriori message encryption the legitimate users have absolutesecurity control without the need for third parties. Additionally, the securitylevel does not depend on the unproven difficulty of factoring numbers inprimes. In the proposed scheme a fast optical random source generates randombits and noise for key renewals. The transmitted signals are recorded signalsthat carries both the random binary signals to be exchanged and physical noisethat cannot be eliminated by the attacker. These signals allow amplificationover the Internet network without degrading security. The proposed system isalso secure against a-posteriori known-plaintext attack on the key.Information-theoretic analysis is presented and bounds for secure operation arequantitatively determined.
label: human

text: The secure sharing of random bits over insecure Internet channels poses a significant challenge for cryptographic applications requiring fresh randomness, such as one-time pad encryption. Traditional one-time pad systems offer information-theoretic security but are impractical due to the difficulty of securely distributing and renewing long shared secret keys over public networks. This paper introduces a novel protocol that enables two parties to securely expand a short initial shared secret into arbitrarily long sequences of shared random bits. The method leverages physical noise inherent in signal generation to mask the transmitted information. Specifically, one party generates random bits using a fast optical source and records signals that combine the desired random bits with irreducible physical noise. These deterministic yet noise-perturbed signals are transmitted over standard Internet channels. The receiving party, possessing the initial shared secret, can extract the embedded random bits while the noise prevents an eavesdropper from doing so. The protocol supports signal amplification without compromising security, making it suitable for long-distance communication.
label: llm

text: Thirty years of a deepening information paradox suggest the need to reviseour basic physical framework. Multiple indicators point toward reassessment ofthe principle of locality: lack of a precise definition in quantum gravity,behavior of high-energy scattering, hints from strings and AdS/CFT, conundrumsof quantum cosmology, and finally lack of good alternative resolutions of theparadox. A plausible conjecture states that the non-perturbative dynamics ofgravity is unitary but nonlocal. String theory may directly address theseissues but so far important aspects remain elusive. If this viewpoint iscorrect, critical questions are to understand the "correspondence" limit wherenonlocal physics reduces to local quantum field theory, and beyond, to unveilprinciples of an underlying nonlocal theory.
label: human

text: Abstract The black hole information paradox, persisting for over three decades, poses a profound challenge to the consistency of quantum mechanics and general relativity, suggesting that unitary evolution may be violated during black hole evaporation. Multiple lines of evidence—including the absence of a precise notion of locality in quantum gravity, the behavior of high-energy scattering amplitudes, insights from string theory and the AdS/CFT correspondence, and unresolved issues in quantum cosmology—indicate that the conventional principle of locality must be reconsidered. A plausible resolution proposes that the fundamental dynamics of quantum gravity are unitary but inherently nonlocal, allowing information to escape black holes without violating core quantum principles. String theory provides partial support for such a picture, although key details remain elusive.
label: llm

text: Let P(z) and Q(y) be polynomials of the same degree k>=1 in the complexvariables z and y, respectively. In this extended abstract we study thenon-linear functional equation P(z)=Q(y(z)), where y(z) is restricted to beanalytic in a neighborhood of z=0. We provide sufficient conditions to ensurethat all the roots of Q(y) are contained within the range of y(z) as well as tohave y(z)=z as the unique analytic solution of the non-linear equation. Ourresults are motivated from uniqueness considerations of polynomial canonicalrepresentations of the phase or amplitude terms of oscillatory integralsencountered in the asymptotic analysis of the coefficients of mixed powers andmultivariable generating functions via saddle-point methods. Uniqueness shallprove important for developing algorithms to determine the Taylor coefficientsof the terms appearing in these representations. The uniqueness of Levinson'spolynomial canonical representations of analytic functions in several variablesfollows as a corollary of our one-complex variables results.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the uniqueness of polynomial canonical representations used in the asymptotic analysis of oscillatory integrals arising from multivariable generating functions and mixed powers coefficients via saddle-point methods. We consider polynomials P(z) and Q(y) of the same degree k ≥ 1 over the complex numbers and analyze the nonlinear functional equation P(z) = Q(y(z)), where y(z) is analytic near z = 0. Sufficient conditions are established to ensure that the range of y(z) contains all roots of Q(y). These conditions further guarantee that y(z) = z is the unique analytic solution in a neighborhood of the origin. The results enable the development of algorithms for computing Taylor coefficients in such representations. As a key corollary, the uniqueness of Levinson's polynomial canonical representations for analytic functions in several variables is derived from the one-variable case.
label: llm

text: The Cosmic Far-Infrared Background (CFIRB) contains information about thenumber and distribution of contributing sources and thus gives us an importantkey to understand the evolution of galaxies. Using a confusion study to set afundamental limit to the observations, we investigate the potential to explorethe CFIRB with AKARI/FIS deep observations. The Far-Infrared Surveyor (FIS) isone of the focal-plane instruments on the AKARI (formerly known as ASTRO-F)satellite, which was launched in early 2006. Based upon source distributionmodels assuming three different cosmological evolutionary scenarios (noevolution, weak evolution, and strong evolution), an extensive model fordiffuse emission from infrared cirrus, and instrumental noise estimates, wepresent a comprehensive analysis for the determination of the confusion levelsfor deep far-infrared observations. We use our derived sensitivities to suggestthe best observational strategy for the AKARI/FIS mission to detect the CFIRBfluctuations. If the source distribution follows the evolutionary models,observations will be mostly limited by source confusion. We find that we willbe able to detect the CFIRB fluctuations and that these will in turn provideinformation to discriminate between the evolutionary scenarios of galaxies inmost low-to-medium cirrus regions.
label: human

text: The Cosmic Far-Infrared Background (CFIRB) encodes valuable information on the number density and distribution of distant infrared galaxies, providing key insights into their cosmological evolution. This study employs confusion analysis to assess the feasibility of detecting CFIRB fluctuations using deep far-infrared observations with the Far-Infrared Surveyor (FIS) aboard the AKARI satellite. We incorporate source distribution models based on three distinct evolutionary scenarios—no evolution, weak evolution, and strong evolution—for extragalactic populations. An extensive modeling of diffuse Galactic cirrus emission is combined with estimates of instrumental noise to determine confusion limits in the FIS bands. Sensitivity calculations reveal that source confusion dominates over instrumental noise in evolutionary models, particularly at longer wavelengths. Our analysis demonstrates that AKARI/FIS deep observations can reliably detect CFIRB fluctuations in regions of low to medium cirrus contamination. These detections are expected to discriminate between competing galaxy evolution models, offering constraints on infrared galaxy formation and clustering at high redshifts.
label: llm

text: Observations by the Cores to Disk Legacy Team with the Spitzer SpaceTelescope have identified a low luminosity, mid-infrared source within thedense core, Lynds 1014, which was previously thought to harbor no internalsource. Followup near-infrared and submillimeter interferometric observationshave confirmed the protostellar nature of this source by detecting scatteredlight from an outflow cavity and a weak molecular outflow. In this paper, wereport the detection of cm continuum emission with the VLA. The emission ischaracterized by a quiescent, unresolved 90 uJy 6 cm source within 0.2" of theSpitzer source. The spectral index of the quiescent component is $\alpha =0.37\pm 0.34$ between 6 cm and 3.6 cm. A factor of two increase in 6 cmemission was detected during one epoch and circular polarization was marginallydetected at the $5\sigma$ level with Stokes {V/I} $= 48 \pm 16$% . We havesearched for 22 GHz H2O maser emission toward L1014-IRS, but no masers weredetected during 7 epochs of observations between June 2004 and December 2006.L1014-IRS appears to be a low-mass, accreting protostar which exhibits cmemission from a thermal jet or a wind, with a variable non-thermal emissioncomponent. The quiescent cm radio emission is noticeably above the correlationof 3.6 cm and 6 cm luminosity versus bolometric luminosity, indicating moreradio emission than expected. We characterize the cm continuum emission interms of observations of other low-mass protostars, including updatedcorrelations of centimeter continuum emission with bolometric luminosity andoutflow force, and discuss the implications of recent larger distance estimateson the physical attributes of the protostar and dense molecular core.
label: human

text: The dense core Lynds 1014 was previously considered starless until Spitzer observations revealed an embedded low-luminosity infrared source, designated L1014-IRS. Multi-epoch Very Large Array observations detected weak centimeter-wavelength radio continuum emission coincident with L1014-IRS, confirming its protostellar nature. The source exhibits flux densities at 3.6 cm and 6 cm that place its quiescent radio luminosity significantly above established correlations with bolometric luminosity for other low-mass protostars. Variability was observed, including a factor of ~2 increase in 6 cm flux during one epoch and marginal detection of circular polarization, suggesting a variable nonthermal component. The spectral properties and polarization indicate that the radio emission arises primarily from a thermal jet or ionized wind, superimposed with nonthermal processes likely related to magnetic activity. No 22 GHz water maser emission was detected across multiple epochs, consistent with the low luminosity and early evolutionary stage of the protostar. Comparisons with centimeter emission from other low-mass protostars reveal updated trends in radio luminosity versus bolometric luminosity and outflow force. These characteristics support L1014-IRS as a very low-mass accreting protostar driving a compact outflow. Recent distance revisions to the core imply adjustments to the derived physical parameters, including potentially higher mass and luminosity for the embedded source.
label: llm

text: Tables of mean opacities are often used to compute the transfer of radiationin a variety of astrophysical simulations from stellar evolution models toproto-planetary disks. Often tables, such as Ferguson et al. (2005), arecomputed with a predetermined set of physical assumptions that may or may notbe valid for a specific application. This paper explores the effects of severalassumptions of grain physics on the Rosseland mean opacity in an oxygen richenvironment. We find that changing the distribution of grain sizes, either thepower-law exponent or the shape of the distribution, has a marginal effect onthe total mean opacity. We also explore the difference in the mean opacitybetween solid homogenous grains and grains that are porous or conglomorationsof several species. Changing the amount of grain opacity included in the meanby assuming a grain-to-gas ratio significantly affects the mean opacity, but ina predictable way.
label: human

text: Tables of Rosseland mean opacities are widely employed in radiative transfer calculations for astrophysical models, ranging from stellar interiors to protoplanetary disks. Precomputed opacity tables often rely on fixed assumptions about grain physics that may not hold across all environments. This study investigates the impact of various grain physics parameters on the Rosseland mean opacity in oxygen-rich conditions. Variations in the grain size distribution, including the power-law exponent and overall shape, are found to have only marginal effects on the total mean opacity. Differences between homogeneous solid grains and porous or composite grains also yield relatively small changes in opacity. In contrast, altering the grain-to-gas mass ratio significantly modifies the mean opacity in a systematic and predictable manner. These findings highlight the sensitivity of low-temperature opacities to dust depletion or enrichment scenarios in astrophysical contexts.
label: llm

text: We consider constraints on the planetesimal population residing in the disksof AU Microscopii, Beta Pictoris and Fomalhaut taking into account theirobserved thicknesses and normal disk opacities. We estimate that bodies ofradius 5, 180 and 70 km are responsible for initiating the collisional cascadeaccounting for the dust production for AU-Mic, Beta-Pic and Fomalhaut's disks,respectively, at break radii from the star where their surface brightnessprofiles change slope. Larger bodies, of radius 1000km and with surface densityof order 0.01 g/cm^2, are required to explain the thickness of these disksassuming that they are heated by gravitational stirring. A comparison betweenthe densities of the two sizes suggests the size distribution in the largestbodies is flatter than that observed in the Kuiper belt. AU Mic's disk requiresthe shallowest size distribution for bodies with radius greater than 10kmsuggesting that the disk contains planetary embryos experiencing a stage ofrunaway growth.
label: human

text: Thin debris disks around young stars, such as those observed in AU Microscopii, β Pictoris, and Fomalhaut, exhibit small vertical scale heights that imply low velocity dispersions among the smallest dust particles. These low dispersions are attributed to gravitational stirring by larger unseen bodies within the disks, as collisional processes alone cannot maintain the observed thinness over dynamical timescales. By modeling the equilibrium between stirring and damping, constraints are placed on the size distribution and masses of the underlying planetesimal population. The analysis indicates that bodies with radii up to approximately 1000 km—corresponding to planetary embryos—are required to explain the observed disk thicknesses. In particular, the exceptionally thin disk of AU Microscopii suggests a size distribution consistent with ongoing runaway growth among these embryos.
label: llm

text: We are given three strings s, t, and t' of length L over some fixed finitealphabet and an integer m that is polylogarithmic in L. We have a symmetricrelation on substrings of constant length that specifies which substrings areallowed to be replaced with each other. Let Delta(n) denote the differencebetween the numbers of possibilities to obtain t from s and t' from s after nreplacements. The problem is to determine the sign of Delta(m).  As promises we have a gap condition and a growth condition. The former statesthat |Delta(m)| >= epsilon c^m where epsilon is inverse polylogarithmic in Land c>0 is a constant. The latter is given by Delta(n) <= c^n for all n.  We show that this problem is PromiseBQP-complete, i.e., it represents theclass of problems which can be solved efficiently on a quantum computer.
label: human

text: We present a promise problem involving string rewriting systems that captures the full power of quantum polynomial-time computation. Given three strings \(s\), \(t\), and \(t'\) of length \(L\) over a fixed finite alphabet, an integer \(m\) polylogarithmic in \(L\), and a symmetric relation specifying allowed replacements between constant-length substrings, the task is to determine the sign of \(\Delta(m)\). Here, \(\Delta(n)\) denotes the difference between the number of ways to rewrite \(s\) into \(t\) and into \(t'\) after exactly \(n\) replacements. The input satisfies two promises: a gap condition ensuring \(|\Delta(m)| \geq \epsilon c^m\) for some inverse-polylogarithmic \(\epsilon\) in \(L\) and constant \(c > 0\), and a growth condition bounding \(|\Delta(n)| \leq c^n\) for all \(n\). This problem lies in PromiseBQP.
label: llm

text: In this paper we first construct a mathematical model for the Universeexpansion that started up with the original Big Bang. Next, we discuss theproblematic of the mechanical and physical laws invariance regarding thespatial frame exchanges. We then prove the (theoretical) existence of avariable metric $g_t$, depending on time and satisfying to a simplifiedEinstein equation, so that all free ordinary trajectories are geodesics. Thisis done by considering the classical Galileo-Newtonian space and time relation,by using generalized Newtonian principles and adding the approved physical newones (as covariance principle, Mach principle, the Einstein equivalenceprinciple ...) in order to establish a new cosmological model of the dynamicalUniverse as being $(U(t))_{t\geq 0}=(B_e(O,t),g_t)_{t\geq 0}$, where $B_e(O,t)$is the Euclidean ball of radius $t$ in $\mathbb R^3$. The cosmological metric$g_t$ is totally determined, at time $t$, by the mass energy distribution$E_t(X)$ on $B_e(O,t)$. We study also the black holes phenomenon and we provethat the total and global cosmological energy distribution $E_t(X)$ satisfiesto the wave equation whose solutions are characterized by pseudo-frequenciesdepending on time and related to the spectrum of the Dirichlet problem on theunit ball $B_e(O,1)$ for the Laplace-Beltrami operator -$\Delta$. Our model isconsistent in the sense that all Newtonian and classical physical laws arevalid as particular cases in classical situations. Then, we show that all basicresults of Modern Physics are still valid without using the second postulate ofspecial relativity nor the uncertainty principle.
label: human

text: L'expansion de l'Univers, découverte au début du XXe siècle, pose des défis fondamentaux liés à la conservation et à la nature de l'énergie en cosmologie relativiste. Dans un univers en expansion, la symétrie temporelle est brisée, entraînant une non-conservation de l'énergie totale au sens classique. Ce phénomène se manifeste particulièrement par la perte d'énergie des photons due au décalage vers le rouge cosmologique. Les observations indiquent que l'expansion s'accélère depuis environ cinq milliards d'années, impliquant l'existence d'une énergie répulsive dominante. Cette énergie sombre, représentant environ 70 % du contenu énergétique de l'Univers, défie les prédictions de la théorie quantique des champs pour la constante cosmologique. Des modèles alternatifs proposent une métrique variable dépendant du temps pour rendre les trajectoires géodésiques tout en respectant les principes de covariance et d'équivalence. De récentes données suggèrent que l'énergie sombre pourrait évoluer, remettant en question sa constance et ouvrant la voie à de nouveaux scénarios cosmologiques. Ces problèmes d'énergie soulignent la nécessité de réconcilier relativité générale et mécanique quantique dans un cadre unifié.
label: llm

text: The space velocity of a stellar black hole encodes the history of itsformation and evolution. Here we measure the 3-dimensional motion of themicroquasar GRS 1915+105, using a decade of astrometry with the NRAO Very LongBaseline Array, together with the published radial velocity. The velocity inthe Galactic Plane deviates from circular rotation by 53-80 +_ 8 km/s, wherethe range covers any specific distance from 6-12 kpc. Perpendicular to theplane, the velocity is only 10 +_ 4 km/s. The peculiar velocity is minimized ata distance 9-10 kpc, and is then nearly in the radial direction towards theGalactic Center. We discuss mechanisms for the origin of the peculiar velocity,and conclude that it is most likely a consequence of Galactic velocitydiffusion on this old binary, rather than the result of a supernova kick duringthe formation of the 14 Mo black hole. Finally, a brief comparison is made with4 other BH binaries whose kinematics are well determined.
label: human

text: The space velocity of a stellar-mass black hole provides crucial insights into its formation and evolutionary history. This study presents a precise measurement of the three-dimensional kinematics of the microquasar GRS 1915+105, a prominent black hole X-ray binary. We utilize over a decade of high-resolution astrometric observations from the NRAO Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA). These data yield accurate proper motions of the system's compact relativistic jets. Combined with previously published radial velocity measurements, we derive the full space motion of the binary. The resulting peculiar velocity is found to be modest relative to the Galactic disk population. This suggests minimal natal kick during the black hole's formation. Analysis of possible origins indicates that the observed velocity likely arises from gradual Galactic velocity diffusion over the system's age, rather than a significant supernova asymmetry. Comparisons with kinematics of other well-studied black hole binaries reveal diverse velocity distributions, highlighting varied formation channels.
label: llm

text: A DC electrical current is injected through a chain of metallic beads. Theelectrical resistances of each bead-bead contacts are measured. At low current,the distribution of these resistances is large and log-normal. At high enoughcurrent, the resistance distribution becomes sharp and Gaussian due to thecreation of microweldings between some beads. The action of nearbyelectromagnetic waves (sparks) on the electrical conductivity of the chain isalso studied. The spark effect is to lower the resistance values of the moreresistive contacts, the best conductive ones remaining unaffected by the sparkproduction. The spark is able to induce through the chain a current enough tocreate microweldings between some beads. This explains why the electricalresistance of a granular medium is so sensitive to the electromagnetic wavesproduced in its vicinity.
label: human

text: The electrical conductivity of granular metallic media is highly sensitive to intergranular contacts, which often exhibit heterogeneous resistance due to surface oxides and imperfect mechanical junctions. In this study, a model system consisting of a chain of metallic beads is employed to investigate the individual resistance of bead-to-bead contacts under varying current levels. At low applied currents, the distribution of contact resistances is broad and follows a log-normal pattern, reflecting the variability in contact quality. As the current increases, local heating at resistive contacts induces microwelding, narrowing the resistance distribution to a Gaussian profile and enhancing overall conductivity. The influence of external electromagnetic waves, simulated by nearby electrical sparks, is examined on the chain's electrical properties.
label: llm

text: The transverse broadening of jets produced in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS)off a large nucleus is studied in the collinear limit. A class of mediumenhanced higher twist corrections are re-summed to calculate the transversemomentum distribution of the produced collinear jet. In contrast to previousapproaches, resummation of the leading length enhanced higher twist correctionsis shown to lead to a two dimensional diffusion equation for the transversemomentum of the propagating jet. Results for the average transverse momentumobtained from this approach are then compared to the broadening expected from aclassical Langevin analysis for the propagation of the jet under the action ofthe fluctuating color Lorentz force inside the nucleons. The set ofapproximations that lead to identical results from the two approaches areoutlined. The relationship between the momentum diffusion constant $D$ and thetransport coefficient $\hat{q}$ is explicitly derived.
label: human

text: The transverse broadening of jets produced in deep-inelastic scattering off a large nucleus is investigated in the collinear limit. A class of medium-enhanced higher-twist corrections, arising from multiple scattering within the nuclear medium, is resummed to all orders in the length-enhanced contributions. In contrast to prior treatments, this resummation yields a two-dimensional diffusion equation governing the transverse momentum distribution of the propagating jet. The resulting average transverse momentum squared grows linearly with the nuclear path length, consistent with diffusive broadening. These findings are compared to the momentum broadening predicted by a classical Langevin model, where the jet experiences random kicks from a fluctuating color Lorentz force in the medium. The higher-twist approach captures quantum interference effects absent in the classical description, yet yields qualitatively similar diffusive behavior for the non-radiative propagation.
label: llm

text: This paper uses Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models to compute response ofstructural system subject to Indian earthquakes at Chamoli and Uttarkashiground motion data. The system is first trained for a single real earthquakedata. The trained ANN architecture is then used to simulate earthquakes withvarious intensities and it was found that the predicted responses given by ANNmodel are accurate for practical purposes. When the ANN is trained by a part ofthe ground motion data, it can also identify the responses of the structuralsystem well. In this way the safeness of the structural systems may bepredicted in case of future earthquakes without waiting for the earthquake tooccur for the lessons. Time period and the corresponding maximum response ofthe building for an earthquake has been evaluated, which is again trained topredict the maximum response of the building at different time periods. Thetrained time period versus maximum response ANN model is also tested for realearthquake data of other place, which was not used in the training and wasfound to be in good agreement.
label: human

text: This study investigates the application of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to predict the dynamic response of structural systems subjected to earthquake ground motions. Traditional numerical methods for seismic response analysis can be computationally intensive, particularly for nonlinear systems or when evaluating multiple scenarios. ANNs offer a promising alternative by learning complex mappings between input ground accelerations and output structural responses from training data. In this work, a feed-forward ANN architecture is employed and trained using time-history data from recorded earthquakes, such as those from Chamoli and Uttarkashi in India. The network is trained on responses of a single-degree-of-freedom system to capture the underlying dynamics efficiently. Once trained, the ANN model is tested by simulating responses under scaled intensities of the same earthquake as well as unseen ground motions. Results demonstrate that the predicted displacement time histories closely match those obtained from conventional dynamic analysis, indicating high accuracy for practical engineering applications.
label: llm

text: Using the Swift data of GRB 050315, we progress on the uniqueness of ourtheoretically predicted Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB) structure as composed by aproper-GRB (P-GRB), emitted at the transparency of an electron-positron plasmawith suitable baryon loading, and an afterglow comprising the so called "promptemission" as due to external shocks. Thanks to the Swift observations, we cantheoretically fit detailed light curves for selected energy bands on acontinuous time scale ranging over 10^6 seconds. The theoretically predictedinstantaneous spectral distribution over the entire afterglow confirms a clearhard-to-soft behavior encompassing, continuously, the "prompt emission" all theway to the latest phases of the afterglow. Consequences of the instrumentalthreshold on the definition of "short" and "long" GRBs are discussed.
label: human

text: Abstract Using Swift observations of GRB 050315, this work advances the validation of a theoretically predicted unified structure for long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), consisting of a proper-GRB (P-GRB) emitted at the transparency radius of an electron-positron plasma with appropriate baryon loading, followed by an afterglow phase where the traditionally observed "prompt emission" arises from external shocks. Detailed theoretical fits to the BAT and XRT light curves across multiple energy bands demonstrate consistency with this canonical model, revealing a continuous hard-to-soft spectral evolution spanning from the initial P-GRB through the entire afterglow duration. The successful matching of the complete multi-band temporal and spectral behavior for this burst provides strong evidence toward the uniqueness of this overall GRB structure.
label: llm

text: In this paper we present our results of a comprehensive spectroscopicanalysisof WASP-1, the host star to the exoplanet WASP-1b. We derive T_eff = 6110 +/-45 K, log g = 4.28 +/- 0.15, and [M/H] = 0.23 +/- 0.08, and also a highabundance of lithium, log n(Li) = 2.91 +/- 0.05. These parameters suggests anage for the system of 1-3 Gyr and a stellar mass of 1.25-1.35 M_sun. This meansthat WASP-1 has properties very similar to those of HD 149026, the host starfor the highest density planet yet detected. Moreover, their planets orbit atcomparable distances and receive comparable irradiating fluxes from their hoststars. However, despite the similarity of WASP-1 with HD 149026, their planetshave strongly different densities. This suggests that gas-giant planet densityis not a simple function of host-star metallicity or of radiation environmentat ages of ~2 Gyr.
label: human

text: We present a detailed spectroscopic analysis of WASP-1, the host star of the transiting exoplanet WASP-1b. High-resolution spectra reveal an effective temperature of 6110 ± 45 K, surface gravity log g = 4.28 ± 0.15, and super-solar metallicity [M/H] = 0.23 ± 0.08. Notably, the star exhibits a high lithium abundance, with log n(Li) = 2.91 ± 0.05, unusual for its evolutionary stage. These parameters indicate a stellar mass of 1.25–1.35 M⊙ and an age of approximately 1–3 Gyr. The transiting planet WASP-1b has a mass of about 0.85 M_Jup and an inflated radius yielding a low density of roughly 0.27 ρ_Jup, rendering it oversized relative to standard models. Strikingly, WASP-1 shares similar stellar properties with the host of the dense planet HD 149026b, yet the planets exhibit markedly different structures despite comparable orbital distances and irradiation levels.
label: llm

text: The formation of the circumbinary envelope of Cygnus X-3 was studied byparticle simulations of the WR (Wolf Rayet) companion wind. Light curvesresulting from electron scattering absorption in this envelope were computedand compared with observed IBIS/ISGRI and BATSE light curves. The matching wasrelatively good. For reasonable values of binary parameters (masses,inclination) and wind velocities, a stable envelope was formed during a fewbinary orbits. Assuming approximately 10^-6 solar mass/year for the rate of theWR-wind, the observed light curves and accretion luminosity can be re-produced(assuming Thomson scattering opacity in the ionized He-rich envelope). Theilluminated envelope can also model the CHANDRA-spectrum using thephotoionizing XSTAR-code. Furthermore, we discuss observed radial velocitycurves of IR emission lines in the context of simulated velocity fields andfind good agreement.
label: human

text: Cygnus X-3 is a high-mass X-ray binary system consisting of a compact object and a Wolf-Rayet companion star with a strong stellar wind and an orbital period of 4.8 hours. The observed orbital modulation in X-ray light curves is primarily attributed to electron scattering absorption in the dense wind material surrounding the system. In this study, we employ three-dimensional particle simulations to model the dynamics of the Wolf-Rayet wind within the binary gravitational potential. These simulations trace the trajectories of wind particles launched from the companion star, revealing the formation of a circumbinary envelope shaped by orbital motion and gravitational forces. Synthetic X-ray light curves are computed by integrating Thomson scattering optical depths along lines of sight to the compact object across orbital phases. The resulting modulated light curves show good agreement with observations from instruments such as IBIS/ISGRI and BATSE, reproducing the characteristic depth and asymmetry of the modulation.
label: llm

text: The driving mechanism of jets and outflows in star formation process isstudied using resistive MHD nested grid simulations. We calculated cloudevolution from the molecular cloud core to the stellar core. In the collapsingcloud core, we found two distinct flows: Low-velocity flows (sim 5 km/s) with awide opening angle, driven from the adiabatic core, and high-velocity flows(sim 30 km/s) with good collimation, driven from the protostar. High-velocityflows are enclosed by low-velocity flows after protostar formation. Thedifference in the degree of collimation between the two flows is caused by thestrength of the magnetic field and configuration of the magnetic field lines.The magnetic field around an adiabatic core is strong and has an hourglassconfiguration; therefore, flows from the adiabatic core are driven mainly bythe magnetocentrifugal mechanism and guided by the hourglass-like field lines.In contrast, the magnetic field around the protostar is weak and has a straightconfiguration owing to Ohmic dissipation in the high-density gas region.Therefore, flows from the protostar are driven mainly by the magnetic pressuregradient force and guided by straight field lines. Differing depth of thegravitational potential between the adiabatic core and the protostar cause thedifference of the flow speed. Low-velocity flows correspond to the observedmolecular outflows, while high-velocity flows correspond to the observedoptical jets. We suggest that the outflow and the jet are driven by differentcores, rather than that the outflow being entrained by the jet.
label: human

text: Jets and outflows are ubiquitous phenomena in the star formation process, playing a crucial role in regulating accretion and dispersing angular momentum. This study investigates the driving mechanisms of these flows using three-dimensional resistive magnetohydrodynamic simulations of collapsing cloud cores. Simulations reveal two distinct components: low-velocity wide-angle outflows and high-velocity collimated jets. Low-velocity outflows, with speeds of ~5-10 km/s and wide opening angles, emerge from the first adiabatic core or outer regions of the circumstellar disk, primarily driven by the magnetocentrifugal mechanism along hourglass-shaped magnetic field lines. In contrast, high-velocity jets, reaching ~30-100 km/s with excellent collimation, originate near the protostar or inner disk edge, propelled mainly by the magnetic pressure gradient force along straighter field lines. The difference in driving regions and forces arises from varying gravitational potential depths and magnetic field configurations between the adiabatic core and protostar. These dual flows suggest that wide molecular outflows and narrow optical jets are powered independently, rather than the former being solely entrained by the latter. Protostellar outflows and jets thus provide essential feedback, ejecting significant mass and momentum to influence the final stellar mass and cloud evolution.
label: llm

text: We present a theoretical study of the interplay between cyclotron motion andspin splitting of charge carriers in solids. While many of our results applymore generally, we focus especially on discussing the Rashba model describingelectrons in the conduction band of asymmetric semiconductor heterostructures.Appropriate semiclassical limits are distinguished that describe varioussituations of experimental interest. Our analytical fomulae, which take fullaccount of Zeeman splitting, are used to analyse recent magnetic-focusing data.Surprisingly, it turns out that the Rashba effect can dominate the splitting ofcyclotron orbits even when the Rashba and Zeeman spin-splitting energies are ofthe same order. We also find that the origin of spin-dependent cyclotron motioncan be traced back to Zitterbewegung-like oscillatory dynamics of chargecarriers from spin-split bands. The relation between the two phenomena isdiscussed, and we estimate the effect of Zitterbewegung-related corrections tothe charge carriers' canonical position.
label: human

text: We present a theoretical investigation into the interplay between cyclotron orbits and spin-orbit-induced splitting of charge-carrier bands in solids, with particular emphasis on the Rashba model relevant to asymmetric semiconductor heterostructures. Analytical expressions for spin-dependent cyclotron radii are derived, fully incorporating Zeeman effects, and applied to interpret magnetic-focusing experiments. Surprisingly, the Rashba spin splitting is found to dominate the separation of cyclotron orbits even when comparable in magnitude to Zeeman splitting. The origin of this spin-dependent cyclotron motion is traced to a semiclassical manifestation of Zitterbewegung-like oscillatory dynamics inherent to charge carriers in spin-split bands. Finally, the relation between magnetic focusing and Zitterbewegung is elucidated, including estimates of corrections to the carriers' canonical position arising from these trembling motions.
label: llm

text: The emergence of magnetic flux from the convection zone into the corona is animportant process for the dynamical evolution of the coronal magnetic field. Inthis paper we extend our previous numerical investigations, by looking at theprocess of flux interaction as an initially twisted flux tube emerges into aplane parallel, coronal magnetic field. Significant differences are found inthe dynamical appearance and evolution of the emergence process depending onthe relative orientation between the rising flux system and any preexistingcoronal field. When the flux systems are nearly anti-parallel, the experimentsshow substantial reconnection and demonstrate clear signatures of a hightemperature plasma located in the high velocity outflow regions extending fromthe reconnection region. However, the cases that have a more parallelorientation of the flux systems show very limited reconnection and none of theassociated features. Despite the very different amount of reconnection betweenthe two flux systems, it is found that the emerging flux that is stillconnected to the original tube, reaches the same height as a function of time.As a compensation for the loss of tube flux, a clear difference is found in theextent of the emerging loop in the direction perpendicular to the main axis ofthe initial flux tube. Increasing amounts of magnetic reconnection decrease thevolume, which confines the remaining tube flux.
label: human

text: The emergence of magnetic flux from the solar convection zone into the corona plays a crucial role in the dynamical evolution of the coronal magnetic field. This study extends previous numerical investigations by simulating the emergence of an initially twisted flux tube into a plane-parallel preexisting coronal magnetic field. Significant differences are observed in the dynamical appearance and evolution of the flux emergence process, depending on the relative orientation between the emerging flux system and the overlying coronal field. When the fields are oriented in an antiparallel configuration, efficient magnetic reconnection occurs, leading to vigorous dynamical features such as high-velocity outflows and enhanced heating. In contrast, cases with more parallel orientations exhibit very limited reconnection and lack these associated dynamical signatures. Remarkably, despite the varying degrees of reconnection and flux transfer between the systems, the height reached by the emerging flux remaining connected to the original tube is independent of the orientation over time. To compensate for flux loss in strongly reconnecting cases, the emerging magnetic loops expand more extensively in the direction perpendicular to the initial tube axis. These global properties highlight the importance of field orientation in determining the interaction outcomes during flux emergence in the solar atmosphere.
label: llm

text: We use the direct Fourier method to calculate the redshift-space powerspectrum of the maxBCG cluster catalog (Koester et al. 2007) -- currently byfar the largest existing galaxy cluster sample. The total number of clustersused in our analysis is 12,616. After accounting for the radial smearing effectcaused by photometric redshift errors and also introducing a simple treatmentfor the nonlinear effects, we show that currently favored low matter density``concordance'' LambdaCDM cosmology provides a very good fit to the estimatedpower. Thanks to the large volume (~ 0.4 h^{-3} Gpc^3), high clusteringamplitude (linear effective bias parameter b_{eff} ~ 3x(0.85/sigma_8)), andsufficiently high sampling density (~ 3x10^{-5} h^{3} Mpc^{-3}) the recoveredpower spectrum has high enough signal to noise to allow us to find weakevidence (~ 2sigma CL) for the acoustic features. These results are encouragingin light of the several proposed large cluster surveys. In case we use thephotometric redshift errors as suggested in Koester et al. (2007) we are leftwith the excess large-scale power which has previously been noticed by severalother authors.
label: human

text: We present the redshift-space power spectrum of the maxBCG galaxy cluster catalog, the largest optically selected cluster sample available at the time, comprising 12,616 clusters in the redshift range 0.1–0.3. The power spectrum is computed using a direct Fourier transform method applied to the three-dimensional cluster positions derived from photometric redshifts. To account for uncertainties in photometric redshifts, we incorporate a radial smearing correction that models the damping effect along the line of sight. A simple parameterization is also introduced to address mild nonlinear distortions on smaller scales. The measured power spectrum is well described by the concordance ΛCDM model with low matter density, yielding an excellent fit across a broad range of wavenumbers. The large surveyed volume of approximately 0.4 h⁻³ Gpc³, combined with the high linear bias of clusters (b_eff ≈ 3 × (0.85/σ₈)) and moderate sampling density (~3 × 10⁻⁵ h³ Mpc⁻³), results in sufficient signal-to-noise to probe subtle features. We detect weak evidence, at approximately the 2σ confidence level, for baryon acoustic oscillations imprinted in the cluster power spectrum.
label: llm

text: We present results from a study of the distances and distribution of a sampleof intermediate-age clusters in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Using deepnear-infrared photometry obtained with ISPI on the CTIO 4m, we have measuredthe apparent K-band magnitude of the core helium burning red clump stars in 17LMC clusters. We combine cluster ages and metallicities with the work ofGrocholski & Sarajedini to predict each cluster's absolute K-band red clumpmagnitude, and thereby calculate absolute cluster distances. An analysis ofthese data shows that the cluster distribution is in good agreement with thethick, inclined disk geometry of the LMC, as defined by its field stars. Wealso find that the old globular clusters follow the same distribution,suggesting that the LMC's disk formed at about the same time as the globularclusters, ~ 13 Gyr ago. Finally, we have used our cluster distances inconjunction with the disk geometry to calculate the distance to the LMC center,for which we find (m-M)o = 18.40 +/- 0.04_{ran} +/- 0.08_{sys}, or Do = 47.9+/- 0.9 +/- 1.8 kpc.
label: human

text: We present deep near-infrared photometry of 17 intermediate-age populous clusters in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), obtained using the Infrared Side Port Imager (ISPI) on the CTIO 4 m telescope. These data allow precise measurement of the apparent K-band magnitude of the core helium-burning red clump stars in each cluster. By incorporating previously determined cluster ages and metallicities, we apply population corrections to predict the absolute K-band red clump luminosity for each system. The resulting individual cluster distances reveal a spatial distribution consistent with the thick, inclined disk geometry previously established for LMC field stars. Notably, the old globular clusters in the LMC align with this same disk structure, implying that the disk formed contemporaneously with these ancient clusters approximately 13 Gyr ago. Combining these cluster distances with the inferred disk geometry yields a distance modulus to the LMC center of (m-M)_0 = 18.40 ± 0.04 (random) ± 0.08 (systematic) mag, corresponding to a distance of 47.9 ± 0.9 ± 1.8 kpc.
label: llm

text: Heterogeneous materials abound in nature and man-made situations. Examplesinclude porous media, biological materials, and composite materials. Diverseand interesting properties exhibited by these materials result from theircomplex microstructures, which also make it difficult to model the materials.In this first part of a series of two papers, we collect the known necessaryconditions on the standard two-point correlation function S2(r) and formulate anew conjecture. In particular, we argue that given a complete two-pointcorrelation function space, S2(r) of any statistically homogeneous material canbe expressed through a map on a selected set of bases of the function space. Weprovide new examples of realizable two-point correlation functions and suggesta set of analytical basis functions. Moreover, we devise an efficient andisotropy- preserving construction algorithm, namely, the Lattice-Pointalgorithm to generate realizations of materials from their two- pointcorrelation functions based on the Yeong-Torquato technique. Subsequentanalysis can be performed on the generated images to obtain desired macroscopicproperties. These developments are integrated here into a general scheme thatenables one to model and categorize heterogeneous materials via two-pointcorrelation functions.
label: human

text: Heterogeneous materials, such as composites, porous media, and biological tissues, exhibit diverse macroscopic properties that arise from their intricate microstructures. Modeling these materials accurately is challenging due to the complexity of their random heterogeneous morphologies. Two-point correlation functions \(S_2(\mathbf{r})\) provide a fundamental statistical descriptor of microstructure by quantifying the probability of finding points separated by vector \(\mathbf{r}\) in the same phase. This paper, the first in a series, establishes the basic principles for characterizing and reconstructing heterogeneous materials using \(S_2(\mathbf{r})\). Known necessary conditions on \(S_2(\mathbf{r})\) for realizability are reviewed, and a new conjecture regarding its asymptotic behavior is proposed. Examples of realizable two-point correlation functions are presented, along with a suggested set of analytical basis functions spanning the relevant function space. An exact mathematical formulation of the reconstruction problem is discussed, including a proof that \(S_2(\mathbf{r})\) alone cannot uniquely specify a two-phase medium. These foundational elements are integrated into a comprehensive framework for modeling, categorizing, and ultimately designing heterogeneous materials via two-point statistics.
label: llm

text: We study the cosmological evolution of a tachyon scalar field T with aDirac-Born-Infeld type lagrangian and potential V(T) coupled to a canonicallynormalized scalar field \phi with an arbitrary interaction term B(T,\phi) inthe presence of a barotropic fluid $\rb$, which can be matter or radiation. Theforce between the barotropic fluid and the scalar fields is only gravitational.We show that the dynamics is completely determine by only three parameters L1 =- V_T/ V^{3/2}, L2= - B_T /B^{3/2} and L3 =-B_{\phi}/B. We determineanalytically theconditions for $\lm_i$ under which the energy density of T,\phi and $\rb$ have the same redshift. We study the behavior of T and \phi inthe asymptotic limits for L_i and we show the numerical solution for differentinteresting cases.  The effective equation of state for the tachyon field changes due to theinteraction with the scalar field and we show that it is possible for a tachyonfield to redshift as matter in the absence of an interaction term B and asradiation when B is turned on. This result solves then the tachyonic matterproblem.
label: human

text: We study the cosmological evolution of a tachyon scalar field with a Dirac-Born-Infeld type Lagrangian and potential coupled to a canonically normalized scalar field via an arbitrary interaction term, in the presence of a barotropic fluid representing matter or radiation. The interaction modifies the effective dynamics of both fields while preserving purely gravitational coupling with the barotropic component. We demonstrate that the system's evolution is fully determined by a minimal set of three parameters characterizing the potentials and interaction. Analytical solutions are derived for asymptotic regimes, revealing conditions for stable evolution of the fields. The interaction alters the effective equation of state of the tachyon field, enabling it to mimic matter-like redshifting without interaction or radiation-like behavior when the coupling is activated. Numerical investigations confirm these behaviors across various parameter choices, highlighting viable cosmological scenarios that address inconsistencies in standalone tachyon models.
label: llm

text: Following the recent insight in the material structure of comets,protoplanetesimals are assumed to have low densities and to be highly porousagglomerates. It is still unclear if planetesimals can be formed from theseobjects by collisional growth. Therefore, it is important to study numericallythe collisional outcome from low velocity impacts of equal sized porousagglomerates which are too large to be examined in a laboratory experiment. Weuse the Lagrangian particle method Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics to solve theequations that describe the dynamics of elastic and plastic bodies.Additionally, to account for the influence of porosity, we follow a previousdeveloped equation of state and certain relations between the material strengthand the relative density. Collisional growth seems possible for rather lowcollision velocities and particular material strengths. The remnants ofcollisions with impact parameters that are larger than 50% of the radius of thecolliding objects tend to rotate. For small impact parameters, the collidingobjects are effectively slowed down without a prominent compaction of theporous structure, which probably increases the possibility for growth. Theprotoplanetesimals, however, do not stick together for the most part of theemployed material strengths. An important issue in subsequent studies has to bethe influence of rotation to collisional growth. Moreover, for realisticsimulations of protoplanetesimals it is crucial to know the correct materialparameters in more detail.
label: human

text: Recent insights into cometary structures suggest that protoplanetesimals are highly porous, low-density agglomerates of ice grains, raising questions about their ability to grow into larger bodies via collisions. This study employs numerical simulations to investigate low-velocity impacts between equal-sized porous ice grain agglomerates, which are too large for direct laboratory replication. The agglomerates are modeled as ensembles of microscopic ice monomers bound by adhesive forces, with initial porosities reflecting those expected in protoplanetary disks beyond the snow line. Simulations vary collision velocities, impact parameters, and material strengths to capture a range of outcomes. At low velocities, collisions result in sticking and merger, facilitating net growth. For higher velocities, bouncing occurs, often accompanied by energy dissipation through restructuring rather than fragmentation. Central impacts with small impact parameters effectively decelerate the bodies while preserving much of the porous structure, minimizing compaction. Offset collisions with impact parameters exceeding 50% of the agglomerate radius frequently impart significant rotation to the post-collision remnants. Collisional growth appears viable primarily at low velocities and for moderate material strengths, consistent with conditions in the outer protoplanetary disk. These findings imply that rotation induced in grazing collisions may influence subsequent growth efficiency, warranting further investigation in models of planetesimal formation.
label: llm

text: We continue the study of the non-metric theory of gravity introduced inhep-th/0611182 and gr-qc/0703002 and obtain its general spherically symmetricvacuum solution. It respects the analog of the Birkhoff theorem, i.e., thevacuum spherically symmetric solution is necessarily static. As in generalrelativity, the spherically symmetric solution is seen to describe a blackhole. The exterior geometry is essentially the same as in the Schwarzschildcase, with power-law corrections to the Newtonian potential. The behaviorinside the black-hole region is different from the Schwarzschild case in thatthe usual spacetime singularity gets replaced by a singular surface of a newtype, where all basic fields of the theory remain finite but metric ceases toexist. The theory does not admit arbitrarily small black holes: for smallobjects, the curvature on the would-be horizon is so strong that non-metricmodifications prevent the horizon from being formed. The theory allows formodifications of gravity of very interesting nature. We discuss three physicaleffects, namely, (i) correction to Newton's law in the neighborhood of thesource, (ii) renormalization of effective gravitational and cosmologicalconstants at large distances from the source, and (iii) additional redshiftfactor between spatial regions of different curvature. The first two effectscan be responsible, respectively, for the observed anomaly in the accelerationof the Pioneer spacecraft and for the alleged missing mass in spiral galaxiesand other astrophysical objects. The third effect can be used to propose anon-cosmological explanation of high redshifts of quasars and gamma-ray bursts.
label: human

text: This paper presents the general spherically symmetric vacuum solution within a class of non-metric modified gravity theories. These theories generalize the Plebanski formulation of general relativity by incorporating additional terms dependent on the Lagrange multiplier field. The resulting spacetime metric deviates from the Schwarzschild form in the presence of modification parameters. The spherically symmetric solution exhibits three distinct physical effects arising from the non-metric nature of the theory. One effect manifests as a constant acceleration term, potentially accounting for the observed anomalous acceleration of the Pioneer spacecraft. Another effect produces an additional attractive force that mimics the presence of extra mass in gravitational systems. This additional force can explain the flat rotation curves observed in spiral galaxies without invoking dark matter. The solution similarly accounts for the inferred missing mass in clusters and other astrophysical structures. A third effect introduces an extra gravitational redshift for light propagating in the field. This non-cosmological redshift mechanism offers a potential intrinsic explanation for the anomalously high redshifts observed in quasars and gamma-ray bursts.
label: llm

text: We describe an efficient approximation algorithm for evaluating theground-state energy of the classical Ising Hamiltonian with linear terms on anarbitrary planar graph. The running time of the algorithm grows linearly withthe number of spins and exponentially with 1/epsilon, where epsilon is theworst-case relative error. This result contrasts the well known fact that exactcomputation of the ground-state energy for the two-dimensional Ising spin glassmodel is NP-hard. We also present a classical approximation algorithm for theLocal Hamiltonian Problem or Quantum Ising Spin Glass problem on a planar graphwith bounded degree which is known to be a QMA-complete problem. Using adifferent technique we find a classical approximation algorithm for the quantumIsing spin glass problem on the simplest planar graph with unbounded degree,the star graph.
label: human

text: We present a classical polynomial-time approximation scheme for computing the ground-state energy of the classical Ising Hamiltonian, including linear terms, on arbitrary planar graphs. The algorithm achieves a relative error ε with runtime linear in the number of spins and exponential in 1/ε. This contrasts sharply with the NP-hardness of exact computation for the two-dimensional Ising spin glass model. Extending these techniques, we develop a classical approximation algorithm for the quantum Ising spin glass (Local Hamiltonian) problem on planar graphs with bounded degree, despite its QMA-completeness. Additionally, using alternative methods, we obtain approximations for quantum cases on specific planar structures like star graphs with unbounded degree.
label: llm

text: We consider processes with second order long range dependence resulting fromheavy tailed durations. We refer to this phenomenon as duration-driven longrange dependence (DDLRD), as opposed to the more widely studied linear longrange dependence based on fractional differencing of an $iid$ process. Weconsider in detail two specific processes having DDLRD, originally presented inTaqqu and Levy (1986), and Parke (1999). For these processes, we obtain thelimiting distribution of suitably standardized discrete Fourier transforms(DFTs) and sample autocovariances. At low frequencies, the standardized DFTsconverge to a stable law, as do the standardized sample autocovariances atfixed lags.
