We combinegalaxy velocity and position information to select 85 galaxies recognized ascluster members (from 115 galaxies observed at TNG telescope), determine globaldynamical properties and detect substructures. We find that A115 presentsvelocity dispersion of sigma_v=1362_{-108}^{+126} km/s. Our analysis confirmsthe presence of two structures (A115N and A115S) of cluster--type wellrecognizable in the plane of the sky and shows that they differ of ~2000 km/sin the LOS velocity. We estimate that A115S is slightly dynamically moreimportant than A115N having sigma_v=900-1100 km/s vs sigma_v=750-850 km/s.Moreover, we find evidence for two small groups at low velocities. We estimatea global cluster virial mass of 2.2--3.5 e15 h_70 Msun. Our results agree witha pre--merging scenario where A115N and A115S are colliding with a LOS impactvelocity Delta v~1600 km/s.The most likely solution to the two--body problemsuggests that the merging axis lies at $\sim 20$ degrees from the plane of thesky and that the cores will cross after ~0.1 Gyr. The radio relic with itslargest dimension perpendicular to the merging axis is likely connected to thismerger.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive dynamical analysis of the galaxy cluster Abell 115 at *z* = 0.193, a hot X-ray system known for its binary morphology and prominent radio relic. Our study is based on new spectroscopic observations of 115 galaxies obtained with the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo and wide-field photometric data from the Isaac Newton Telescope. By combining positional and velocity information, we identify 85 confirmed cluster members and investigate the global dynamical properties as well as substructure. The overall cluster exhibits a high line-of-sight velocity dispersion of 1362 km s⁻¹, indicative of significant gravitational potential depth. Detailed substructure analysis reveals two prominent subclusters: a southern low-velocity component (A115S) centered on the brightest cluster galaxy and aligned with the southern X-ray peak, and a northern high-velocity component (A115N) associated with the second-brightest galaxy (coincident with the radio source 3C 28) and the northern X-ray peak. These subclusters show a relative line-of-sight velocity difference of approximately 2000 km s⁻¹, confirming an ongoing major merger. The southern subcluster appears dynamically dominant with a velocity dispersion of 900–1100 km s⁻¹ compared to 750–850 km s⁻¹ for the northern one, in addition to evidence for smaller infalling groups at lower velocities.
label: llm

text: We study and simulate N=2 supersymmetric Wess-Zumino models in one and twodimensions. For any choice of the lattice derivative, the theories can be mademanifestly supersymmetric by adding appropriate improvement terms correspondingto discretizations of surface integrals. In one dimension, our simulations showthat a model with the Wilson derivative and the Stratonovitch prescription forthis discretization leads to far better results at finite lattice spacing thanother models with Wilson fermions considered in the literature. In particular,we check that fermionic and bosonic masses coincide and the unbroken Wardidentities are fulfilled to high accuracy. Equally good results for theeffective masses can be obtained in a model with the SLAC derivative (evenwithout improvement terms).  In two dimensions we introduce a non-standard Wilson term in such a way thatthe discretization errors of the kinetic terms are only of order O(a^2). Massesextracted from the corresponding manifestly supersymmetric model prove toapproach their continuum values much quicker than those from a model containingthe standard Wilson term. Again, a comparable enhancement can be achieved in atheory using the SLAC derivative.
label: human

text: We investigate \(\mathcal{N}=2\) supersymmetric Wess-Zumino models formulated on discrete lattices in one and two spacetime dimensions. Preserving supersymmetry on the lattice poses significant challenges due to the breakdown of Leibniz rule and the emergence of doublers. To address these issues, we render the theories manifestly supersymmetric for arbitrary lattice derivatives by incorporating suitable improvement terms that discretize surface contributions. In one dimension, this approach ensures exact supersymmetry at finite lattice spacing while maintaining locality. For two dimensions, we propose a novel non-standard Wilson term that reduces discretization errors in the kinetic sector to \(\mathcal{O}(a^2)\), significantly improving convergence. Numerical simulations reveal that particle masses extracted from the improved manifestly supersymmetric action approach continuum limits far more rapidly compared to standard Wilson formulations. Comparable enhancements are observed when employing the SLAC derivative. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of manifest supersymmetry in mitigating fine-tuning and artifacts in low-dimensional lattice models. Our results pave the way for reliable non-perturbative studies of supersymmetric theories in higher dimensions.
label: llm

text: We explore further the discovery potential for heavy quarks at the LHC, withemphasis on the $t'$ and $b'$ of a sequential fourth family associated withelectroweak symmetry breaking. We consider QCD multijets, $t\bar{t}+\rm{jets}$,$W+\rm{jets}$ and single $t$ backgrounds using event generation based onimproved matrix elements and low sensitivity to the modeling of initial stateradiation. We exploit a jet mass technique for the identification ofhadronically decaying $W$'s and $t$'s, to be used in the reconstruction of the$t'$ or $b'$ mass. This along with other aspects of event selection can reducebackgrounds to very manageable levels. It even allows a search for both $t'$and $b'$ in the absence of $b$-tagging, of interest for the early running ofthe LHC. A heavy quark mass of order 600 GeV is motivated by the connection toelectroweak symmetry breaking, but our analysis is relevant for any new heavyquarks with weak decay modes.
label: human

text: The search for heavy quarks beyond the Standard Model's top quark, such as fourth-generation or vector-like quarks, is a key objective at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) to probe new physics addressing electroweak symmetry breaking and the hierarchy problem. These heavy quarks, often denoted as t' or b' with charges +2/3 or -1/3, or exotic charges like +5/3, are predicted in extensions like sequential fourth families or composite Higgs models. Pair production via strong interactions dominates at lower masses, while single production becomes relevant at higher masses through electroweak processes. Typical decay modes include t' → Wb, t' → Ht, or t' → Zt, leading to signatures with multiple jets, b-quarks, leptons, and missing energy. Advanced analysis techniques, including boosted object tagging and machine learning, enhance sensitivity to masses beyond 1 TeV. Current LHC results from ATLAS and CMS experiments set stringent lower mass limits around 1.
label: llm

text: The MEGAPIE project is a key experiment on the road to Accelerator DrivenSystems and it provides the scientific community with unique data on thebehavior of a liquid lead-bismuth spallation target under realistic and longterm irradiation conditions. The neutronic of such target is of course of primeimportance when considering its final destination as an intense neutron source.This is the motivation to characterize the inside neutron flux of the target inoperation. A complex detector, made of 8 micro fission-chambers, has been builtand installed in the core of the target, few tens of centimeters from theproton/Pb-Bi interaction zone. This detector is designed to measure theabsolute neutron flux inside the target, to give its spatial distribution andto correlate its temporal variations with the beam intensity. Moreover,integral information on the neutron energy distribution as a function of theposition along the beam axis could be extracted, giving integral constraints onthe neutron production models implemented in transport codes such as MCNPX.
label: human

text: The MEGAPIE (MEGAwatt Pilot Experiment) target, a liquid lead-bismuth eutectic (LBE) spallation neutron source, was designed and operated at the SINQ facility to demonstrate the feasibility of high-power liquid metal targets for accelerator-driven systems and intense neutron production. Neutronic performance was assessed through in-target measurements using micro-fission chambers and activation foils positioned near the spallation zone, alongside external flux monitoring at beam lines. Experimental results revealed a significantly higher neutron yield compared to previous solid lead targets, with thermal and epithermal flux increases ranging from a factor of 1.6 to 1.8 depending on the beam line. Monte Carlo simulations generally reproduced the overall performance enhancements but showed discrepancies in fission rates, particularly for fast neutrons, due to challenges in modeling the mixed neutron spectrum. These findings validate the superior neutronic efficiency of liquid LBE targets and provide critical data for optimizing future high-power spallation sources and ADS designs.
label: llm

text: We present an analysis of the Lyman alpha forests of five quasar spectra inthe near UV. Properties of the intergalactic medium (IGM) at an intermediateredshift interval (0.9 < z < 1.9) are studied. The amount of baryons in thediffuse photoionised IGM and the warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM) aretraced to get constraints on the redshift evolution of the different phases ofthe intergalactic gas. The baryon density of the diffuse IGM is determined withphotoionisation calculations under the assumption of local hydrostaticequilibrium. We assume that the gas is ionised by a metagalactic backgroundradiation with a Haardt & Madau (2001) spectrum. The WHIM is traced with broadLyman alpha (BLA) absorption. The properties of a number of BLA detections arestudied. Under the assumption of collisional ionisation equilibrium a lowerlimit to the baryon density could be estimated. It is found that the diffusephotoionised IGM contains at least 25% of the total baryonic matter atredshifts 1 < z < 2. For the WHIM a lower limit of 2.4% could be determined.Furthermore the data indicates that the intergalactic gas is in a state ofevolution at z=1.5. We confirm that a considerable part of the WHIM is createdbetween z=1 and z=2.
label: human

text: The amount of baryons residing in the diffuse photoionized intergalactic medium (IGM) and the warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM) is investigated at intermediate redshifts (0.9 < z < 1.9) to constrain the evolutionary history of intergalactic gas phases. High-resolution Lyman α forest spectra from five background quasars in the near-UV are analyzed. The baryon content of the diffuse photoionized IGM is estimated using photoionization models assuming local hydrostatic equilibrium. Ionization by a metagalactic UV background is modeled with a Haardt & Madau (2001) spectrum. Broad Lyman α (BLA) absorbers are identified and characterized as tracers of collisionally ionized gas in the WHIM. The physical properties of detected BLAs, including column densities and Doppler widths, are derived through Voigt profile fitting. Under the assumption of collisional ionization equilibrium, a minimum baryon overdensity is inferred for these systems. The diffuse photoionized IGM is found to account for at least 25% of the total baryonic matter in this redshift range. A lower limit of approximately 2.4% is established for the WHIM contribution traced by BLAs. These results indicate ongoing evolution in the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic gas around z ≈ 1.
label: llm

text: Barchans are dunes of high mobility which have a crescent shape and propagateunder conditions of unidirectional wind. However, sand dunes only appear abovea critical size, which scales with the saturation distance of the sand flux [P.Hersen, S. Douady, and B. Andreotti, Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf{89,}} 264301 (2002);B. Andreotti, P. Claudin, and S. Douady, Eur. Phys. J. B {\bf{28,}} 321 (2002);G. Sauermann, K. Kroy, and H. J. Herrmann, Phys. Rev. E {\bf{64,}} 31305(2001)]. It has been suggested by P. Hersen, S. Douady, and B. Andreotti, Phys.Rev. Lett. {\bf{89,}} 264301 (2002) that this flux fetch distance is itselfconstant. Indeed, this could not explain the proto size of barchan dunes, whichoften occur in coastal areas of high litoral drift, and the scale of dunes onMars. In the present work, we show from three dimensional calculations of sandtransport that the size and the shape of the minimal barchan dune depend on thewind friction speed and the sand flux on the area between dunes in a field. Ourresults explain the common appearance of barchans a few tens of centimeter highwhich are observed along coasts. Furthermore, we find that the rate at whichgrains enter saltation on Mars is one order of magnitude higher than on Earth,and is relevant to correctly obtain the minimal dune size on Mars.
label: human

text: Barchan dunes are crescent-shaped aeolian bedforms that form under unidirectional wind regimes and limited sand supply. These dunes exhibit high mobility and propagate while maintaining their characteristic shape. A key feature of barchan dunes is the existence of a minimal stable size below which they cannot persist. Previous studies have linked this minimal size to the saturation length of the sand flux, which represents the distance required for the sediment transport rate to adjust to local wind conditions. However, assuming a constant saturation length fails to account for the small barchan dunes commonly observed in coastal environments. It also does not explain the scale of barchan dunes on Mars. In this study, we employ three-dimensional numerical simulations of sand transport to investigate the formation and stability of barchan dunes. The model incorporates detailed calculations of saltation trajectories, grain entrainment, and erosion-deposition processes. We demonstrate that the minimal dune size depends on the wind friction speed. Stronger winds result in smaller minimal dunes due to reduced saturation transients. The interdune sand flux, influenced by the density of dunes in a field, also plays a critical role in determining the threshold size. Our simulations reproduce the emergence of small barchans with heights of a few tens of centimeters.
label: llm

text: We devise a {\sl non--perturbative} method, called {\sl ParametricPerturbation Theory} (PPT), which is alternative to the ordinary perturbationtheory. The method relies on a principle of simplicity for the observablesolutions, which are constrained to be linear in a certain (unphysical)parameter. The perturbative expansion is carried out in this parameter and notin the physical coupling (as in ordinary perturbation theory). We provide anumber of nontrivial examples, where our method is capable to resum thedivergent perturbative series, {\sl extract} the leading asymptotic (strongcoupling) behavior and {\sl predict} with high accuracy the coefficients of theperturbative series. In the case of a zero dimensional field theory we provethat PPT can be used to provide the imaginary part of the solution, when theproblem is analytically continued to negative couplings. In the case of a$\phi^4$ lattice model 1+1 and of elastic theory we have shown that theobservables resummed with PPT display a branch point at a finite value of thecoupling, signaling the transition from a stable to a metastable state. We havealso applied the method to the prediction of the virial coefficients for a hardsphere gas in two and three dimensions; in this example we have also found thatthe solution resummed with PPT has a singularity at finite density. Predictionsfor the unknown virial coefficients are made.
label: human

text: Traditional perturbation theory often yields divergent series for problems with finite or strong couplings, limiting its applicability beyond weak perturbation regimes. This work introduces Parametric Perturbation Theory (PPT), a non-perturbative approach that extends beyond conventional perturbation methods. PPT relies on a principle of simplicity, constraining observable solutions to be linear in an auxiliary, unphysical parameter. The perturbative expansion is performed in this parameter rather than the physical coupling constant. By optimizing the choice of the unphysical parameter, PPT effectively resums divergent perturbative series. Several nontrivial examples demonstrate that PPT accurately captures the leading asymptotic behavior in the strong-coupling limit. Moreover, it predicts higher-order coefficients of the original perturbative expansion with remarkable precision. In the context of a zero-dimensional field theory analytically continued to negative couplings, PPT successfully extracts the imaginary part of the solution, revealing non-perturbative effects. Overall, PPT provides a powerful alternative framework for addressing problems where standard perturbation theory fails.
label: llm

text: We present results for kaon decay widths of baryon resonances from arelativistic study with constituent quark models. The calculations are done inthe point-form of Poincare-invariant quantum mechanics with a spectator-modeldecay operator. We obtain covariant predictions of the Goldstone-boson-exchangeand a variant of the one-gluon-exchange constituent quark models for all kaondecay widths of established baryon resonances. They are generally characterizedby underestimating the available experimental data. In particular, the widthsof kaon decays with increasing strangeness in the baryon turn out to beextremely small. We also consider the nonrelativistic limit, leading to thefamiliar elementary emission model, and demonstrate the importance ofrelativistic effects. It is found that the nonrelativistic approach evidentlymisses sensible influences from Lorentz boosts and some essential spin-couplingterms.
label: human

text: We present covariant predictions for the strong decay widths of strange baryon resonances into channels involving kaons and other strange mesons, employing a relativistic constituent-quark model. The calculations are performed within the point-form of Poincaré-invariant relativistic quantum mechanics, using a spectator-model decay operator that ensures manifest covariance. Baryon wave functions are derived from models incorporating one-gluon-exchange and Goldstone-boson-exchange interactions, extended to include strange quarks. Particular attention is given to open-strangeness decays of excited Λ, Σ, and Ξ resonances, where kaon emission dominates. The computed partial widths for selected resonances show reasonable agreement with available experimental data from the Particle Data Group, though systematic underestimations are observed in some cases. These discrepancies are analyzed in terms of limitations in the quark-model wave functions and the simplicity of the decay operator.
label: llm

text: The impact of the strongly attractive electromagnetic field of heavy nucleion electrons in quasi-elastic (e,e') scattering is often accounted for by theeffective momentum approximation. This method is a plane wave Bornapproximation which takes the twofold effect of the attractive nucleus oninitial and final state electrons into account, namely the modification of theelectron momentum in the vicinity of the nucleus, and the focusing of electronstowards the nuclear region leading to an enhancement of the corresponding wavefunction amplitudes. The focusing effect due to the attractive Coulomb field ofa homogeneously charged sphere on a classical ensemble of charged particlesincident on the field is calculated in the highly relativistic limit andcompared to results obtained from exact solutions of the Dirac equation. Theresult is relevant for the theoretical foundation of the effective momentumapproximation and describes the high energy behavior of the amplitude ofcontinuum Dirac waves in the potential of a homogeneously charged sphere. Ourfindings indicate that the effective momentum approximation is a usefulapproximation for the calculation of Coulomb corrections in (e,e') scatteringoff heavy nuclei for sufficiently high electron energies and momentum transfer.
label: human

text: The effective momentum approximation (EMA) is commonly employed in quasi-elastic electron scattering off heavy nuclei to account for Coulomb distortions, incorporating both the local modification of electron momentum near the nucleus and the focusing effect that enhances wave function amplitudes in the nuclear region. This work investigates the focusing phenomenon classically for high-energy charged particles incident on the attractive electrostatic field of a homogeneously charged sphere, modeling the finite nuclear charge distribution. In the highly relativistic limit, the classical trajectories of an ensemble of particles are analyzed to quantify the focusing effect. The results are compared with exact continuum solutions of the Dirac equation in the same potential. This comparison validates the EMA's description of wave function enhancement at high energies and provides insight into its theoretical foundations for nuclear scattering processes.
label: llm

text: We report measurements of the spin polarization (\textbf{\textit{P}}) of theconcentrated magnetic semiconductor EuS using both zero-field and Zeeman-splitAndreev reflection spectroscopy (ARS) with EuS/Al planar junctions. Thezero-field ARS spectra are well described by the modified (spin-polarized) BTKmodel with expected superconducting energy gap and actual measurementtemperature (no additional spectral broadening). The fittings consistentlyyield \textbf{\textit{P}} close to 80% regardless of the barrier strength.Moreover, we performed ARS in the presence of a Zeeman-splitting of thequasiparticle density of states in Al. To describe the Zeeman-split ARSspectra, we develop a theoretical model which incorporates the solution to theMaki-Fulde equations into the modified BTK analysis. The method enables thedetermination of the magnitude as well as the sign of \textbf{\textit{P}} withARS, and the results are consistent with those from the zero-field ARS. Theexperiments extend the utility of field-split superconducting spectroscopy fromtunnel junctions to Andreev junctions of arbitrary barrier strengths.
label: human

text: We report measurements of the spin polarization of the concentrated magnetic semiconductor EuS using both zero-field and Zeeman-split Andreev reflection spectroscopy with EuS/Al planar junctions. The zero-field Andreev reflection spectra are accurately fitted by the modified spin-polarized Blonder-Tinkham-Klapwijk model, incorporating the expected superconducting energy gap of aluminum and the actual measurement temperature without requiring additional spectral broadening parameters. These fits yield a consistent transport spin polarization value near 80%, independent of the interfacial barrier strength. To further probe the spin polarization, we conducted measurements under applied magnetic fields that induce Zeeman splitting of the quasiparticle density of states in the aluminum superconductor. A theoretical model was developed, integrating solutions to the Maki-Fulde equations with the modified Blonder-Tinkham-Klapwijk framework, enabling determination of both the magnitude and sign of the spin polarization from the Zeeman-split spectra. The results from this field-split approach align closely with those obtained in zero field, confirming the robustness of the measured spin polarization in EuS.
label: llm

text: We present radio observations and optical spectroscopy of the giant lowsurface brightness (LSB) galaxy PGC 045080 (or 1300+0144). PGC 045080 is amoderately distant galaxy having a highly inclined optical disk and massive HIgas content. Radio continuum observations of the galaxy were carried out at 320MHz, 610 MHz and 1.4 GHz. Continuum emission was detected and mapped in thegalaxy. The emission appears extended over the inner disk at all threefrequencies. At 1.4 GHz and 610 MHz it appears to have two distinct lobes. Wealso did optical spectroscopy of the galaxy nucleus; the spectrum did not showany strong emission lines associated with AGN activity but the presence of aweak AGN cannot be ruled out. Furthermore, comparison of the H$\alpha$ flux andradio continuum at 1.4 GHz suggests that a significant fraction of the emissionis non-thermal in nature. Hence we conclude that a weak or hidden AGN may bepresent in PGC 045080. The extended radio emission represents lobes/jets fromthe AGN. These observations show that although LSB galaxies are metal poor andhave very little star formation, their centers can host significant AGNactivity. We also mapped the HI gas disk and velocity field in PGC 045080. TheHI disk extends well beyond the optical disk and appears warped. In the HIintensity maps, the disk appears distinctly lopsided. The velocity field isdisturbed on the lopsided side of the disk but is fairly uniform in the otherhalf. We derived the HI rotation curve for the galaxy from the velocity field.The rotation curve has a flat rotation speed of ~ 190 km/s.
label: human

text: We present multi-frequency radio continuum observations and optical spectroscopy of the giant low surface brightness (LSB) galaxy PGC 045080, also known as 1300+0144. PGC 045080 is a moderately distant system characterized by a highly inclined optical disk. It possesses a massive neutral hydrogen (HI) gas reservoir typical of LSB galaxies. Radio observations were conducted at 320 MHz, 610 MHz, and 1.4 GHz using interferometric arrays. Continuum emission was detected and mapped across all frequencies. The emission appears extended over the inner regions of the disk. At higher frequencies (610 MHz and 1.4 GHz), the morphology reveals two distinct lobes symmetric about the nucleus. Optical spectroscopy of the central region shows no prominent emission lines indicative of strong AGN activity. However, weak or obscured AGN signatures cannot be entirely excluded. Comparison of the Hα flux with the 1.4 GHz radio continuum suggests a significant non-thermal contribution. The spectral index analysis of the radio emission supports a synchrotron origin. The extended lobe-like structures are interpreted as jets or outflows powered by a central active galactic nucleus (AGN). We also present HI synthesis mapping of the gas disk and its velocity field. The HI distribution is extensive and lopsided, consistent with the massive gas content observed in many LSB systems. These results indicate that despite their low metallicity, suppressed star formation, and diffuse stellar disks, LSB galaxies can harbor significant central AGN activity. This finding challenges conventional views of AGN hosting in low-density environments and highlights the potential role of AGN feedback in the evolution of LSB galaxies.
label: llm

text: We study scaling relations of compressible strongly magnetized turbulence. Wefind a good correspondence of our results with the Fleck (1996) model ofcompressible hydrodynamic turbulence. In particular, we find that thedensity-weighted velocity, i.e. $u \equiv \rho^{1/3} v$, proposed in Kritsuk etal. (2007) obeys the Kolmogorov scaling, i.e. $E_{u}(k)\sim k^{-5/3}$ for thehigh Mach number turbulence. Similarly, we find that the exponents of the thirdorder structure functions for $u$ stay equal to unity for the all the Machnumbers studied. The scaling of higher order correlations obeys the She-Leveque(1994) scalings corresponding to the two-dimensional dissipative structures,and this result does not change with the Mach number either. In contrast to $v$which exhibits different scaling parallel and perpendicular to the localmagnetic field, the scaling of $u$ is similar in both directions. In addition,we find that the peaks of density create a hierarchy in which both physical andcolumn densities decrease with the scale in accordance to the Fleck (1996)predictions. This hierarchy can be related ubiquitous small ionized and neutralstructures (SINS) in the interstellar gas. We believe that studies ofstatistics of the column density peaks can provide both consistency check forthe turbulence velocity studies and insight into supersonic turbulence, whenthe velocity information is not available.
label: human

text: Compressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence plays a crucial role in many astrophysical environments, where strong magnetic fields and supersonic flows coexist. This study investigates the scaling relations in compressible MHD turbulence through high-resolution isothermal numerical simulations of strongly magnetized plasmas. The simulations reveal that the density-weighted velocity field, defined as \( v_l = \rho^{1/3} v \), exhibits a Kolmogorov-like spectrum with a power-law index of approximately -5/3 in the inertial range for high sonic Mach numbers. This finding aligns closely with the predictions of the Fleck model originally developed for compressible hydrodynamic turbulence. In strongly magnetized regimes, Alfvén and slow modes dominate the cascade, displaying scalings and anisotropies similar to those in incompressible MHD turbulence, following the Goldreich-Sridhar model. Fast modes, however, show more isotropic behavior with a shallower spectrum, consistent with acoustic turbulence scaling. The hierarchy of density peaks observed in the simulations decreases with scale in accordance with Fleck's theoretical expectations for both volume and column densities. These density structures may correspond to observed small-scale ionized and neutral features in the interstellar medium. Weak correlations are found between enhancements in magnetic field strength and density, suggesting limited direct coupling in certain regimes.
label: llm

text: We present a nonrelativistic theory for the quantum mechanical description oflongitudinal atomic beam spin echo experiments, where a beam of neutral atomsis subjected to static electric and magnetic fields. The atomic wave functionis the solution of a matrix-valued Schroedinger equation and can be written assuperposition of local (atomic) eigenstates of the potential matrix. Theposition- and time-dependent amplitude function of each eigenstate representsan atomic wave packet and can be calculated in a series expansion with a masterformula that we derive. The zeroth order of this series expansion describes theadiabatic limit, whereas the higher order contributions contain the mixing ofthe eigenstates and the corresponding amplitude functions.  We give a tutorial for the theoretical description of longitudinal atomicbeam spin echo experiments and for the so-called Fahrplan model, which is avisualisation tool for the propagation of wave packets of different atomiceigenstates.  As an example for the application of our theory, we study parity violatinggeometric (Berry-)phases. In this context, we define geometric flux densities,which for certain field configurations can be used to illustrate geometricphases in a vector diagram. Considering an example with a specific fieldconfiguration, we prove the existence of a parity violating geometric phase.
label: human

text: In dieser Arbeit wird eine nichtrelativistische quantenmechanische Theorie für longitudinale Atomstrahl-Spinecho-Experimente entwickelt, bei denen ein Strahl neutraler Atome statische elektrische und magnetische Felder durchquert. Die atomare Wellenfunktion genügt einer matrixwertigen Schrödinger-Gleichung und kann als Superposition lokaler Eigenzustände der Potentialmatrix dargestellt werden. Es wird eine detaillierte Anleitung zur theoretischen Beschreibung solcher Experimente gegeben, einschließlich des sogenannten Fahrplanmodells, das die Schwerpunktsbewegung der Wellenpakete grafisch visualisiert. Die Propagation der Wellenpakete wird durch die unterschiedliche Aufspaltung der lokalen Eigenwerte der Potentialmatrix bestimmt. Als Anwendung der entwickelten Theorie werden paritätsverletzende geometrische Berry-Phasen in Atomen untersucht. Hierzu werden geometrische Flussdichten eingeführt, die eine anschauliche Darstellung der Berry-Phasen in speziellen Feldkonfigurationen mittels Vektordiagrammen ermöglichen. Anhand einer ausgewählten Feldkonfiguration wird die Existenz einer paritätsverletzenden geometrischen Phase explizit nachgewiesen. Diese Ergebnisse legen den Grundstein für potenzielle Messungen paritätsverletzender Effekte in Atomstrahl-Spinecho-Experimenten und eröffnen neue Perspektiven auf schwache Wechselwirkungen in atomaren Systemen.
label: llm

text: We study the connection between the appearance of a `metastable' behavior ofweakly chaotic orbits, characterized by a constant rate of increase of theTsallis q-entropy (Tsallis 1988), and the solutions of the variationalequations of motion for the same orbits. We demonstrate that the variationalequations yield transient solutions, lasting for long time intervals, duringwhich the length of deviation vectors of nearby orbits grows in time almost asa power-law. The associated power exponent can be simply related to theentropic exponent for which the q-entropy exhibits a constant rate of increase.This analysis leads to the definition of a new sensitive indicatordistinguishing regular from weakly chaotic orbits, that we call `Average PowerLaw Exponent' (APLE). We compare the APLE with other established indicators ofthe literature. In particular, we give examples of application of the APLE ina) a thin separatrix layer of the standard map, b) the stickiness region aroundan island of stability in the same map, and c) the web of resonances of a 4Dsymplectic map. In all these cases we identify weakly chaotic orbits exhibitingthe `metastable' behavior associated with the Tsallis q-entropy.
label: human

text: The paper investigates the connection between the production of Tsallis entropy and the dynamics of weakly chaotic orbits in Hamiltonian systems, where the largest Lyapunov exponent vanishes or is very small. It demonstrates that such orbits exhibit a metastable behavior characterized by a constant rate of increase in the Tsallis q-entropy (with q > 1), contrasting with the linear growth of Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy in strongly chaotic regimes. This behavior arises from the solutions of the variational equations of motion, which reveal power-law rather than exponential divergence of nearby trajectories. To quantify this weak chaoticity, the authors introduce a new indicator called the Average Power Law Exponent (APLE), derived from the time evolution of the Tsallis entropy production rate. The APLE is compared with established chaos indicators and applied to specific cases, including the thin separatrix layer and stickiness regions of the standard map, as well as the resonance web in a 4D symplectic map. In all examined scenarios, the APLE effectively identifies weakly chaotic orbits associated with the metastable Tsallis q-entropy growth.
label: llm

text: Aims. This work presents a new hydrodynamical algorithm to studyastrophysical detonations. A prime motivation of this development is thedescription of a carbon detonation in conditions relevant to superbursts, whichare thought to result from the propagation of a detonation front around thesurface of a neutron star in the carbon layer underlying the atmosphere.Methods. The algorithm we have developed is a finite-volume method inspired bythe original MUSCL scheme of van Leer (1979). The algorithm is of second-orderin the smooth part of the flow and avoids dimensional splitting. It is appliedto some test cases, and the time-dependent results are compared to thecorresponding steady state solution. Results. Our algorithm proves to be robustto test cases, and is considered to be reliably applicable to astrophysicaldetonations. The preliminary one-dimensional calculations we have performeddemonstrate that the carbon detonation at the surface of a neutron star is amultiscale phenomenon. The length scale of liberation of energy is $10^6$ timessmaller than the total reaction length. We show that a multi-resolutionapproach can be used to solve all the reaction lengths. This result will bevery useful in future multi-dimensional simulations. We present alsothermodynamical and composition profiles after the passage of a detonation in apure carbon or mixed carbon-iron layer, in thermodynamical conditions relevantto superbursts in pure helium accretor systems.
label: human

text: Superbursts are rare, long-duration X-ray bursts observed from accreting neutron stars, believed to arise from unstable carbon burning in deep oceanic layers. A key mechanism proposed for superbursts involves the lateral propagation of a detonation front through the carbon-rich layer beneath the helium atmosphere on the neutron star surface. This work introduces a novel hydrodynamical algorithm designed specifically for modeling such astrophysical detonations under extreme conditions. The algorithm employs a second-order accurate scheme in smooth flow regions while effectively capturing discontinuities without dimensional splitting. It incorporates reactive Euler equations coupled with nuclear burning and neutrino losses relevant to neutron star environments. Validation is performed through standard shock-tube tests and comparisons with analytical steady-state detonation solutions. The time-dependent simulations closely reproduce the expected steady-state profiles, confirming the algorithm's accuracy and stability. Preliminary one-dimensional simulations are conducted for carbon detonations in conditions mimicking pure helium-accreting systems. These reveal that the detonation structure involves multiple scales, from nuclear burning zones to broader hydrodynamic features. The multiscale nature implies challenges for resolution in future multidimensional studies. Post-detonation thermodynamic profiles exhibit sharp transitions in temperature and density across the front.
label: llm

text: The behavior of the angular velocity of a test particle moving in a stablecircular orbit in the vacuum on the brane is considered. In the brane worldscenario, the four dimensional effective Einstein equation acquire extra terms,called dark radiation and dark pressure, respectively, which arise from theembedding of the 3-brane in the bulk. A large number of independentobservations have shown that the rotational velocities of test particlesgravitating around galaxies tend, as a function of the distance from thegalactic center, toward constant values. By assuming a constant tangentialvelocity, the general solution of the vacuum gravitational field equations onthe brane can be obtained in an exact analytic form. This allows us to obtainthe explicit form of the projections of the bulk Weyl tensor on the brane, andthe equation of state of the dark pressure as a function of the dark radiation.The physical and geometrical quantities are expressed in terms ofobservable/measurable parameters, like the tangential velocity, the baryonicmass and the radius of the galaxy. We also analyze the dynamics of testparticles by using methods from the qualitative analysis of dynamical systems,by assuming a simple linear equation of state for the dark pressure. Theobtained results provide a theoretical framework for the observational testingat the extra-galactic scale of the predictions of the brane world models.
label: human

text: In brane world models, the effective four-dimensional Einstein equations on the brane include additional terms arising from the embedding of the 3-brane in a higher-dimensional bulk spacetime. These non-local bulk effects manifest as dark radiation and dark pressure terms, originating from the free gravitational field in the bulk. Observations of flat galactic rotation curves, where tangential velocities remain constant at large radii, traditionally require the presence of dark matter halos to explain the discrepancy with visible baryonic mass. This work proposes that these bulk gravitational effects can mimic the role of dark matter on galactic scales without invoking exotic particles. We analyze the behavior of test particles in stable circular orbits within the vacuum region on the brane, deriving the modified angular velocity profile influenced by the dark pressure term. The asymptotic form of the rotation curves naturally yields flat velocity profiles at large distances due to the specific radial dependence of the bulk-induced terms. Comparisons with observational data from spiral galaxies suggest that brane world predictions align well with measured rotation curves, providing a geometric alternative to particle dark matter and offering testable distinctions via gravitational lensing and extra-galactic dynamics.
label: llm

text: A generalization of the usual ideles group is proposed, namely, we constructcertain adelic complexes for sheaves of $K$-groups on schemes. More generally,such complexes are defined for any abelian sheaf on a scheme. We focus on thecase when the sheaf is associated to the presheaf of a homology theory withcertain natural axioms, satisfied by $K$-theory. In this case it is proven thatthe adelic complex provides a flasque resolution for the above sheaf and thatthe natural morphism to the Gersten complex is a quasiisomorphism. The mainadvantage of the new adelic resolution is that it is contravariant andmultiplicative in contrast to the Gersten resolution. In particular, thisallows to reprove that the intersection in Chow groups coincides up to signwith the natural product in the corresponding $K$-cohomology groups. Also, weshow that the Weil pairing can be expressed as a Massey triple product in$K$-cohomology groups with certain indices.
label: human

text: We propose a generalization of the classical idele group by constructing adelic complexes associated to sheaves of K-groups on arbitrary schemes. These adelic complexes are defined more broadly for any abelian sheaf on a scheme. Particular attention is devoted to the case where the sheaf arises from the presheaf of a homology theory satisfying specific natural axioms, as exemplified by algebraic K-theory. In this setting, we prove that the adelic complex yields a flasque (flabby) resolution of the corresponding sheaf on smooth varieties over an infinite perfect field. Furthermore, we establish that the canonical morphism from the adelic complex to the Gersten complex is a quasi-isomorphism. A key advantage of this adelic resolution lies in its contravariant and multiplicative properties, in contrast to the Gersten resolution. As an application, this framework allows us to recover the compatibility (up to sign) between intersection products in Chow groups and natural products in the associated K-cohomology groups.
label: llm

text: We analyze the properties of the shallow decay segment with a sample of 53long Swift GRBs. We show that the distributions of its characteristics arelog-normal or normal, and its isotropic X-ray energy (E_{iso,X}) is linearlycorrelated with the prompt gamma-ray energy, but with a steeper photon spectrumexcept for some X-ray flashes. No significant spectral evolution is observedfrom this phase to the follow-up phase, and the follow-up phase is usuallyconsistent with the external shock models, implying that this segment likelydue to a refreshed external shock. Within this scenario, the data are generallyconsistent with a roughly constant injection luminosity up to the end of thisphase $t_b$. A positive correlation between E_{iso, X} and t_b also favors thisscenario. Among the 13 bursts that have well-sampled optical light curves, 6have an optical break around t_b and the breaks are consistent with beingachromatic. However, the other 7 bursts either do not show an optical break orhave a break at a different epoch than t_b. This raises a concern to the energyinjection scenario, suggesting that the optical and X-ray emissions may not bethe same component at least for a fraction of bursts. There are 4 significantoutliers in the sample, and this shallow decau phase in these bursts isimmediately followed by a very steep decay after t_b, which is inconsistentwith any external shock model. The optical data of these bursts evolveindependently from the X-ray data. These X-ray plateaus likely have an internalorigin and demand continuous operation of a long-term GRB central engine. Weconclude that the observed shallow decay phase likely has diverse physicalorigins(Abridged).
label: human

text: The shallow decay segment, also known as the plateau phase, in the X-ray afterglows of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) observed by the Swift X-ray Telescope (XRT) remains a key puzzle in understanding post-prompt emission mechanisms. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of this segment using a sample of 53 long-duration GRBs detected by Swift prior to February 2007. The temporal and spectral properties of the shallow decay phase are systematically extracted from the XRT light curves. Distributions of key parameters, including the decay slope, break time, and isotropic X-ray energy release, are found to follow log-normal or normal distributions. A significant linear correlation is identified between the isotropic X-ray energy in the shallow segment (E_{iso,X}) and the prompt gamma-ray energy (E_{iso,γ}). However, the photon spectrum during the shallow decay is generally steeper than that of the prompt emission, with exceptions noted in some X-ray flash events. Optical afterglow data, where available, show independent temporal evolution from the X-ray light curves, suggesting possible chromatic breaks or distinct emission components. Most shallow decay segments transition smoothly to the subsequent normal decay phase, consistent with models involving energy injection into the external forward shock. Four outlier GRBs (060413, 060522, 060607A, and 070110) exhibit abrupt steep drops immediately following the shallow phase, incompatible with standard external shock predictions. These outliers display X-ray plateaus likely originating from internal processes, such as prolonged activity of the central engine. The independence of optical and X-ray behaviors in these cases further supports an internal origin for the plateau emission.
label: llm

text: Using in-medium hadron properties according to the Brown-Rho scaling due tothe chiral symmetry restoration at high densities and considering naturalnessof the coupling constants, we have newly constructed several relativisticmean-field Lagrangians with chiral limits. The model parameters are adjustedsuch that the symmetric part of the resulting equation of state at supra-normaldensities is consistent with that required by the collective flow data fromhigh energy heavy-ion reactions, while the resulting density dependence of thesymmetry energy at sub-saturation densities agrees with that extracted from therecent isospin diffusion data from intermediate energy heavy-ion reactions. Theresulting equations of state have the special feature of being soft atintermediate densities but stiff at high densities naturally. With theseconstrained equations of state, it is found that the radius of a 1.4$M_\odot$canonical neutron star is in the range of 11.9 km$\leq$R$\leq$13.1 km, and themaximum neutron star mass is around 2.0$M_\odot$ close to the recentobservations.
label: human

text: We present new relativistic mean-field models incorporating chiral limits, where in-medium hadron masses follow Brown-Rho scaling to reflect partial restoration of chiral symmetry at high densities, while ensuring naturalness in the meson-nucleon coupling constants. These models are calibrated to reproduce empirical properties of symmetric nuclear matter at saturation and constrained at high densities by collective flow data from heavy-ion collisions, yielding a moderately soft equation of state for isospin-symmetric matter. For isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter, the density dependence of the symmetry energy is adjusted to match constraints from isospin diffusion measurements in intermediate-energy heavy-ion reactions, resulting in a symmetry energy that increases mildly with density below saturation before softening at supranuclear densities. The resulting equation of state provides a consistent description of neutron-rich matter relevant to astrophysical applications, such as neutron star structure and heavy-ion reaction dynamics.
label: llm

text: Rotating deformed neutron stars are important potential sources forgroundbased gravitational-wave interferometers such as LIGO, GE0600 and VIRGO.One mechanism that may lead to significant non-asymmetries is the internalmagnetic field. It is well known that a magnetic star will not be sphericaland, if the magnetic axis is not aligned with the spin axis, the deformationwill lead to the emission of gravitational waves. The aim of this paper is todevelop a formalism that would allow us to model magnetically deformed stars,using both realistic equations of state and field configurations. As a firststep, we consider a set of simplified model problems. Focusing on dipolarfields, we determine the internal magnetic field which is consistent with agiven neutron star model. We then calculate the associated deformation. Weconclude by discussing the relevance of our results for currentgravitational-wave detectors and future prospects.
label: human

text: Neutron stars with strong internal magnetic fields experience significant deviations from spherical symmetry due to Lorentz forces acting on the stellar interior. This magnetic deformation induces a quadrupolar asymmetry, which, when misaligned with the rotation axis, can drive the emission of continuous gravitational waves detectable by ground-based interferometers. In this work, we develop a perturbative framework to model the equilibrium configurations of magnetically deformed neutron stars, incorporating realistic equations of state for dense nuclear matter. Focusing primarily on dipolar poloidal fields, we solve for self-consistent internal field structures that satisfy magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium conditions. The resulting deformations are quantified through the stellar ellipticity, which scales quadratically with magnetic field strength for moderate fields below the critical threshold. For mixed poloidal-toroidal configurations.
label: llm

text: Heteroepitaxial self-assembled quantum dots (SAQDs) will allow breakthroughsin electronics and optoelectronics. SAQDs are a result of Stranski-Krastanowgrowth whereby a growing planar film becomes unstable after an initial wettinglayer is formed. Common systems are Ge$_{x}$Si$_{1-x}$/Si andIn$_{x}$Ga$_{1-x}$As/GaAs. For applications, SAQD arrays need to be ordered.The role of crystal anisotropy, random initial conditions and thermalfluctuations in influencing SAQD order during early stages of SAQD formation isstudied through a simple stochastic model of surface diffusion. Surfacediffusion is analyzed through a linear and perturbatively nonlinear analysis.The role of crystal anisotropy in enhancing SAQD order is elucidated. It isalso found that SAQD order is enhanced when the deposited film is allowed toevolve at heights near the critical wetting surface height that marks the onsetof non-planar film growth.
label: human

text: Heteroepitaxial self-assembled quantum dots (SAQDs) hold significant promise for advancing electronics and optoelectronics due to their unique quantum confinement properties. These nanostructures form via the Stranski-Krastanow growth mode, in which a compressively strained planar film becomes unstable beyond a critical wetting layer thickness, leading to the spontaneous emergence of three-dimensional islands. Common material systems include Ge_x Si_{1-x} on Si and In_x Ga_{1-x} As on GaAs, where lattice mismatch drives the morphological transition. This work presents a linear stochastic model that extends prior deterministic approaches to predict the spatial ordering of SAQDs, incorporating thermal fluctuations as natural nucleation seeds rather than arbitrary initial roughness. Simulations reveal enhanced lateral order when film evolution occurs near the critical height for non-planar growth onset. These findings provide insights into controlling SAQD arrangements for improved uniformity and device performance.
label: llm

text: We present a systematic study of exclusive charmless nonleptonic two-body Bdecays including axial-vector mesons in the final state. We calculate branchingratios of B\to PA, VA and AA decays, where A, V and P denote an axial-vector, avector and a pseudoscalar meson, respectively. We assume naive factorizationhypothesis and use the improved version of the nonrelativistic ISGW quark modelfor form factors in B\to A transitions. We include contributions that arisefrom the effective \Delta B=1 weak Hamiltonian H_{eff}. The respectivefactorized amplitude of these decays are explicitly showed and their penguincontributions are classified. We find that decays B^-to a_1^0\pi^-,\barB^0\toa_1^{\pm}\pi^{\mp}, B^-\to a_1^-\bar K^0, \bar B^0\to a_1^+K^-, \bar B^0\tof_1\bar K^0, B^-\to f_1K^-, B^-\to K_1^-(1400)\etap, B^-\to b_1^-\bar K^{0},and \bar B^0\to b_1^+\pi^-(K^-) have branching ratios of the order of 10^{-5}.We also study the dependence of branching ratios for B \to K_1P(V,A) decays(K_1=K_1(1270),K_1(1400)) with respect to the mixing angle between K_A and K_B.
label: human

text: We present a systematic study of exclusive charmless nonleptonic two-body B decays involving axial-vector mesons in the final state. Within the framework of QCD factorization, we analyze the decay amplitudes for channels such as B → pseudoscalar-axial (PA), vector-axial (VA), and axial-axial (AA), where the axial-vector mesons include both $^3P_1$ and $^1P_1$ states. The calculation incorporates next-to-leading-order corrections in α_s, including vertex corrections, penguin contributions, and spectator scattering terms. Particular attention is given to the distinct decay constants and light-cone distribution amplitudes of axial-vector mesons, which differ significantly for the $^3P_1$ and $^1P_1$ multiplets due to their quark model assignments. Power-suppressed effects, such as weak annihilation and chirally-enhanced terms, are estimated to assess their impact on branching ratios and polarization fractions. Our predictions for branching ratios and CP asymmetries provide testable benchmarks for experiments at LHCb and Belle II, highlighting potential signatures of transverse polarization dominance in certain penguin-dominated modes.
label: llm

text: Cosmic rays produced in cluster accretion and merger shocks provide pressureto the intracluster medium (ICM) and affect the mass estimates of galaxyclusters. Although direct evidence for cosmic-ray ions in the ICM is stilllacking, they produce gamma-ray emission through the decay of neutral pionsproduced in their collisions with ICM nucleons. We investigate the capabilityof the Gamma-ray Large Area Space Telescope (GLAST) and imaging atmosphericCerenkov telescopes (IACTs) for constraining the cosmic-ray pressurecontribution to the ICM. We show that GLAST can be used to place stringentupper limits, a few per cent for individual nearby rich clusters, on the ratioof pressures of the cosmic rays and thermal gas. We further show that it ispossible to place tight (<~10%) constraints for distant (z <~ 0.25) clusters inthe case of hard spectrum, by stacking signals from samples of known clusters.The GLAST limits could be made more precise with the constraint on thecosmic-ray spectrum potentially provided by IACTs. Future gamma-rayobservations of clusters can constrain the evolution of cosmic-ray energydensity, which would have important implications for cosmological tests withupcoming X-ray and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect cluster surveys.
label: human

text: Cosmic rays accelerated at accretion and merger shocks in galaxy clusters contribute non-thermal pressure to the intracluster medium (ICM), potentially biasing hydrostatic mass estimates used in cosmological analyses. Although direct evidence for cosmic-ray ions remains elusive, their interactions with ICM protons produce neutral pions that decay into detectable gamma-ray emission. Current observations impose only loose constraints on this cosmic-ray component, but forthcoming gamma-ray telescopes such as GLAST (now Fermi) and imaging atmospheric Čerenkov telescopes (IACTs) are expected to provide significantly tighter limits or even detections from rich clusters. Improved gamma-ray measurements would enable precise quantification of cosmic-ray pressure support and its radial profile within clusters. By constraining the cosmic-ray energy density and its evolution with redshift, such observations will help mitigate systematic uncertainties in cluster mass calibrations. Ultimately, these advances will enhance the reliability of galaxy clusters as probes of cosmology, particularly for constraining dark energy through X-ray and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect surveys.
label: llm

text: A supersymmetric extension of the dynamical symmetry group $Sp^{B}(12,R)$ ofthe Interacting Vector Boson Model (IVBM), to the orthosymplectic group$OSp(2\Omega/12,R)$ is developed in order to incorporate fermion degrees offreedom into the nuclear dynamics and to encompass the treatment of odd massnuclei. The bosonic sector of the supergroup is used to describe the complexcollective spectra of the neighboring even-even nuclei and is considered as acore structure of the odd nucleus. The fermionic sector is represented by thefermion spin group $SO^{F}(2\Omega)\supset SU^{F}(2)$.  The so obtained, new exactly solvable limiting case is applied for thedescription of the nuclear collective spectra of odd mass nuclei. Thetheoretical predictions for different collective bands in three odd massnuclei, namely $^{157}Gd$, $^{173}Yb$ and $^{163}Dy$ from rare earth region arecompared with the experiment. The $B(E2)$ transition probabilities for the$^{157}Gd$ and $^{163}Dy$ between the states of the ground band are alsostudied. The important role of the symplectic structure of the model for theproper reproduction of the $B(E2)$ behavior is revealed. The obtained resultsreveal the applicability of the models extension.
label: human

text: The Interacting Vector Boson Model (IVBM), based on the symplectic algebra Sp(12,R), provides a framework for describing collective excitations in even-even nuclei through interacting vector bosons. This work extends the IVBM to odd-mass nuclei by incorporating a supersymmetric extension to the orthosymplectic group OSp(4/12,R), which couples fermionic degrees of freedom to the bosonic core. The bosonic sector describes the even-even core of neighboring nuclei, while the odd nucleon is treated as a fermion coupled to this core. Collective states in odd-mass nuclei emerge as a combination of bosonic vector excitations and single-particle fermionic modes. The model predicts energy spectra, including ground-state bands and excited collective bands, with good agreement to experimental data in regions such as the actinides. Electromagnetic transition rates and moments are calculated within the dynamical symmetry limits of the extended algebra. The approach highlights the role of symplectic structures in accommodating both rotational and transitional behaviors in odd-A systems. Overall, this extension demonstrates the versatility of the IVBM in unifying descriptions of even-even and odd-mass nuclear collective phenomena.
label: llm

text: In recent investigations, it has been found that conservation laws generallylead to precision limits on quantum computing. Lower bounds of the errorprobability have been obtained for various logic operations from thecommutation relation between the noise operator and the conserved quantity orfrom the recently developed universal uncertainty principle for thenoise-disturbance trade-off in general measurements. However, the problem ofobtaining the precision limit to realizing the quantum NOT gate has eluded asolution from these approaches. Here, we develop a new method for this problembased on analyzing the trace distance between the output state from therealization under consideration and the one from the ideal gate. Using themathematical apparatus of orthogonal polynomials, we obtain a general lowerbound on the error probability for the realization of the quantum NOT gate interms of the number of qubits in the control system under the conservation ofthe total angular momentum of the computational qubit plus the the controlsystem along the direction used to encode the computational basis. The lowerbound turns out to be more stringent than one might expect from previousresults. The new method is expected to lead to more accurate estimates forphysical realizations of various types of quantum computations underconservation laws, and to contribute to related problems such as the accuracyof programmable quantum processors.
label: human

text: The quantum NOT gate, represented by the Pauli X operator, is a fundamental unitary transformation in quantum information processing that flips computational basis states. However, its physical implementation in realistic systems is subject to constraints imposed by underlying conservation laws derived from continuous symmetries via Noether's theorem. This work investigates how such conservation laws—particularly additive ones like angular momentum or charge—limit the fidelity and repeatability of approximate realizations of the quantum NOT gate. We show that, in the presence of a conserved quantity that does not commute with the ideal gate, perfect unitary implementation is impossible without access to an ancillary system possessing unbounded variance in the conserved observable. Quantitative bounds are derived using extensions of the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem, revealing that the accuracy of the gate is fundamentally capped by the apparatus's resource limitations in the conserved quantity. These limits manifest as unavoidable noise or decoherence in physical platforms, such as spin systems under angular momentum conservation or charged qubits under gauge symmetries. Implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and the design of robust quantum gates in conserved systems are discussed, highlighting the need for resource-intensive ancillas to approach ideal performance.
label: llm

text: In the equilibrium statistical mechanics of classical Coulomb fluids, thelong-range tail of the Coulomb potential gives rise to the Stillinger-Lovettsum rules for the charge correlation functions. For the jellium model of mobileparticles of charge $q$ immersed in a neutralizing background, the fixing ofone of the $q$-charges induces a screening cloud of the charge density whosezeroth and second moments are determined just by the Stillinger-Lovett sumrules. In this paper, we generalize these sum rules to the screening cloudinduced around a pointlike guest charge $Z q$ immersed in the bulk interior ofthe 2D jellium with the coupling constant $\Gamma=\beta q^2$ ($\beta$ is theinverse temperature), in the whole region of the thermodynamic stability of theguest charge $Z>-2/\Gamma$. The derivation is based on a mapping technique ofthe 2D jellium at the coupling $\Gamma$ = (even positive integer) onto adiscrete 1D anticommuting-field theory; we assume that the final results remainvalid for all real values of $\Gamma$ corresponding to the fluid regime. Thegeneralized sum rules reproduce for arbitrary coupling $\Gamma$ the standardZ=1 and the trivial Z=0 results. They are also checked in the Debye-H\"uckellimit $\Gamma\to 0$ and at the free-fermion point $\Gamma=2$. The generalizedsecond-moment sum rule provides some exact information about possible signoscillations of the induced charge density in space.
label: human

text: In the equilibrium statistical mechanics of classical Coulomb fluids, the long-range nature of the Coulomb potential leads to exact Stillinger-Lovett sum rules governing charge correlations. In the two-dimensional jellium model, consisting of mobile point charges immersed in a uniform neutralizing background, these rules determine the zeroth and second moments of the screening cloud around a fixed particle. This work generalizes the Stillinger-Lovett sum rules to the induced charge density surrounding a pointlike guest charge of amplitude Zq placed in the bulk of the two-dimensional jellium, characterized by the coupling constant Γ = βq². The generalization applies within the thermodynamic stability region Z > -2/Γ, where collapse is avoided due to the logarithmic interaction. The derivation employs a mapping of the two-dimensional jellium at even integer couplings Γ onto a one-dimensional discrete anticommuting-field theory, with results extended analytically to the fluid regime. The generalized rules recover the standard cases for Z=1 (identical to jellium particles) and Z=0 (no perturbation). Verification in limiting cases, including the Debye-Hückel regime (Γ → 0) and the free-fermion point (Γ=2), confirms consistency, while the second-moment rule yields insights into potential sign oscillations in the spatial profile of the induced charge density.
label: llm

text: We consider boundary Harnack inequalities for regional fractional Laplacianwhich are generators of censored stable-like processes on G taking\kappa(x,y)/|x-y|^{n+\alpha}dxdy, x,y\in G as the jumping measure. When G is aC^{1,\beta-1} open set, 1<\alpha<\beta\leq 2 and \kappa\inC^{1}(\overline{G}\times \overline{G}) bounded between two positive numbers, weprove a boundary Harnack inequality giving dist(x,\partial G)^{\alpha-1} orderdecay for harmonic functions near the boundary. For a C^{1,\beta-1} open setD\subset \overline{D}\subset G, 0<\alpha\leq (1\vee\alpha)<\beta\leq 2, weprove a boundary Harnack inequality giving dist(x,\partial D)^{\alpha/2} orderdecay for harmonic functions near the boundary. These inequalities aregeneralizations of the known results for the homogeneous case on C^{1,1} opensets. We also prove the boundary Harnack inequality for regional fractionalLaplacian on Lipschitz domain.
label: human

text: This paper investigates boundary Harnack inequalities for the regional fractional Laplacian, a nonlocal operator defined by restricting jumps to within a domain and serving as the infinitesimal generator of censored stable-like processes with jumping kernel \(\kappa(x,y)/|x-y|^{n+\alpha}\). For sufficiently smooth open sets, specifically \(C^{1,\beta-1}\) domains where \(1 < \beta \leq 2\), we establish that positive harmonic functions vanishing on a portion of the boundary exhibit comparable decay rates near that boundary. In particular, for a subdomain \(D\) contained in a larger domain \(G\), the boundary Harnack inequality holds with a decay order of \(\mathrm{dist}(x, \partial D)^{\alpha/2}\) for such harmonic functions. These results extend previous findings for the homogeneous case on \(C^{1,1}\) domains and inhomogeneous kernels. The proofs rely on probabilistic techniques involving Carleson-type estimates and interior Harnack inequalities, with potential applications to more general Markov operators.
label: llm

text: We present deep optical and infrared observations of the short duration GRB050906. Although no X-ray or optical/IR afterglow was discovered to deeplimits, the error circle of the GRB (as derived from the Swift BAT) is unusualincontaining the relatively local starburst galaxy IC328. This makes GRB 050906a candidate burst from a soft-gamma repeater, similar to the giant flare fromSGR 1806-20. The probability of chance alignment of a given BAT position withsuch a galaxy is small (<1%), although the size of the error circle (2.6arcminute radius) is such that a higher-z origin can't be ruled out. Indeed,the error circle also includes a moderately rich galaxy cluster at z=0.43,which is a plausible location for the burst given the apparent preference thatshort GRBs have for regions of high mass density. No residual optical orinfrared emission has been observed, either in the form of an afterglow orlater time emission from any associated supernova-like event. We discuss theconstraints these limits place on the progenitor of GRB 050906 based on theexpected optical signatures from both SGRs and merging compact object systems.
label: human

text: We present deep optical and infrared observations of the short-duration gamma-ray burst GRB 050906, detected by the Swift Burst Alert Telescope. No X-ray, optical, or infrared afterglow was identified despite sensitive follow-up searches to deep limiting magnitudes. The refined BAT error circle is notable for encompassing the nearby starburst galaxy IC 328 (also known as IC 0327) at a distance of approximately 132 Mpc. This positional coincidence raises the possibility that GRB 050906 originated as a giant flare from a soft gamma repeater within this galaxy, analogous to the 2004 flare from SGR 1806-20. Alternatively, the error circle overlaps a galaxy cluster at redshift z = 0.43, consistent with the observed tendency of short-duration GRBs to occur in regions of elevated stellar mass density, potentially favoring a compact object merger progenitor. No transient residual emission was detected in late-time imaging, ruling out bright afterglows or supernova-like rebrightening events. These non-detections impose stringent constraints on progenitor models, particularly limiting the likelihood of significant kilonova emission from neutron star mergers or optical signatures from magnetar flares.
label: llm

text: We present optical UBVRI sky brightness measures from 1992 through 2006. Thedata are based on CCD imagery obtained with the CTIO 0.9-m, 1.3-m, and 1.5-mtelescopes. The B- and V-band data are in reasonable agreement withmeasurements previously made at Mauna Kea, though on the basis of a smallnumber of images per year there are discrepancies for the years 1992 through1994. Our CCD-based data are not significantly different than values obtainedat Cerro Paranal. We find that the yearly averages of V-band sky brightness arebest correlated with the 10.7-cm solar flux taken 5 days prior to the skybrightness measures. This implies an average speed of 350 km/sec for the solarwind. While we can measure an enhancement of the night sky levels over LaSerena 10 degrees above the horizon, at elevation angles above 45 degrees wefind no evidence that the night sky brightness at Cerro Tololo is affected byartificial light of nearby towns and cities.
label: human

text: We present optical UBVRI sky brightness measurements at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO) spanning from 1992 to 2006. These data were derived from CCD imagery acquired using the CTIO 0.9-m, 1.3-m, and 1.5-m telescopes. The B- and V-band measurements show reasonable agreement with prior observations at Mauna Kea, although discrepancies exist for the years 1992–1994 due to limited sampling in those early periods. Our CCD-derived values across all bands are not significantly different from contemporaneous measurements at Cerro Paranal. Analysis of yearly averages reveals natural variations potentially correlated with solar activity, as indicated by comparisons with 10.7-cm solar flux data. While an enhancement in night-sky brightness is detectable at low elevation angles (10°) toward the nearby city of La Serena, no significant artificial light contribution is evident at zenith or elevation angles above 45°. These findings suggest that CTIO maintained excellent dark-sky conditions over the 15-year period, with minimal impact from regional urban growth.
label: llm

text: We study the prospects for detecting Weakly Interacting Massive Particles(WIMPs), in a number of phenomenological scenarios, with a detector composed ofa target simultaneously sensitive to both spin-dependent and spin-independentcouplings, as is the case of COUPP (Chicagoland Observatory for UndergroundParticle Physics). First, we show that sensitivity to both couplings optimizeschances of initial WIMP detection. Second, we demonstrate that in case ofdetection, comparison of the signal on two complementary targets, such as inCOUPP CF3I and C4F10 bubble chambers, allows a significantly more precisedetermination of the dark matter axial and scalar couplings. This strategywould provide crucial information on the nature of the WIMPs, and possiblyallow discrimination between neutralino and Kaluza-Klein dark matter.
label: human

text: We study the prospects for identifying weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) through direct detection experiments sensitive to both spin-independent (scalar) and spin-dependent (axial) couplings to nucleons. Sensitivity to both types of interactions significantly enhances the probability of initial WIMP detection across a wide range of phenomenological scenarios, including neutralino dark matter models where one coupling may dominate or suppress the signal in single-target experiments. Upon detection, employing complementary nuclear targets—such as fluorine-rich (e.g., CF₃I) and carbon-rich (e.g., C₄F₁₀) bubble chambers—allows for a comparative analysis of recoil rates. This combined measurement enables a substantially more precise determination of the relative strengths of the axial and scalar couplings.
label: llm

text: We present a search for the decay B+ -> tau+ nu using 383x10^6 BBbar pairscollected at the Y(4S) resonance with the BABAR detector at the SLAC PEP-IIB-Factory. A sample of events with one reconstructed semileptonic B decay (B--> D0 l nu X)) is selected, and in the recoil a search for B+ -> tau+ nu isperformed. The tau is identified in the following channels: tau+ -> e nu nubar,tau+ -> mu nu nubar, tau+ -> pi+ nu, and tau+ -> pi+ pi0 nu. We measure abranching fraction of B(B+ -> tau+ nu)=(0.9 +- 0.6(stat.) +- 0.1(syst.)) x10^-4. In the absence of a significant signal, we calculate an upper limit atthe 90% confidence level of B(B+ -> tau+ nu) < 1.7 x 10^-4. We calculate theproduct of the B meson decay constant f_B and |V_ub| to be f_B x |V_ub| =(7.2^{+2.0}_{-2.8}(stat.) +- 0.2 (syst.)) x 10^-4 GeV.
label: human

text: The purely leptonic decay \(B^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau\) is a flavor-changing charged-current process mediated by the W boson in the Standard Model (SM) at tree level. This decay is helicity-suppressed due to the small tau lepton mass relative to the B meson mass, resulting in a predicted SM branching fraction on the order of \(10^{-4}\). The branching ratio depends sensitively on the CKM matrix element \(|V_{ub}|\) and the B meson decay constant \(f_B\), providing a probe of these fundamental parameters. Experimental searches for this mode are challenging because the signal involves multiple neutrinos, leading to significant missing energy and reliance on tagging the accompanying B meson in \(e^+e^-\) collisions at the \(\Upsilon(4S)\) resonance. Previous measurements by the BaBar and Belle collaborations have reported evidence for the decay, with branching fractions consistent with SM expectations within uncertainties.
label: llm

text: We prove the following theorem about relative entropy of quantum states."Substate theorem: Let rho and sigma be quantum states in the same Hilbertspace with relative entropy S(rho|sigma) = Tr rho (log rho - log sigma) = c.Then for all epsilon > 0, there is a state rho' such that the trace distance||rho' - rho||_t = Tr sqrt{(rho' - rho)^2} <= epsilon, andrho'/2^{O(c/epsilon^2)} <= sigma."  It states that if the relative entropy of rho and sigma is small, then thereis a state rho' close to rho, i.e. with small trace distance ||rho' - rho||_t,that when scaled down by a factor 2^{O(c)} `sits inside', or becomes a`substate' of, sigma. This result has several applications in quantumcommunication complexity and cryptography. Using the substate theorem, wederive a privacy trade-off for the set membership problem in the two-partyquantum communication model. Here Alice is given a subset A of [n], Bob aninput i in [n], and they need to determine if i in A.  "Privacy trade-off for set membership: In any two-party quantum communicationprotocol for the set membership problem, if Bob reveals only k bits ofinformation about his input, then Alice must reveal at least n/2^{O(k)} bits ofinformation about her input."  We also discuss relationships between various information theoreticquantities that arise naturally in the context of the substate theorem.
label: human

text: We introduce a novel theorem concerning the quantum relative entropy between two density operators ρ and σ acting on the same finite-dimensional Hilbert space. The theorem asserts that if the relative entropy S(ρ ‖ σ) is bounded above by a constant c, then there exists a density operator ρ' close to ρ in trace distance such that ρ'/2^{O(c)} is a substate of σ. This substate property provides an operational interpretation of bounded relative entropy in terms of approximate embedding. The proof relies on constructive techniques involving purification and careful control of entropy distortions. We establish precise bounds on the trace distance between ρ and ρ' as well as the scaling factor required for the substate inclusion. This result strengthens prior inequalities relating relative entropy to trace distance and fidelity. As an application, we consider privacy aspects in two-party quantum communication protocols. Specifically, for the set membership problem, where Alice holds a subset and Bob an index, we derive a privacy trade-off: if Bob reveals only k bits about his input (measured via relative entropy), Alice must reveal at least n/2^{O(k)} bits about hers in any correct protocol. This demonstrates the utility of the theorem in bounding information leakage in quantum interactive settings.
label: llm

text: This is the second part of an article about q-deformed analogs of spinorcalculus. The considerations refer to quantum spaces of physical interest, i.e.q-deformed Euclidean space in three or four dimensions as well as q-deformedMinkowski space. The Clifford algebras corresponding to these quantum spacesare treated. Especially, their commutation relations and their Hopf structuresare written down. Bases of the four-dimensional Clifford algebras areconstructed and their properties are discussed. Matrix representations of theClifford algebras lead to q-deformed Dirac-matrices for the four-dimensionalquantum spaces. Moreover, q-analogs of the four-dimensional spin matrices arepresented. A very complete set of trace relations and rearrangement formulaeconcerning spin and Dirac-matrices is given. Dirac spinors together with theirbilinear covariants are defined. Their behavior under q-deformed Lorentztransformation is discussed in detail.
label: human

text: This paper presents the second part of a comprehensive study on q-deformed analogs of classical spinor calculus, focusing on quantum spaces of direct physical relevance. The analysis centers on q-deformed Euclidean spaces in three and four dimensions, as well as q-deformed Minkowski space. The corresponding Clifford algebras for these noncommutative spaces are systematically constructed and investigated. Matrix representations of these Clifford algebras are derived, yielding explicit q-deformed Dirac matrices suitable for four-dimensional quantum spaces. Furthermore, q-analogues of the conventional four-dimensional spin matrices are introduced and analyzed in detail. A comprehensive collection of trace relations and rearrangement formulae involving both the q-deformed spin and Dirac matrices is provided to facilitate practical computations. Dirac spinors are defined within this q-deformed framework, extending the classical concept to the noncommutative setting.
label: llm
