text: The extended Hubbard Hamiltonian is a widely accepted model for uncoveringthe effects of strong correlations on the phase diagram of low-dimensionalsystems, and a variety of theoretical techniques have been applied to it. Inthis paper the world-line quantum Monte Carlo method is used to study spin,charge, and bond order correlations of the one-dimensional extended Hubbardmodel in the presence of coupling to the lattice. A static alternating latticedistortion (the ionic Hubbard model) leads to enhanced charge density wavecorrelations at the expense of antiferromagnetic order. When the latticedegrees of freedom are dynamic (the Hubbard-Holstein model), we show that asimilar effect occurs even though the charge asymmetry must arisespontaneously. Although the evolution of the total energy with lattice couplingis smooth, the individual components exhibit sharp crossovers at the phaseboundaries. Finally, we observe a tendency for bond order in the region betweenthe charge and spin density wave phases.
label: human

text: The one-dimensional extended Hubbard model, incorporating on-site repulsion \(U\) and nearest-neighbor repulsion \(V\), serves as a fundamental framework for investigating strongly correlated electrons in low-dimensional systems. This study employs the world-line quantum Monte Carlo method to examine spin, charge, and bond-order correlations, with particular attention to the influence of lattice coupling. We compare scenarios where lattice distortions are imposed statically, as in the ionic Hubbard model, against cases where phonons introduce dynamic lattice degrees of freedom, as in the Hubbard-Holstein model. A static alternating lattice distortion enhances charge-density-wave correlations while suppressing antiferromagnetic spin order. In contrast, dynamic lattice fluctuations allow spontaneous charge asymmetry to emerge, yielding a similar enhancement of charge correlations at the expense of spin order. These findings highlight the distinct roles of static versus dynamic fluctuations in shaping the competition between charge and spin ordering in correlated one-dimensional systems.
label: llm

text: In the absence of direct kinematic measurements, the mass of an accretingblack hole is sometimes inferred from the X-ray spectral parameters of itsaccretion disk; specifically, from the temperature and normalization of adisk-blackbody model fit. Suitable corrections have to be introduced when theaccretion rate approaches or exceeds the Eddington limit. We summarizephenomenological models that can explain the very high state, with apparentlyhigher disk temperatures and lower inner-disk radii. Conversely, ultraluminousX-ray sources often contain cooler disks with large characteristic radii. Weintroduce another phenomenological model for this accretion state. We arguethat a standard disk dominates the radiative output for radii larger than acharacteristic transition radius R_c ~ mdot x R_{ISCO}, where mdot is theaccretion rate in Eddington units and R_{ISCO} is the innermost stable orbit.For R_{ISCO} < R < R_c, most of the accretion power is released via non-thermalprocesses. We predict the location of such sources in a luminosity-temperatureplot. We conclude that black holes with masses ~ 50-100 Msun accreting at mdot~ 10-20 may explain the X-ray properties of many ULXs.
label: human

text: Determining black hole masses in accreting systems without direct dynamical measurements relies on modeling the thermal emission from accretion disks observed in soft X-ray spectra. The soft X-ray band often reveals a prominent thermal component, typically fitted with disk-blackbody (diskbb) models, which approximate the multicolor blackbody emission from a thin accretion disk. In stellar-mass black hole X-ray binaries, the inner disk temperature peaks around 1 keV in high/soft states, scaling inversely with black hole mass due to the larger gravitational radius in more massive systems. For ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs), however, the observed soft thermal components are cooler (kT_in ≈ 0.1–0.2 keV) and, if interpreted as standard disk emission, imply intermediate-mass black holes (10^3–10^4 M_⊙) when combined with high luminosities. Standard diskbb fits assume sub-Eddington accretion and a fixed inner radius at the innermost stable circular orbit, but these break down near or above the Eddington limit, where advection and Comptonization dominate. Corrections for color temperature hardening (f_col ≈ 1.7–2.6) and super-Eddington effects, such as those in slim disk or extended diskbb models, are essential to avoid underestimating masses.
label: llm

text: We study the elasticity of random stiff fiber networks. The elastic responseof the fibers is characterized by a central force stretching stiffness as wellas a bending stiffness that acts transverse to the fiber contour. Previousstudies have shown that this model displays an anomalous elastic regime wherethe stretching mode is fully frozen out and the elastic energy is completelydominated by the bending mode. We demonstrate by simulations and scalingarguments that, in contrast to the bending dominated \emph{elastic energy}, theequally important \emph{elastic forces} are to a large extent stretchingdominated. By characterizing these forces on microscopic, mesoscopic andmacroscopic scales we find two mechanisms of how forces are transmitted in thenetwork. While forces smaller than a threshold $F_c$ are effectively balancedby a homogeneous background medium, forces larger than $F_c$ are found to beheterogeneously distributed throughout the sample, giving rise to highlylocalized force-chains known from granular media.
label: human

text: We investigate the elastic properties of random networks composed of stiff fibers, where individual fibers exhibit both central-force stretching stiffness and transverse bending stiffness. Previous work has established that these networks display an anomalous elastic regime in which stretching modes are effectively frozen, and the total elastic energy is dominated by bending contributions. Here, we focus on the distribution of internal forces under applied shear deformation. Simulations and scaling arguments reveal that, despite the bending-dominated energy, the elastic forces transmitted along fibers are predominantly stretching in nature. Force transmission occurs via two distinct mechanisms: smaller forces below a characteristic threshold \(F_c\) are balanced within a homogeneous effective medium, while larger forces exceed this threshold and propagate heterogeneously. These supra-threshold forces form highly localized structures known as force chains, analogous to those observed in granular materials, leading to strong spatial inhomogeneities in the stress distribution.
label: llm

text: On large angular scales, the polarization of the CMB contains informationabout the evolution of the average ionization during the epoch of reionization.Interpretation of the polarization spectrum usually requires the assumption ofa fixed functional form for the evolution, e.g. instantaneous reionization. Wedevelop a model-independent method where a small set of principal componentscompletely encapsulate the effects of reionization on the large-angle E-modepolarization for any reionization history within an adjustable range inredshift. Using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, we apply this approach toboth the 3-year WMAP data and simulated future data. WMAP data constrain twoprincipal components of the reionization history, approximately correspondingto the total optical depth and the difference between the contributions to theoptical depth at high and low redshifts. The optical depth is consistent withthe constraint found in previous analyses of WMAP data that assumeinstantaneous reionization, with only slightly larger uncertainty due to theexpanded set of models. Using the principal component approach, WMAP data alsoplace a 95% CL upper limit of 0.08 on the contribution to the optical depthfrom redshifts z>20. With improvements in polarization sensitivity andforeground modeling, approximately five of the principal components canultimately be measured. Constraints on the principal components, which probethe entire reionization history, can test models of reionization, providemodel-independent constraints on the optical depth, and detect signatures ofhigh-redshift reionization.
label: human

text: The large-scale E-mode polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) provides valuable information about the evolution of the intergalactic medium's ionization during the epoch of reionization. Traditional analyses of this signal typically rely on simplified assumptions, such as instantaneous reionization at a single redshift, which can bias interpretations of the data. In this work, we present a model-independent approach that employs a small set of principal components to fully encapsulate the effects of arbitrary reionization histories on large-angle CMB polarization within a specified redshift range. These principal components are derived from the kernel relating the ionization fraction evolution to the observed polarization power spectrum. Using Markov Chain Monte Carlo techniques, we apply this framework to the three-year WMAP data, demonstrating that the measurements constrain primarily the first two principal components. These components predominantly correspond to the total optical depth to reionization and the difference in contributions to this optical depth from high and low redshifts. The inferred total optical depth remains consistent with previous instantaneous reionization analyses, albeit with a modestly increased uncertainty due to the broader model space considered. Application of the principal component method further yields a 95% confidence upper limit of 0.08 on the contribution to the optical depth from redshifts z > 20. With anticipated advancements in polarization sensitivity and foreground subtraction, future observations are expected to constrain approximately five principal components.
label: llm

text: We present a numerical method for spatially 1.5-dimensional andtime-dependent studies of accretion disks around black holes, that isoriginated from a combination of the standard pseudo-spectral method and theadaptive domain decomposition method existing in the literature, but with anumber of improvements in both the numerical and physical senses. Inparticular, we introduce a new treatment for the connection at the interfacesof decomposed subdomains, construct an adaptive function for the mappingbetween the Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto collocation points and the physicalcollocation points in each subdomain, and modify the over-simplified1-dimensional basic equations of accretion flows to account for the effects ofviscous stresses in both the azimuthal and radial directions. Our method isverified by reproducing the best results obtained previously by Szuszkiewicz &Miller on the limit-cycle behavior of thermally unstable accretion disks withmoderate viscosity. A new finding is that, according to our computations, theBernoulli function of the matter in such disks is always and everywherenegative, so that outflows are unlikely to originate from these disks. We areencouraged to study the more difficult case of thermally unstable accretiondisks with strong viscosity, and wish to report our results in a subsequentpaper.
label: human

text: We present a novel numerical method for time-dependent, spatially 1.5-dimensional modeling of accretion disks around black holes, combining an enhanced pseudo-spectral approach with adaptive domain decomposition to achieve high accuracy across large radial extents. This method incorporates improved subdomain interface treatments, adaptive mapping of Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto points to physical coordinates, and refined equations accounting for viscous stresses in both azimuthal and radial directions. The technique is validated by accurately reproducing prior limit-cycle oscillations in thermally unstable disks with moderate viscosity, as previously reported by Szuszkiewicz & Miller. Simulations reveal that the Bernoulli function remains negative throughout such disks, indicating that outflows are unlikely under these conditions. Future work will extend the approach to explore the more challenging regime of thermally unstable disks with strong viscosity.
label: llm

text: An information-theoretic approach is proposed to watermark embedding anddetection under limited detector resources. First, we consider the attack-freescenario under which asymptotically optimal decision regions in theNeyman-Pearson sense are proposed, along with the optimal embedding rule.Later, we explore the case of zero-mean i.i.d. Gaussian covertext distributionwith unknown variance under the attack-free scenario. For this case, we proposea lower bound on the exponential decay rate of the false-negative probabilityand prove that the optimal embedding and detecting strategy is superior to thecustomary linear, additive embedding strategy in the exponential sense.Finally, these results are extended to the case of memoryless attacks andgeneral worst case attacks. Optimal decision regions and embedding rules areoffered, and the worst attack channel is identified.
label: human

text: An information-theoretic framework is proposed for optimal watermark embedding and detection when the detector operates under constrained computational resources, limiting the complexity of feasible detection strategies. In the absence of attacks, asymptotically optimal decision regions are derived in the Neyman-Pearson sense, maximizing the false-negative error exponent while constraining the false-positive rate, accompanied by the corresponding optimal embedding rule that outperforms traditional linear additive embedding strategies in the exponential sense. These results are extended to scenarios involving zero-mean i.i.d. Gaussian covertext with unknown variance, demonstrating robust performance under realistic host signal assumptions. The approach highlights the trade-off between detection reliability and resource limitations, providing universal asymptotically optimal rules based on low-complexity statistics such as second-order joint empirical moments.
label: llm

text: The low-luminosity black hole Sgr A* provides a testbed for models ofRadiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows (RIAFs). Recent sub-millimeter linearpolarization measurements of Sgr A* have provided evidence that the electronsin the accretion flow are relativistic over a large range of radii. Here, weshow that these high temperatures result in elliptical plasma normal modes.Thus, polarized millimeter and sub-millimeter radiation emitted within RIAFswill undergo generalized Faraday rotation, a cyclic conversion between linearand circular polarization. This effect will not depolarize the radiation evenif the rotation measure is extremely high. Rather, the beam will take on thelinear and circular polarization properties of the plasma normal modes. As aresult, polarization measurements of Sgr A* in this frequency regime willconstrain the temperature, density and magnetic profiles of RIAF models.
label: human

text: Radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAFs) are hot, optically thin plasmas that accrete onto low-luminosity black holes, such as Sagittarius A* at the Galactic center, with much of the gravitational energy advected inward rather than radiated away. Recent submillimeter linear polarization observations of Sgr A* indicate that relativistic electrons persist across a broad radial range in these flows. In the millimeter and submillimeter regimes, polarized synchrotron emission from RIAFs undergoes generalized Faraday rotation, leading to cyclic conversion between linear and circular polarization modes. Unlike classical Faraday rotation, this process does not depolarize the radiation even at very high rotation measures, preserving information about the plasma properties. Instead, the emergent beam adopts the polarization characteristics of the plasma's normal modes. Consequently, detailed polarization measurements in this frequency range can tightly constrain the electron temperature.
label: llm

text: In this paper we study magnetization excitations induced in a thin extendedfilm by a spin-polarized dc-current injected through a point contact in thecurrent-perpendicular-to-plane (CPP) geometry. Using full-scale micromagneticsimulations, we demonstrate that in addition to the oscillations of thepropagating wave type, there exist also two localized oscillation modes. Thefirst localized mode has a relatively homogeneous magnetization structure ofits kernel and corresponds to the so called 'bullet' predicted analytically bySlavin and Tiberkevich (Phys. Rev. Lett., 95 (2005) 237201). Magnetizationpattern of the second localized mode kernel is highly inhomogeneous, leading toa much smaller power of magnetoresistance oscillations caused by this mode. Wehave also studied the influence of a non-linear damping for this system andhave found the following main qualitative effects: (i) the appearance offrequency jumps within the existence region of the propagating wave mode and(ii) the narrowing of the current region where the 'bullet' mode exists, untilthis mode completely disappears for a sufficiently strong non-linear damping.
label: human

text: Abstract This study investigates magnetization excitations induced in a thin extended ferromagnetic film by a spin-polarized dc current injected through a point contact in the current-perpendicular-to-plane geometry, employing full micromagnetic simulations. In addition to extended propagating spin-wave modes, two distinct localized oscillation modes are identified: a primary "bullet" mode characterized by a relatively homogeneous core and a secondary mode exhibiting a highly inhomogeneous magnetization pattern, resulting in significantly reduced magnetoresistance oscillation power. The transitions between these modes manifest as abrupt frequency and power jumps, indicative of mode-hopping phenomena as the spin-torque magnitude varies. Incorporation of nonlinear damping effects profoundly alters the system behavior, introducing frequency discontinuities within the propagating wave mode regime and progressively narrowing the current range supporting the bullet mode. For sufficiently strong nonlinear damping, the bullet mode is completely suppressed. These findings highlight the critical interplay between spatial mode localization.
label: llm

text: This paper provides an introduction to some stochastic models of latticegases out of equilibrium and a discussion of results of various kinds obtainedin recent years. Although these models are different in their microscopicfeatures, a unified picture is emerging at the macroscopic level, applicable,in our view, to real phenomena where diffusion is the dominating physicalmechanism. We rely mainly on an approach developed by the authors based on thestudy of dynamical large fluctuations in stationary states of open systems. Theoutcome of this approach is a theory connecting the non equilibriumthermodynamics to the transport coefficients via a variational principle. Thisleads ultimately to a functional derivative equation of Hamilton-Jacobi typefor the non equilibrium free energy in which local thermodynamic variables arethe independent arguments. In the first part of the paper we give a detailedintroduction to the microscopic dynamics considered, while the second part,devoted to the macroscopic properties, illustrates many consequences of theHamilton-Jacobi equation. In both parts several novelties are included.
label: human

text: Stochastic interacting particle systems provide a fundamental framework for modeling non-equilibrium phenomena in lattice gases, where particles hop according to rates influenced by local configurations and external drives. These systems, often driven out of equilibrium by boundary reservoirs or applied fields, exhibit persistent currents and long-range correlations absent in equilibrium settings. Despite diverse microscopic rules, a unified macroscopic description emerges through hydrodynamic limits, typically governed by diffusive or hyperbolic partial differential equations. Central to recent advances is the macroscopic fluctuation theory, which characterizes large deviations of density and current profiles in stationary non-equilibrium states. This approach reveals a variational structure linking transport coefficients to non-equilibrium thermodynamics via a Hamilton-Jacobi equation for the quasi-potential. Key features include non-local effects, such as power-law correlations in low dimensions, and additivity principles that simplify fluctuation functionals. The framework applies broadly to diffusive transport in physical systems and highlights open challenges in understanding generic non-equilibrium universality.
label: llm

text: Recent rapid localizations of short, hard gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) by theSwift and HETE satellites have led to the observation of the first afterglowsand the measurement of the first redshifts from this type of burst. Detectionof >100 GeV counterparts would place powerful constraints on GRB mechanisms.Seventeen short duration (< 5 s) GRBs detected by satellites occurred withinthe field of view of the Milagro gamma-ray observatory between 2000 January and2006 December. We have searched the Milagro data for >100 GeV counterparts tothese GRBs and find no significant emission correlated with these bursts. Dueto the absorption of high-energy gamma rays by the extragalactic backgroundlight (EBL), detections are only expected for redshifts less than ~0.5. Whilemost long duration GRBs occur at redshifts higher than 0.5, the opposite isthought to be true of short GRBs. Lack of a detected VHE signal thus allowssetting meaningful fluence limits. One GRB in the sample (050509b) has a likelyassociation with a galaxy at a redshift of 0.225, while another (051103) hasbeen tentatively linked to the nearby galaxy M81. Fluence limits are correctedfor EBL absorption, either using the known measured redshift, or computing thecorresponding absorption for a redshift of 0.1 and 0.5, as well as for the caseof z=0.
label: human

text: Short-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), typically lasting less than 5 seconds, are thought to originate from compact object mergers, such as neutron star-neutron star or neutron star-black hole systems, in contrast to long-duration GRBs associated with massive star collapses. Recent rapid localizations by satellites like Swift and HETE have enabled the detection of afterglows and redshift measurements for short GRBs, revealing a population potentially at lower redshifts compared to long GRBs. The Milagro gamma-ray observatory, a wide-field water Cherenkov detector sensitive to photons above ~100 GeV, offers high duty cycle monitoring of the northern sky, making it suitable for searching very high energy (VHE) emission from GRBs. Detection of VHE counterparts to short GRBs would provide stringent constraints on emission mechanisms, bulk Lorentz factors, and progenitor models. Between January 2000 and December 2006, seventeen short-duration GRBs detected by satellites occurred within Milagro's field of view. A detailed search of Milagro data for coincident >100 GeV emission from these bursts yielded no significant signals correlated with the GRB positions or times. Upper limits on VHE fluence were derived for each event, accounting for detector sensitivity and zenith angles. Due to pair-production absorption by the extragalactic background light, VHE detections are primarily feasible for bursts at redshifts z < ~0.
label: llm

text: We analyze fading interference relay networks where M single-antennasource-destination terminal pairs communicate concurrently and in the samefrequency band through a set of K single-antenna relays using half-duplextwo-hop relaying. Assuming that the relays have channel state information(CSI), it is shown that in the large-M limit, provided K grows fast enough as afunction of M, the network "decouples" in the sense that the individualsource-destination terminal pair capacities are strictly positive. Thecorresponding required rate of growth of K as a function of M is found to besufficient to also make the individual source-destination fading links convergeto nonfading links. We say that the network "crystallizes" as it breaks up intoa set of effectively isolated "wires in the air". A large-deviations analysisis performed to characterize the "crystallization" rate, i.e., the rate (as afunction of M,K) at which the decoupled links converge to nonfading links. Inthe course of this analysis, we develop a new technique for characterizing thelarge-deviations behavior of certain sums of dependent random variables. Forthe case of no CSI at the relay level, assuming amplify-and-forward relaying,we compute the per source-destination terminal pair capacity for M,K convergingto infinity, with K/M staying fixed, using tools from large random matrixtheory.
label: human

text: This paper investigates fading interference-limited relay networks consisting of M single-antenna source-destination pairs communicating concurrently via K single-antenna relays in a half-duplex two-hop fashion. Assuming relays possess channel state information (CSI), we demonstrate that in the asymptotic regime where M grows large, the network decouples if K scales sufficiently rapidly with M, yielding positive capacity for each individual pair. The required growth rate of K relative to M is characterized precisely. This scaling condition further ensures that the effective fading channels for each source-destination pair converge to deterministic nonfading links. We term this phenomenon "crystallization," whereby the highly interfered network fragments into a collection of effectively isolated virtual wires in the air. A novel large-deviations technique is developed to analyze the dependent random variables arising in the interference sums. For the case without relay CSI and using amplify-and-forward relaying, random matrix theory tools are employed to derive the per-pair capacity in the joint limit of M and K to infinity with fixed ratio K/M.
label: llm

text: Measurable spectra are theoretically very often derived from complicatedmany-body Green's functions. In this way, one calculates much more informationthan actually needed. Here we present an in principle exact approach toconstruct effective potentials and kernels for the direct calculation ofelectronic spectra. In particular, the potential that yields the spectralfunction needed to describe photoemission turns out to be dynamical but {\itlocal} and {\it real}. As example we illustrate this ``photoemissionpotential'' for sodium and aluminium, modelled as homogeneous electron gas, anddiscuss in particular its frequency dependence stemming from the nonlocality ofthe corresponding self-energy. We also show that our approach leads to a veryshort derivation of a kernel that is known to well describe absorption andenergy-loss spectra of a wide range of materials.
label: human

text: Measurable spectra in condensed matter physics are commonly obtained from many-body Green's functions, which often require computing excessive information beyond the directly observable quantities. This work introduces an exact theoretical framework to derive effective potentials and kernels that enable the direct computation of electronic spectra, bypassing the full complexity of Green's function approaches. By reformulating the nonlocal and complex self-energy operator, the method transforms spatial nonlocality into an equivalent frequency-dependent but spatially local description. Notably, for photoemission spectroscopy, the resulting effective potential is dynamical, local, and real-valued, directly yielding the spectral function. Applications to model solids, such as the homogeneous electron gas representing sodium and aluminum, demonstrate the frequency dependence of this "photoemission potential" arising purely from the underlying nonlocality of the self-energy.
label: llm

text: We report a structural and thermodynamic study of the "stuffed spin ice"material Ho2TiO5 (i.e., Ho2(Ti1.33Ho0.67)O6.67), comparing samples synthesizedthrough two different routes. Neutron powder diffraction and electrondiffraction reveal that the previously reported defect fluorite phase hasshort-range pyrochlore ordering, in that there are domains in which the Ho andHo/Ti sublattices are distinct. By contrast, a sample prepared through afloating zone method has long range ordering of these sublattices. Despite thedifferences in crystal structures, the two versions of Ho2TiO5 display similarmagnetic susceptibilities. Field dependent magnetization and measured recoveredentropies, however, show a difference between the two forms, suggesting thatthe magnetic properties of the stuffed pyrochlores depend on the localstructure.
label: human

text: We report a structural and thermodynamic investigation of the stuffed spin ice compound Ho₂TiO₅, equivalently formulated as Ho₂(Ti₁.₃₃Ho₀.₆₇)O₆.₆₇, using samples prepared via distinct synthesis methods. Neutron powder diffraction and electron diffraction analyses demonstrate that the material previously identified as a defect fluorite structure actually exhibits short-range pyrochlore ordering, characterized by nanoscale domains where the Ho and mixed Ho/Ti sublattices remain distinct. In contrast, samples produced by the floating zone technique display long-range pyrochlore ordering of these sublattices. Although the variants show comparable magnetic susceptibilities, differences emerge in field-dependent magnetization and recovered entropy measurements. These findings indicate that the magnetic behavior of stuffed pyrochlores is strongly influenced by local structural disorder.
label: llm

text: Initiated by Gromov, the study of holomorphic curves in symplectic manifoldshas been a powerfull tool in symplectic topology, however the moduli space ofholomorphic curves is often very difficult to find. A common technique is tostudy the limiting behavior of holomorphic curves in a degenerating family ofcomplex structures which corresponds to a kind of adiabatic limit. The categoryof exploded fibrations is an extension of the smooth category in which some ofthese degenerations can be described as smooth families.  The first part of this paper is devoted to defining exploded fibrations and aslightly more specialized category of exploded torus fibrations. Later sectionscontain the transverse interesction theory for exploded fibrations and someexamples of holomorphic curves in exploded torus fibrations, including a briefdiscussion of the relationship between tropical geometry and exploded torusfibrations. In the final section, the perturbation theory of holomorphic curvesin exploded torus fibrations is sketched.
label: human

text: This paper introduces the category of exploded fibrations, a novel extension of the smooth category designed to accommodate certain adiabatic degenerations of complex structures as smooth families. Exploded fibrations enable the description of limiting behaviors in degenerating families of holomorphic curves, particularly those arising in symplectic topology and Gromov-Witten theory. A specialized subcategory of exploded torus fibrations is defined, which captures degenerations relevant to tropical geometry and normal crossing singularities in algebraic families. The paper develops transverse intersection theory within the exploded category, providing tools for analyzing curve intersections in these generalized spaces. Examples of holomorphic curves in exploded torus fibrations are presented, illustrating their correspondence with tropical curves. Finally, a sketch of perturbation theory for holomorphic curves in exploded torus fibrations is outlined, laying groundwork for future compactness and regularity results.
label: llm

text: The vortex density of a rotating superfluid, divided by its particle mass,dictates the superfluid's angular velocity through the Feynman relation. Tofind how the Feynman relation applies to superfluid mixtures, we investigate arotating two-component Bose-Einstein condensate, composed of bosons withdifferent masses. We find that in the case of sufficiently strong interspeciesattraction, the vortex lattices of the two condensates lock and rotate at thedrive frequency, while the superfluids themselves rotate at two differentvelocities, whose ratio is the ratio between the particle mass of the twospecies. In this paper, we characterize the vortex-locked state, establish itsregime of stability, and find that it surives within a disk smaller than acritical radius, beyond which vortices become unbound, and the two Bose-gasrings rotate together at the frequency of the external drive.
label: human

text: We investigate the behavior of vortex lattices in a rotating two-component Bose-Einstein condensate consisting of bosons with unequal masses. The Feynman relation, which connects vortex density to superfluid angular velocity via particle mass, is generalized to this multicomponent system. For sufficiently strong interspecies attractive interactions, the vortex lattices in both components lock together, corotating rigidly at the external drive frequency. Remarkably, despite this lattice locking, the individual superfluid components rotate at distinct angular velocities, with their ratio precisely matching the inverse ratio of the particle masses.
label: llm

text: We present a study of eegamma and mumugamma events using 1109 (1009) pb-1 ofdata in the electron (muon) channel, respectively. These data were collectedwith the D0 detector at the Fermilab Tevatron ppbar Collider at sqrt(s) = 1.96TeV. Having observed 453 (515) candidates in the eegamma (mumugamma) finalstate, we measure the Zgamma production cross section for a photon withtransverse energy ET > 7 GeV, separation between the photon and leptons DeltaR(lgamma) > 0.7, and invariant mass of the di-lepton pair M(ll) > 30 GeV/c^2,to be 4.96 +/- 0.30(stat. + syst.) +/- 0.30(lumi.) pb, in agreement with thestandard model prediction of 4.74 +/- 0.22 pb. This is the most precise Zgammacross section measurement at a hadron collider. We set limits on anomaloustrilinear Zgammagamma and ZZgamma gauge boson couplings of -0.085 <h(30)^(gamma) < 0.084, -0.0053 < h(40)^(gamma) < 0.0054 and -0.083 < h(30)^(Z)< 0.082, -0.0053 < h(40)^(Z) < 0.0054 at the 95% C.L. for the form-factor scaleLambda = 1.2 TeV.
label: human

text: We present a study of Zγ production in proton-antiproton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of √s = 1.96 TeV, using data collected with the D0 detector at the Fermilab Tevatron Collider. The analysis focuses on events where the Z boson decays to electron or muon pairs (eeγ and μμγ final states). Candidate events are selected requiring a high-transverse-energy photon (E_T^γ > 7 GeV), significant separation between the photon and leptons (ΔR(l,γ) > 0.7), and an invariant mass of the dilepton pair greater than 30 GeV. A total of 453 (515) candidate events are observed in the electron (muon) channel. The measured Zγ production cross section is 4.96 ± 0.30 (stat. + syst.) ± 0.30 (lumi.) pb. This result agrees well with the standard model prediction of 4.74 ± 0.22 pb. This measurement represents the most precise determination of the Zγ cross section at a hadron collider to date. To probe for new physics, we set 95% confidence level limits on anomalous trilinear ZZγ and Zγγ gauge boson couplings, parameterized by h_{30,40}^{Z,γ} with a form-factor scale Λ = 1.
label: llm

text: Data assimilation refers to the process of obtaining an estimate of asystem's state using a model for the system's time evolution and a time seriesof measurements that are possibly noisy and incomplete. However, for practicalreasons, the high dimensionality of large spatiotemporally chaotic systemsprevents the use of classical data assimilation techniques. Here, via numericalcomputations on the paradigmatic example of large aspect ratio Rayleigh-Benardconvection, we demonstrate the applicability of a recently developed dataassimilation method designed to circumvent this difficulty. In addition, wedescribe extensions of the algorithm for estimating unknown system parameters.Our results suggest the potential usefulness of our data assimilation techniqueto a broad class of situations in which there is spatiotemporally chaoticbehavior.
label: human

text: Large spatiotemporally chaotic systems pose significant challenges for accurate state estimation due to their high dimensionality, sensitivity to initial conditions, and rapid error growth from incomplete or noisy observations. Traditional global Kalman filter approaches become computationally prohibitive as the number of degrees of freedom increases. This paper introduces an efficient local ensemble-based method that leverages spatial locality to perform data assimilation, enabling scalable state reconstruction even in extensively chaotic regimes. Numerical experiments on benchmark models, such as the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation, demonstrate superior performance in reducing estimation errors and maintaining synchronization with the true system dynamics over extended periods.
label: llm

text: We discuss in detail the problem of counting BPS gauge invariant operators inthe chiral ring of quiver gauge theories living on D-branes probing generictoric CY singularities. The computation of generating functions that includecounting of baryonic operators is based on a relation between the baryoniccharges in field theory and the Kaehler moduli of the CY singularities. A studyof the interplay between gauge theory and geometry shows that given geometricalsectors appear more than once in the field theory, leading to a notion of"multiplicities". We explain in detail how to decompose the generating functionfor one D-brane into different sectors and how to compute their relevantmultiplicities by introducing geometric and anomalous baryonic charges. ThePlethystic Exponential remains a major tool for passing from one D-brane toarbitrary number of D-branes. Explicit formulae are given for few examples,including C^3/Z_3, F_0, and dP_1.
label: human

text: We discuss in detail the counting of BPS gauge-invariant operators in the chiral ring of \mathcal{N}=1 quiver gauge theories arising from D-branes probing generic toric Calabi-Yau three-fold singularities. These operators correspond to holomorphic functions on the moduli space of vacua, providing insight into the geometric structure of the probed singularity. A key challenge lies in incorporating baryonic operators, which carry charges under U(1) symmetries associated with non-trivial cycles in the Calabi-Yau geometry. We establish a precise mapping between the baryonic charges in the gauge theory and the Kähler moduli parameters of the toric variety. This correspondence enables the computation of refined generating functions that enumerate both mesonic and baryonic chiral operators via plethystic techniques. Applications to specific examples, such as conical singularities, demonstrate consistency with expected geometric properties and AdS/CFT dual descriptions.
label: llm

text: Thin films of Co-TiO2 are deposited on silicon and quartz substrates usingPulse Laser Deposition (PLD) process at various oxygen partial pressuresranging from 6.6 x 10-3 Pascals (Pa) to 53 Pa. Crystal structure, transport andmagnetic properties of reduced CoxTi(1-x)O2 (0 <x< 0.03) thin films areinvestigated and are found to have a strong dependence on the oxygen partialpressure. X-ray diffraction (XRD) data reveals the presence of mixed phasematerial containing both anatase and rutile. However, these phasesintertransform with the change in the oxygen partial pressure in the chamberduring the growth of the films. X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) shows noCo or CoO related peaks for samples with Co concentration up to x=0.03.However, the oxygen 1s peaks are asymmetric suggesting the presence of oxygenvacancies. The transport and magnetic measurements show a clear dependence onthe concentration of oxygen vacancies. There is an enhancement in theelectrical conductivity and the magnetization as more vacancies are created inthe material. The resistivity as a function of temperature rho(T) follows thepolaronic behavior and the activation energies obtained, ~100 to 150meV, arewithin the range that is typical for semiconducting materials.
label: human

text: Cobalt-doped TiO₂ thin films were deposited using pulsed laser deposition on silicon and quartz substrates under varying oxygen partial pressures from approximately 6.6 × 10⁻³ Pa to 53 Pa. The crystal structure of the reduced CoₓTi₁₋ₓO₂ films (with x up to 0.03) exhibited a strong dependence on oxygen partial pressure, maintaining the anatase or rutile phase while showing variations in lattice parameters due to defect incorporation. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed no evidence of metallic cobalt clusters or cobalt oxide phases for low doping levels, confirming substitutional doping of Co into the TiO₂ lattice. Asymmetric oxygen 1s peaks indicated the presence of oxygen vacancies, with their concentration increasing at lower oxygen partial pressures. Transport measurements demonstrated enhanced electrical conductivity in films grown under reduced oxygen pressure, attributed to higher carrier densities from oxygen vacancies acting as donors. Magnetic characterization showed room-temperature ferromagnetism that intensified with decreasing oxygen partial pressure, correlating directly with vacancy concentration. The observed magnetization enhancement suggests that oxygen vacancies mediate ferromagnetic coupling between substituted Co ions, possibly through bound magnetic polaron mechanisms.
label: llm

text: The Grassmann manifold G_{n,p}(L) is the set of all p-dimensional planes(through the origin) in the n-dimensional Euclidean space L^{n}, where L iseither R or C. This paper considers an unequal dimensional quantization inwhich a source in G_{n,p}(L) is quantized through a code in G_{n,q}(L), where pand q are not necessarily the same. It is different from most works inliterature where p\equiv q. The analysis for unequal dimensional quantizationis based on the volume of a metric ball in G_{n,p}(L) whose center is inG_{n,q}(L). Our chief result is a closed-form formula for the volume of ametric ball when the radius is sufficiently small. This volume formula holdsfor Grassmann manifolds with arbitrary n, p, q and L, while previous resultspertained only to some special cases. Based on this volume formula, severalbounds are derived for the rate distortion tradeoff assuming the quantizationrate is sufficiently high. The lower and upper bounds on the distortion ratefunction are asymptotically identical, and so precisely quantify the asymptoticrate distortion tradeoff. We also show that random codes are asymptoticallyoptimal in the sense that they achieve the minimum achievable distortion withprobability one as n and the code rate approach infinity linearly. Finally, wediscuss some applications of the derived results to communication theory. Ageometric interpretation in the Grassmann manifold is developed for capacitycalculation of additive white Gaussian noise channel. Further, the deriveddistortion rate function is beneficial to characterizing the effect ofbeamforming matrix selection in multi-antenna communications.
label: human

text: The Grassmann manifold \(G_{n,p}(\mathbb{L})\) consists of all \(p\)-dimensional subspaces in the \(n\)-dimensional Euclidean space over \(\mathbb{L}\), where \(\mathbb{L}\) is either \(\mathbb{R}\) or \(\mathbb{C}\). This paper investigates unequal-dimensional quantization, where a source subspace from \(G_{n,p}(\mathbb{L})\) is approximated by codewords from \(G_{n,q}(\mathbb{L})\), with \(p \neq q\) in general. Unlike prior studies that primarily assume equal dimensions (\(p = q\)), the unequal case introduces additional geometric challenges. The analysis centers on the volume of small metric balls in \(G_{n,p}(\mathbb{L})\) centered at points in \(G_{n,q}(\mathbb{L})\). A key contribution is the derivation of a closed-form expression for this volume when the ball radius is sufficiently small. This volume formula is valid for arbitrary \(n\), \(p\), \(q\), and \(\mathbb{L}\), extending beyond previous results limited to specific cases. Using the volume formula, bounds on quantization distortion are established for the unequal-dimensional setting. Random codebooks are shown to be asymptotically optimal, achieving minimal distortion as dimension and rate grow linearly. The results provide insights into high-rate quantization performance on Grassmann manifolds. Applications to communication systems are discussed, including a geometric perspective on channel capacity in additive white Gaussian noise models. These findings generalize equal-dimensional quantization theory and highlight the role of manifold geometry in code design.
label: llm

text: We present an analysis of long-term optical monitoring observations andoptical spectroscopic observations of the counterpart to CXOU J205847.5+414637(high mass X-ray binary system). We search for a variability in the light curveof Be star. We used differential magnitudes in the time series analysis. Thevariability search in the optical light curve was made by using differentalgorithms. The reduction and analysis of spectra were done by using MIDAS andits suitable packages. We have performed a frequency search which gave us thevalue 2.404 1/day. This value is attributed to the non-radial pulsation of Bestar. H alpha emission line profiles always show double-peaked emissions with amean equivalent width of 2.31 \pm 0.19 \AA ~and a peak separation of 516 \pm 45km/s. This suggests that Be star disk is still present. CXOU J205847.5+414637is in X-ray quiescent state.
label: human

text: GRO J2058+42 is a transient Be/X-ray binary system featuring a neutron star accreting from a massive O9.5–B0 IV–V companion star surrounded by a circumstellar disk. The system exhibits occasional giant (type II) X-ray outbursts, followed by periods of weaker type I activity or quiescence. Long-term optical photometric monitoring reveals significant variability in the brightness of the Be star counterpart. The optical light curve shows maxima that coincide with or closely follow periods of enhanced X-ray emission. After these peaks, a noticeable decline in optical brightness occurs, consistent with changes in the circumstellar disk. Spectroscopic observations indicate persistent double-peaked Hα emission lines, with equivalent widths varying over time but maintaining a symmetric profile. Unlike many Be/X-ray binaries, no V/R asymmetry is detected in the emission lines, suggesting the absence of a precessing warped disk.
label: llm

text: While the structure of chromatin has been studied in great detail on lengthscales below 30 nm, amazingly little is known about the higher-order foldingmotifs of chromatin in interphase. Recent experiments give evidence that thefolding may depend locally on gene density and transcriptional activity andshow a leveling-off at long distances where approximately $<R^2> \sim O(1)$. Wepropose a new model that can explain this leveling-off by the formation ofrandom loops. We derive an analytical expression for the mean squaredisplacement between two beads where the average is taken over the thermalensemble with a fixed but random loop configuration, while quenched averagingover the ensemble of different loop configurations -- which turns out to beequivalent to averaging over an ensemble of random matrices -- is performednumerically. A detailed investigation of this model shows that loops on allscales are necessary to fit experimental data.
label: human

text: We introduce a random loop model to describe the conformational statistics of long polymers, particularly motivated by the higher-order folding of chromatin fibers in interphase nuclei. Experimental observations reveal that, beyond genomic distances of approximately 5–10 Mb, the mean-square spatial distance ⟨R²⟩ between pairs of loci becomes independent of contour length, contrasting with the linear scaling expected in simple random walk models. This leveling-off is attributed to the formation of random loops along the polymer chain, which effectively compact the structure on large scales. We derive an analytical expression for the mean-square displacement between arbitrary monomers, averaging over thermal fluctuations for fixed loop configurations and performing quenched averaging over random loop ensembles via random matrix techniques. Numerical investigations demonstrate that a broad distribution of loop sizes across all scales is required to quantitatively reproduce experimental data on chromatin organization.
label: llm

text: We have investigated a sample of 5088 quasars from the Sloan Digital SkySurvey Second Data Release in order to determine how the frequency andproperties of broad absorptions lines (BALs) depend on black hole mass,bolometric luminosity, Eddington fraction (L/L_Edd), and spectral slope. Wefocus only on high-ionization BALs and find a number of significant results.While quasars accreting near the Eddington limit are more likely to show BALsthan lower $L/L_{Edd}$ systems, BALs are present in quasars accreting at only afew percent Eddington. We find a stronger effect with bolometric luminosity,such that the most luminous quasars are more likely to show BALs. There is anadditional effect, previously known, that BAL quasars are redder on averagethan unabsorbed quasars. The strongest effects involving the quasar physicalproperties and BAL properties are related to terminal outflow velocity. Maximumobserved outflow velocities increase with both the bolometric luminosity andthe blueness of the spectral slope, suggesting that the ultraviolet luminosityto a great extent determines the acceleration. These results support the ideaof outflow acceleration via ultraviolet line scattering.
label: human

text: Quasar outflows, manifested as broad absorption lines (BALs) in ultraviolet spectra, represent powerful winds driven by accretion disk radiation and potentially magnetic forces around supermassive black holes. These outflows exhibit a range of velocities, from thousands to tens of thousands of km/s, with terminal velocities strongly correlated to the quasar's bolometric luminosity and Eddington ratio. Observations indicate that more luminous quasars are more likely to host detectable BAL outflows, suggesting a dependency on accretion rate. Additionally, BAL quasars tend to appear redder due to dust extinction associated with the outflowing gas. Physical properties such as column densities, ionization parameters, and distances from the central engine (typically parsecs to kiloparsecs) are derived from photoionization modeling of absorption troughs. Kinetic energies in these outflows can reach levels sufficient for significant AGN feedback, with mass outflow rates often comparable to or exceeding the accretion rate. Ultimately, these outflows play a crucial role in regulating black hole growth and quenching star formation in host galaxies through gas ejection and momentum injection.
label: llm

text: High resolution optical and ultraviolet spectra of two B-type post-AsymptoticGiant Branch (post-AGB) stars in globular clusters, Barnard 29 in M 13 and ROA5701 in omega Cen, have been analysed using model atmosphere techniques. Theoptical spectra have been obtained with FEROS on the ESO 2.2-m telescope andthe 2d-Coud\'e spectrograph on the 2.7-m McDonald telescope, while theultraviolet observations are from the GHRS on the HST. Abundances of lightelements (C, N, O, Mg, Al and S) plus Fe have been determined from the opticalspectra, while the ultraviolet data provide additional Fe abundance estimatesfrom Fe III absorption lines in the 1875-1900 {\AA} wavelength region. Ageneral metal underabundance relative to young B-type stars is found for bothBarnard 29 and ROA 5701. These results are consistent with the metallicities ofthe respective clusters, as well as with previous studies of the objects. Thederived abundance patterns suggest that the stars have not undergone a gas-dustseparation, contrary to previous suggestions, although they may have evolvedfrom the AGB before the onset of the third dredge-up. However, the Feabundances derived from the HST spectra are lower than those expected from themetallicities of the respective clusters, by 0.5 dex for Barnard 29 and 0.8 dexfor ROA 5701. A similar systematic underabundance is also found for otherB-type stars in environments of known metallicity, such as the MagellanicClouds. These results indicate that the Fe III ultraviolet lines may yieldabundance values which are systematically too low by typically 0.6 dex andhence such estimates should be treated with caution.
label: human

text: High-resolution optical and ultraviolet spectra of the B-type post-asymptotic giant branch stars Barnard 29 in the globular cluster M 13 and ROA 5701 in ω Centauri have been analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium model atmospheres. The optical data were acquired with FEROS on the ESO 2.2-m telescope and the 2d-Coudé spectrograph on the McDonald 2.7-m telescope, while ultraviolet observations utilized the Goddard High Resolution Spectrograph on the Hubble Space Telescope. Abundances for light elements including carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, magnesium, aluminum, and sulfur, along with iron, were derived primarily from the optical spectra. Additional iron abundance estimates were obtained from Fe III lines in the ultraviolet region around 1875–1900 Å. Both stars exhibit a general metal underabundance compared to young Galactic B-type stars. The derived iron abundances from optical spectra are consistent with the metallicities of their host clusters, M 13 and ω Centauri. In contrast, the ultraviolet-derived iron abundances are systematically lower than cluster values by approximately 0.5 dex for Barnard 29 and 0.8 dex for ROA 5701. The abundance patterns indicate no evidence of significant gas-dust separation processes in the progenitor asymptotic giant branch phases. These findings suggest that both stars likely departed the asymptotic giant branch prior to the onset of third dredge-up episodes.
label: llm

text: In wireless data networks, communication is particularly susceptible toeavesdropping due to its broadcast nature. Security and privacy systems havebecome critical for wireless providers and enterprise networks. This paperconsiders the problem of secret communication over the Gaussian broadcastchannel, where a multi-antenna transmitter sends independent confidentialmessages to two users with perfect secrecy. That is, each user would like toobtain its own message reliably and confidentially. First, a computableSato-type outer bound on the secrecy capacity region is provided for amulti-antenna broadcast channel with confidential messages. Next, a dirty-papersecure coding scheme and its simplified version are described. For each case,the corresponding achievable rate region is derived under the perfect secrecyrequirement. Finally, two numerical examples demonstrate that the Sato-typeouter bound is consistent with the boundary of the simplified dirty-papercoding secrecy rate region.
label: human

text: In wireless networks, the broadcast nature of radio propagation makes transmissions vulnerable to eavesdropping, necessitating robust security mechanisms beyond traditional cryptography. This paper investigates physical layer security for a multi-antenna transmitter broadcasting independent confidential messages to multiple legitimate receivers over Gaussian channels. We model the system as a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) broadcast channel with confidential messages (BCC), where perfect secrecy is required such that each receiver decodes its intended message reliably while obtaining no information about others. A computable outer bound on the secrecy capacity region is derived using a Sato-type argument, extending classical broadcast channel results to incorporate secrecy constraints. To achieve secrecy, we propose a dirty-paper coding scheme that treats one user's signal as interference for the other, combined with Gaussian signaling. A simplified version of this scheme is presented, leveraging artificial noise projection into the null space of legitimate channels to degrade eavesdropper performance when present.
label: llm

text: A path-integral for the t-J model in two dimensions is constructed based onDirac quantization, with an action found originally by Wiegmann (Phys. Rev.Lett. {\bf 60}, 821 (1988); Nucl. Phys. B323, 311 (1989)). Concentrating on thelow doping limit, we assume short range antiferromagnetic order of the spindegrees of freedom. Going over to a local spin quantization axis of the dopantfermions, that follows the spin degree of freedom, staggered CP$^1$ fieldsresult and the constraint against double occupancy can be resolved. Thestaggered CP$^1$ fields are split into slow and fast modes, such that after agradient expansion, and after integrating out the fast modes and the dopantfermions, a CP$^1$ field-theory with a massive gauge field is obtained thatdescribes generically incommensurate coplanar magnetic structures, as discussedpreviously in the context of frustrated quantum antiferromagnets. Hence, thepossibility of deconfined spinons is opened by doping a colinearantiferromagnet.
label: human

text: We derive a low-energy effective field theory for lightly doped antiferromagnets starting from a microscopic spin-fermion model, focusing on the long-wavelength limit. Assuming short-range antiferromagnetic order in the low-doping regime, we introduce a local spin quantization axis aligned with the dopant fermions. This transformation yields staggered CP$^1$ fields that effectively represent the spin degrees of freedom while enforcing the no-double-occupancy constraint. The dopant fermions couple minimally to these CP$^1$ fields via a U(1) gauge interaction. To capture slow dynamics, we decompose the staggered CP$^1$ fields into slow and fast modes. A gradient expansion is then performed on the slow modes. Integrating out the fast CP$^1$ modes and the dopant fermions generates an effective action for the slow fields. This procedure results in a CP$^1$ model with a massive gauge field, distinguishing it from massless cases in undoped or frustrated systems. The effective theory generically describes incommensurate coplanar magnetic structures.
label: llm

text: We study the effects of frustration in an antiferromagnetic film of FCClattice with Heisenberg spin model including an Ising-like anisotropy. MonteCarlo (MC) simulations have been used to study thermodynamic properties of thefilm. We show that the presence of the surface reduces the ground state (GS)degeneracy found in the bulk. The GS is shown to depend on the surface in-planeinteraction $J_s$ with a critical value at which ordering of type I coexistswith ordering of type II. Near this value a reentrant phase is found. Variousphysical quantities such as layer magnetizations and layer susceptibilities areshown and discussed. The nature of the phase transition is also studied byhistogram technique. We have also used the Green's function (GF) method for thequantum counterpart model. The results at low-$T$ show interesting effects ofquantum fluctuations. Results obtained by the GF method at high $T$ arecompared to those of MC simulations. A good agreement is observed.
label: human

text: We investigate the effects of geometric frustration in thin films of classical Heisenberg spins on a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice with nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic interactions, incorporating a small Ising-like anisotropy to mimic realistic magnetic materials. The bulk FCC antiferromagnet exhibits extensive ground-state degeneracy due to the tetrahedral coordination, leading to highly frustrated spin configurations. In thin-film geometries, finite-size effects along the growth direction break translational symmetry and introduce surface layers with reduced coordination. Monte Carlo simulations are employed to explore the thermodynamic properties, including specific heat, magnetization sublattices, and order parameters as functions of temperature and film thickness. The presence of free surfaces significantly lifts part of the bulk ground-state degeneracy by favoring specific spin alignments at the boundaries. Surface spins show enhanced fluctuations compared to interior layers, resulting in layer-dependent magnetization profiles.
label: llm

text: We investigate the coupled formation and evolution of galaxies and theirembedded supermassive black holes using state-of-the-art hydrodynamicsimulations of cosmological structure formation. For the first time, weself-consistently follow the dark matter dynamics, radiative gas cooling, starformation, as well as black hole growth and associated feedback processes,starting directly from initial conditions appropriate for the LambdaCDMcosmology. Our modeling of the black hole physics is based on an approach wehave developed in simulations of isolated galaxy mergers. Here we examine: (i)the predicted global history of black hole mass assembly (ii) the evolution ofthe local black hole-host mass correlations and (iii) the conditions that allowrapid growth of the first quasars, and the properties of their hosts anddescendants today. We find a total black hole mass density in good agreementwith observational estimates. The black hole accretion rate density peaks atlower redshift and evolves more strongly at high redshift than the starformation rate density, but the ratio of black hole to stellar mass densitiesshows only a moderate evolution at low redshifts. We find strong correlationsbetween black hole masses and properties of the stellar systems, agreeing wellwith the measured local M_BH-sigma and M_BH -M_* relationships, but alsosuggesting (dependent on the mass range) a weak evolution with redshift in thenormalization and the slope. Our simulations also produce massive black holesat high redshift, due to extended periods of exponential growth in regions thatcollapse early and exhibit strong gas inflows. These first supermassive BHsystems however are not necessarily the most massive ones today, since they areoften overtaken in growth by quasars that form later. (abridged)
label: human

text: We present results from state-of-the-art direct cosmological hydrodynamic simulations that self-consistently track the co-evolution of supermassive black holes and their host galaxies within a ΛCDM framework. These simulations incorporate dark matter dynamics, radiative gas cooling, star formation, black hole seeding, Eddington-limited accretion, mergers, and associated feedback energy injection starting from cosmological initial conditions. Black hole growth is modeled via Bondi-Hoyle accretion boosted for unresolved multiphase gas, coupled with thermal and kinetic feedback modes to regulate gas inflows and outflows. The simulations reproduce the observed cosmic star formation rate density evolution and black hole accretion rate density, with the latter peaking at slightly lower redshifts. Strong correlations emerge between black hole masses and host galaxy properties, closely matching local M_BH–σ and M_BH–M_* relations with minimal redshift evolution in normalization. At high redshifts, rapid exponential growth phases in early-collapsing halos enable the formation of massive black holes exceeding 10^9 M_⊙ by z ≈ 6. Feedback from active galactic nuclei efficiently quenches star formation in massive galaxies, preventing overcooling and aligning simulated galaxy mass functions with observations. The ratio of black hole to stellar mass density evolves moderately at low redshifts, reflecting self-regulated co-growth. Merger-driven inflows contribute significantly to episodic high-accretion phases, while secular processes dominate in isolated systems. Overall, these direct simulations demonstrate that gravitational torque-limited gas supply and feedback mechanisms drive the observed black hole–galaxy scaling relations across cosmic time.
label: llm

text: In the framework of the effective field theory method, we use theexperimental data and the perturbative unitarity bounds to determine the valuesand uncertainty of all the 11 chiral coefficients ($\al_i, i=0, ..., 10$) ofthe standard electroweak chiral Lagrangian. Up to linear terms in $\al_i$, weprovide the one-loop renormalization group equations of all the chiralcoefficients, which are calculated in the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge using themodified minimal subtraction scheme. With the improved renormalization groupequations to sum over the logarithmic corrections, we analyze the currentexperimental uncertainty of oblique correction parameters, $S(\Lambda)$ and$T(\Lambda)$. We find that, due to the large uncertainty in the triplegauge-boson coupling measurements, the parameter space of positive $S(\Lambda)$for $\Lambda > 1$ TeV is still allowed by the current experimental data.$T(\Lambda)$ tends to increase with $\Lambda$ even in the presence of theoperators that contribute to the triple and quartic gauge-boson couplings.
label: human

text: The electroweak chiral Lagrangian provides an effective field theory description of electroweak symmetry breaking without assuming a light Higgs boson, parameterizing potential deviations from the Standard Model through higher-dimensional operators. In this framework, the 11 dimensionless chiral coefficients (α₀ to α₁₀) encode low-energy effects of new physics, including contributions to oblique corrections and triple gauge-boson couplings. Precision electroweak data from LEP, Tevatron, and low-energy experiments, combined with perturbative unitarity bounds, tightly constrain these coefficients, yielding central values close to zero with uncertainties typically at the 10⁻³ level or smaller for most parameters. Additionally, one-loop renormalization group equations for these coefficients are derived, facilitating the evolution of constraints across energy scales and highlighting the consistency of the approach with experimental observations.
label: llm

text: This paper presents a fault classification method which makes use of aTakagi-Sugeno neuro-fuzzy model and Pseudomodal energies calculated from thevibration signals of cylindrical shells. The calculation of PseudomodalEnergies, for the purposes of condition monitoring, has previously been foundto be an accurate method of extracting features from vibration signals. Thiscalculation is therefore used to extract features from vibration signalsobtained from a diverse population of cylindrical shells. Some of the cylindersin the population have faults in different substructures. The pseudomodalenergies calculated from the vibration signals are then used as inputs to aneuro-fuzzy model. A leave-one-out cross-validation process is used to test theperformance of the model. It is found that the neuro-fuzzy model is able toclassify faults with an accuracy of 91.62%, which is higher than the previouslyused multilayer perceptron.
label: human

text: This paper presents a fault classification method for cylindrical shells using a Takagi-Sugeno neuro-fuzzy model trained on pseudomodal energies extracted from vibration signals. Pseudomodal energies are employed as effective feature descriptors, as they have previously demonstrated high accuracy in capturing structural dynamics for condition monitoring applications. Vibration signals are collected from a diverse population of cylindrical shells, some of which exhibit faults in various substructures. These signals are processed to compute pseudomodal energies, which serve as input features for the neuro-fuzzy classifier. The neuro-fuzzy model is trained and evaluated using a leave-one-out cross-validation procedure to ensure robust performance assessment. Results indicate that the proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 91.62%, outperforming traditional methods such as multilayer perceptrons. This hybrid neuro-fuzzy framework offers a promising solution for reliable fault diagnosis in structural health monitoring of cylindrical components.
label: llm

text: The precise determination of the arrival direction of cosmic rays is afundamental prerequisite for the search for sources or the study of theiranisotropies on the sky. One of the most important aspects to achieve anoptimal measurement of these directions is to properly take into account themeasurement uncertainties in the estimation procedure. In this article wepresent a model for the uncertainties associated with the time measurements inthe Auger surface detector array. We show that this model represents well themeasurement uncertainties and therefore provides the basis for an optimaldetermination of the arrival direction. With this model and a description ofthe shower front geometry it is possible to estimate, on an event by eventbasis, the uncertainty associated with the determination of the arrivaldirections of the cosmic rays.
label: human

text: The precise determination of the arrival directions of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays is essential for investigating potential sources and large-scale anisotropies in their distribution. Accurate reconstruction of these directions relies heavily on the timing information provided by the surface detector array of the Pierre Auger Observatory, where uncertainties in individual station time measurements must be properly accounted for in the fitting procedure. This work introduces an empirical model for the time uncertainties in the water-Cherenkov detectors, incorporating contributions from particle arrival fluctuations, signal size, and detector response characteristics. The model is validated against real data from extensive air showers, demonstrating good agreement across a range of signal strengths and zenith angles. By enabling a more optimal weighting of timing data.
label: llm

text: We present a simple implementation of the dynamical mean-field theoryapproach to the electronic structure of strongly correlated materials. Thisimplementation achieves full self-consistency over the charge density, takinginto account correlation-induced changes to the total charge density andeffective Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian. A linear muffin-tin orbital basis-set is used,and the charge density is computed from moments of the many bodymomentum-distribution matrix. The calculation of the total energy is alsoconsidered, with a proper treatment of high-frequency tails of the Green'sfunction and self-energy. The method is illustrated on two materials withwell-localized 4f electrons, insulating cerium sesquioxide Ce2O3 and thegamma-phase of metallic cerium, using the Hubbard-I approximation to thedynamical mean-field self-energy. The momentum-integrated spectral function andmomentum-resolved dispersion of the Hubbard bands are calculated, as well asthe volume-dependence of the total energy. We show that full self-consistencyover the charge density, taking into account its modification by strongcorrelations, can be important for the computation of both thermodynamical andspectral properties, particularly in the case of the oxide material.
label: human

text: We present a straightforward implementation of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for the electronic structure of strongly correlated materials, achieving full self-consistency over the charge density within the linear muffin-tin orbital (LMTO) framework. This approach accounts for correlation-induced modifications to the total charge density and the effective Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian by expressing the charge density through moments of the k-dependent many-body momentum-distribution matrix. The method is applied to two cerium-based systems with well-localized 4f electrons: the insulating cerium sesquioxide Ce₂O₃ and the γ-phase of metallic cerium, using the Hubbard-I approximation as the DMFT impurity solver. Momentum-integrated spectral functions and k-resolved dispersions of the Hubbard bands are computed, along with the volume dependence of the total energy. Results demonstrate that incorporating full charge self-consistency significantly influences both spectral and thermodynamical properties. This effect proves particularly pronounced in the oxide material Ce₂O₃, where correlation-driven charge redistribution plays a crucial role. The proposed implementation offers a computationally efficient route to more accurate descriptions of strongly correlated systems compared to one-shot or partially self-consistent schemes.
label: llm

text: Rigorous computer simulations of propagating electromagnetic fields havebecome an important tool for optical metrology and optics design ofnanostructured components. As has been shown in previous benchmarks some of thepresently used methods suffer from low convergence rates and/or low accuracy ofthe results and exhibit very long computation times which makes application toextended 2D layout patterns impractical. We address 3D simulation tasks byusing a finite-element solver which has been shown to be superior to competingmethods by several orders of magnitude in accuracy and computational time fortypical microlithography simulations. We report on the current status of thesolver, incorporating higher order edge elements, adaptive refinement methods,and fast solution algorithms. Further, we investigate the performance of thesolver in the 3D simulation project of light diffraction off an alternatingphase-shift contact-hole mask.
label: human

text: Rigorous numerical simulations of electromagnetic fields in nanostructures are essential for advancing optical metrology and designing nano-optical devices. However, many existing methods exhibit slow convergence, limited accuracy, or excessive computational demands, rendering them unsuitable for complex three-dimensional problems. This study employs the time-harmonic finite-element method to perform accurate 3D simulations of electromagnetic wave propagation and scattering in nanostructures. The approach incorporates higher-order vectorial edge elements, adaptive mesh refinement, and efficient iterative solvers to achieve superior performance. Results demonstrate high convergence rates and reduced computation times, enabling practical application to challenging nanostructures such as those in microlithography and photonics.
label: llm

text: A release of multicolor broad band (BVRI) photometry for a subsample of 44isolated spirals drawn from the Catalogue of Isolated Galaxies (CIG) ispresented. Total magnitudes and colors at various circular apertures, as wellas some global structural/morphological parameters are estimated. Morphology isreevaluated through optical and sharp/filtered R band images, (B-I) color indexmaps, and archive near-IR JHK images from the Two-Micron Survey. The CASstructural parameters (Concentration, Asymmetry, and Clumpiness) werecalculated from the images in each one of the bands. The fraction of galaxieswith well identified optical/near-IR bars (SB) is 63%, while a 17% more showsevidence of weak or suspected bars (SAB). The sample average value of themaximum bar ellipticity is 0.4. Half of the galaxies in the sample shows rings.We identify two candidates for isolated galaxies with disturbed morphology. Thestructural CAS parameters change with the observed band, and the tendenciesthey follow with the morphological type and global color are more evident inthe redder bands. In any band, the major difference between our isolatedspirals and a sample of interacting spirals is revealed in the A-S plane. Adeep and uniformly observed sample of isolated galaxies is intended for variouspurposes including (i) comparative studies of environmental effects, (ii)confronting model predictions of galaxy evolution and (iii) evaluating thechange of galaxy properties with redshift.
label: human

text: We present multicolor broadband BVRI surface photometry for a sample of isolated spiral galaxies selected from the Catalogue of Isolated Galaxies (CIG). Deep CCD imaging in the B, V, R, and I bands was obtained to derive accurate surface brightness profiles, isophotal parameters, and geometric profiles including ellipticity and position angle. Total magnitudes and integrated colors within various circular apertures were calculated for each galaxy, providing a homogeneous photometric database. Exponential disk components were fitted to the surface brightness profiles in all four bands to determine disk scale lengths and central surface brightnesses. A systematic decrease in disk scale length from B to I band was observed in the majority of the sample, consistent with the presence of negative color gradients in isolated disks. Color profiles reveal radial variations indicative of inside-out disk formation and different stellar population distributions. Structural parameters such as concentration, asymmetry, and clumpiness were measured to characterize the morphological properties of these galaxies. The results show that isolated spirals generally exhibit regular and symmetric structures with minimal evidence of recent gravitational perturbations. Comparison with previous studies confirms the reliability of the derived photometric parameters within the estimated uncertainties. These data provide a valuable reference for investigating the role of environment in spiral galaxy evolution by serving as a control sample for interacting systems.
label: llm

text: Solar coronal mass ejections (CMEs) show a large variety in their kinematicproperties. CMEs originating in active regions and accompanied by strong flaresare usually faster and accelerated more impulsively than CMEs associated withfilament eruptions outside active regions and weak flares. It has been proposedmore than two decades ago that there are two separate types of CMEs, fast(impulsive) CMEs and slow (gradual) CMEs. However, this concept may not bevalid, since the large data sets acquired in recent years do not show twodistinct peaks in the CME velocity distribution and reveal that both fast andslow CMEs can be accompanied by both weak and strong flares. We presentnumerical simulations which confirm our earlier analytical result that aflux-rope CME model permits describing fast and slow CMEs in a unified manner.We consider a force-free coronal magnetic flux rope embedded in the potentialfield of model bipolar and quadrupolar active regions. The eruption is drivenby the torus instability which occurs if the field overlying the flux ropedecreases sufficiently rapidly with height. The acceleration profile depends onthe steepness of this field decrease, corresponding to fast CMEs for rapiddecrease, as is typical of active regions, and to slow CMEs for gentledecrease, as is typical of the quiet Sun. Complex (quadrupolar) active regionslead to the fastest CMEs.
label: human

text: Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) exhibit a wide range of kinematics, with fast CMEs typically originating from active regions and slow CMEs from quieter solar environments. This study employs three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) numerical simulations to investigate the dynamics of both fast and slow CMEs within a unified flux-rope framework. A force-free magnetic flux rope is embedded in potential magnetic field configurations representing bipolar and quadrupolar active regions, as well as quieter coronal structures. The overlying coronal magnetic field strength and its radial decay rate are varied to model different source region characteristics.
